A card takes the width its style gives it; `flexGrow` with `flexBasis` puts two across a window
and one across a phone.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 16 }}>
  <Card style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexBasis: 300 }}>…</Card>
  <Card style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexBasis: 300 }}>…</Card>
</View>
```

### A footer that wraps [#a-footer-that-wraps]

`CardFooter` is a row that wraps: a long pair of buttons goes to two lines on a phone rather than
squeezing both.

```tsx
<CardFooter>
  <Button style={{ flexGrow: 1 }}>Login</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" style={{ flexGrow: 1 }}>
    Google
  </Button>
</CardFooter>
```

### Flush [#flush]

`flush` on `CardContent` drops the side padding and pulls the body through the card's bottom padding, so a picture meets the rim. The card's `overflow: hidden` clips it to the radius. The header stays padded. Off in the terminal.

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Cover</CardTitle>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent flush>
    <View style={{ height: 160, backgroundColor: "var(--inset)" }} />
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

## API [#api]

Each part is the `nsh` element it is drawn with, wearing the look `cardLook()` gives it. Every
view prop passes through; `style` goes over the look's.

| Part              | Props   | Description                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Card`            | —       | The flat surface holding related content: `cardLook().card`.                            |
| `CardHeader`      | —       | Title over description in the first column, the action at the trailing edge: `.header`. |
| `CardTitle`       | —       | A step larger than body, semibold, the text colour: `.title`.                           |
| `CardDescription` | —       | Body size in the muted colour: `.description`.                                          |
| `CardAction`      | —       | The control at the trailing edge, beside title and description: `.action`.              |
| `CardContent`     | `flush` | What the card is about. `flush` meets the card's side and bottom edges: `.content`.     |
| `CardFooter`      | —       | A wrapping row, centred, 8 apart: `.footer`.                                            |

`CardTitle` and `CardDescription` are `Text`, so they take text props (`numberOfLines`, `role`).
`CardHeader` is a grid of two columns: the title over the description in the first and the action
at the trailing edge of the first row, whichever order the three are written in.
`cardLook()` is exported for a card the app draws itself.

# Carousel (/dev/docs/components/carousel)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add carousel
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Carousel,
  CarouselContent,
  CarouselItem,
  CarouselNext,
  CarouselPagination,
  CarouselPrevious,
} from "@/components/ui/carousel";
```

```tsx
<Carousel>
  <CarouselContent>
    <CarouselItem>…</CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselPrevious />
  <CarouselNext />
</Carousel>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Carousel`:

```text
Carousel
├── CarouselContent
│   └── CarouselItem
├── CarouselPrevious
├── CarouselPagination
│   └── CarouselPaginationItem
│       └── CarouselDot
└── CarouselNext
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Slides [#slides]

```tsx
<Carousel index={index()} onChange={({ index }) => setIndex(index)} accessibilityLabel="Photos">
  <CarouselContent style={{ height: 120 }}>
    <CarouselItem>
      <Text>Harbor</Text>
    </CarouselItem>
    <CarouselItem>
      <Text>Dunes</Text>
    </CarouselItem>
    <CarouselItem>
      <Text>Glacier</Text>
    </CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
</Carousel>
```

### Caption over a photo [#caption-over-a-photo]

A slide that holds a photograph draws its caption itself: the theme has no text role that reads
over an arbitrary picture, so the ink is `on-media` (white in every theme, both appearances) and
the veil behind it is `scrim`. A text role such as `foreground` flips with the appearance and
leaves the caption unreadable in one of them.

```tsx
<View style={{ backgroundImage: `url(${photo})`, justifyContent: "flex-end" }}>
  <View
    style={{
      backgroundImage: `linear-gradient(to top, ${alpha(token("scrim"), 0.9)}, transparent)`,
    }}
  >
    <Text style={{ color: colors.onMedia, fontWeight: "700" }}>{title}</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Arrows [#arrows]

`CarouselPrevious` and `CarouselNext` draw their own icon and size; `side` and `glass` change the
chrome. Under every theme they are the same floating pill beside the dots; `carouselArrowLook()`
has no per-theme form to follow.

```tsx
<CarouselPrevious accessibilityLabel="Previous slide" />
<CarouselNext accessibilityLabel="Next slide" />
```

### Pagination [#pagination]

The indicator travels to `index`; each item shows the `CarouselDot` you give it. The carousel keeps
the slide shown to itself (`nsh/base` only reports it through `onChange`), so an item with no child
draws nothing: pass the dot, and tell it which slide it is on.

```tsx
<CarouselPagination accessibilityLabel="Choose a slide">
  {SLIDES.map((_, i) => (
    <CarouselPaginationItem index={i} accessibilityLabel={`Slide ${i + 1}`}>
      <CarouselDot selected={index() === i} />
    </CarouselPaginationItem>
  ))}
</CarouselPagination>
```

### Autoplay [#autoplay]

The carousel holds no timer: a slide that moves on by itself is the app's — a controlled `index` a
timer advances, around the ends. Hold it while the user is at the carousel: the pointer over a
`View` around it (`onMouseEnter` / `onMouseLeave`), the keyboard focus in it (`onFocus` /
`onBlur`) and a drag (`onDragStart` / `onDragEnd`), and leave it off with `reduceMotion()`. Key the
effect on the index, so every change — a timer's, an arrow's, a dot's, the rotation control's —
starts a whole interval, or a press would be cut short by the turn already under way. The rotation
control comes first in the row, beside the dots, and names itself `Pause announcements` or
`Play announcements`.

```tsx
import { Pause, Play } from "lucide";
import { cleanup, effect, reduceMotion, signal } from "nsh";

import { IconButton } from "@/components/ui/button";

function rotation(count: number, ms: number) {
  const index = signal(0);
  const playing = signal(true);
  const hovered = signal(false);
  const focused = signal(false);
  const dragging = signal(false);
  const held = () => hovered() || focused() || dragging();
  const running = () => playing() && !held() && !reduceMotion();
  effect(() => {
    index();
    if (!running()) return;
    const timer = setInterval(() => index.set((index() + 1) % count), ms);
    cleanup(() => clearInterval(timer));
  });
  return {
    index,
    playing,
    // The pointer's half: a view of the app's around the carousel.
    hover: {
      onMouseEnter: () => hovered.set(true),
      onMouseLeave: () => hovered.set(false),
    },
    // The carousel's half: its keyboard focus and its drags.
    carousel: {
      onFocus: () => focused.set(true),
      onBlur: () => focused.set(false),
      onDragStart: () => dragging.set(true),
      onDragEnd: () => dragging.set(false),
    },
  };
}

const roll = rotation(3, 4000);

<View {...roll.hover}>
  <Carousel
    looping
    index={roll.index()}
    accessibilityLabel="Announcements"
    onChange={({ index }) => roll.index.set(index)}
    {...roll.carousel}
  >
    <CarouselContent>{/* the announcements */}</CarouselContent>
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
      <IconButton
        accessibilityLabel={roll.playing() ? "Pause announcements" : "Play announcements"}
        onPress={() => roll.playing.set(!roll.playing())}
      >
        <Icon icon={roll.playing() ? Pause : Play} size={14} />
      </IconButton>
      <CarouselPagination accessibilityLabel="Choose an announcement">
        {/* one CarouselPaginationItem and CarouselDot per announcement */}
      </CarouselPagination>
    </View>
  </Carousel>
</View>;
```

## API [#api]

Uses `carouselArrowLook`, `carouselPaginationLook`, `carouselDotItemLook`, and `CarouselDot`. `carouselArrowLook()`'s `icon` is the glyph an arrow draws and its `style` / `hoverStyle` / `activeStyle` / `focusVisibleStyle` are the arrow's chrome. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Carousel](https://nsh.dev/elements/carousel) parts passes through.

| Part                     | Props                                             | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Carousel`               | —                                                 | The carousel over [`nsh/base` Carousel](https://nsh.dev/elements/carousel).                  |
| `CarouselContent`        | —                                                 | The snap viewport the slides scroll in.                                                      |
| `CarouselItem`           | —                                                 | One slide: one per view unless the app gives it a width.                                     |
| `CarouselPrevious`       | `glass`, `side`                                   | The arrow back: `glass` and `side` shape its look, an arrow unless given a child.            |
| `CarouselNext`           | `glass`, `side`                                   | The arrow forward, as the previous one.                                                      |
| `CarouselPagination`     | —                                                 | The dot row, with the pill that travels to the slide shown.                                  |
| `CarouselPaginationItem` | `children` (a `CarouselDot`; nothing without one) | One slide's dot, named `Slide 1`, `Slide 2`, …                                               |
| `CarouselDot`            | `selected`                                        | A quiet circle that brightens under the pointer and hides under the pill on the slide shown. |

# Checkbox (/dev/docs/components/checkbox)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add checkbox
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/ui/checkbox";
```

```tsx
<Checkbox checked={on()} onChange={({ checked }) => on.set(checked)}>
  Photos
</Checkbox>
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Size [#size]

```tsx
<Checkbox size="sm">Small</Checkbox>
<Checkbox size="default">Regular</Checkbox>
<Checkbox size="lg">Large</Checkbox>
```

`size` multiplies the page's control size: `sm` 0.8, `default` 1, `lg` 1.25 (`ChoiceSize`).

### Disabled [#disabled]

```tsx
<Checkbox checked disabled>
  System settings
</Checkbox>
```

### Round [#round]

```tsx
<Checkbox round checked>
  Round
</Checkbox>
```

### Checked and indeterminate [#checked-and-indeterminate]

```tsx
<Checkbox checked={all()} indeterminate={some()} onChange={({ checked }) => selectAll(checked)}>
  Back up everything
</Checkbox>
```

### The look alone [#the-look-alone]

The look is a function, for a checkbox of your own.

```tsx
<Checkbox
  class="group"
  checked={on()}
  {...checkboxLook()}
  indicator={<CheckboxMark mark={on() ? "check" : null} />}
>
  Photos
</Checkbox>
```

### Names for screen readers [#names-for-screen-readers]

A string child is the row's label and its name for screen readers, so the box and its text are one control to a reader; `accessibilityLabel` wins when it should differ. Children drawn as given are named by the texts inside them.

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Checkbox](https://nsh.dev/elements/checkbox) passes through. `indicatorClass` and `indicatorStyle` go over the look's. The row is the `group` the box sinks with while pressed.

| Part           | Props                                                                                                      | Description                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Checkbox`     | `size`: `ChoiceSize` (default `"default"`), `round` (default `false`), `children`: `string \| JSX.Element` | The box of the theme's choice recipe, filling as it is checked; the row is the group it sinks with. |
| `CheckboxMark` | `mark`: `"check" \| "dash" \| null`, `scale`, `round`                                                      | The check or the dash that springs in, drawn into the look's `indicator`.                           |

`ChoiceSize` is `"sm" | "default" | "lg"`: 0.8, 1 or 1.25 times the page's control size, shared with `Radio` (`choiceScales` is the table).

# CodeBlock (/dev/docs/components/code-block)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add code-block
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockFooter,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockLine,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/code-block";
```

```tsx
<CodeBlock>
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>Terminal</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockActions>
      <CodeBlockCopyButton value={output} />
    </CodeBlockActions>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent>{output}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

The code is one color in the theme's monospaced family: there is no syntax highlighting. For
highlighted, editable code, use [`Editor`](./editor), which is `nsh/base`'s.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `CodeBlock`:

```text
CodeBlock
├── CodeBlockHeader
│   ├── CodeBlockTitle
│   └── CodeBlockActions
│       └── CodeBlockCopyButton
├── CodeBlockContent
│   └── CodeBlockLine
└── CodeBlockFooter
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Variant [#variant]

`variant="destructive"` puts the block in the danger tone: the edge, the title and the code. Use it for errors and failed output.

```tsx
<CodeBlock variant="destructive">
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>Build failed</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockActions>
      <CodeBlockCopyButton value={log} />
    </CodeBlockActions>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent>{log}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

### Size [#size]

`size="sm"` has tighter padding and smaller code, for the output of a tool.

```tsx
<CodeBlock size="sm">
  <CodeBlockContent wrap>{output}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

### Header and copy [#header-and-copy]

`CodeBlockHeader` holds a `CodeBlockTitle`, which keeps to one line, and `CodeBlockActions`, which
sits at the end. `CodeBlockCopyButton` is a ghost `IconButton`: a press writes `value` to the system
clipboard and turns the icon into a check for two seconds. Its `accessibilityLabel` reads "Copy",
then "Copied". Put other buttons in `CodeBlockActions` beside it; a wrap toggle is the app's state,
passed to `wrap`. There is no floating placement: the actions belong in a `CodeBlockHeader`.

```tsx
<CodeBlock>
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>app/api/chat/route.ts</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockActions>
      <CodeBlockCopyButton value={code} />
    </CodeBlockActions>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent>{code}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

### Line numbers [#line-numbers]

`lineNumbers` numbers each line of a string child; `startLine` numbers from a given line, for a snippet from the middle of a file. The gutter is not selected with the code. One trailing newline does not make a line.

```tsx
<CodeBlockContent lineNumbers startLine={12}>
  {code}
</CodeBlockContent>
```

### Lines of your own [#lines-of-your-own]

`CodeBlockLine` is a line you draw yourself, with a `variant`: `highlighted` calls it out, `added` and `removed` mark a diff, each with a `+` or `−` that is not selected either. With `lineNumbers` the lines take their numbers in the order they are drawn. A block that shows a whole diff is [`DiffView`](./diff-view).

```tsx
<CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>
  <CodeBlockLine>{"function greet(name: string) {"}</CodeBlockLine>
  <CodeBlockLine variant="removed">{'  return "Hello " + name;'}</CodeBlockLine>
  <CodeBlockLine variant="added">{"  return `Hello, ${name}!`;"}</CodeBlockLine>
  <CodeBlockLine variant="highlighted">{"}"}</CodeBlockLine>
</CodeBlockContent>
```

### Footer [#footer]

`CodeBlockFooter` is a row under the code, below a hairline: a tool's result and how long it took, or a "Show more" button. A string child is a note in the muted ink; other children keep the ink the app gives them.

```tsx
<CodeBlock size="sm">
  <CodeBlockContent wrap>{output}</CodeBlockContent>
  <CodeBlockFooter>
    Output
    <Text style={{ flexGrow: 1, fontFamily: "monospace", color: colors.up }}>2 pass, 0 fail</Text>
    <Text style={{ color: colors.faint }}>exit 0 · 12 ms</Text>
  </CodeBlockFooter>
</CodeBlock>
```

### Height [#height]

Cap the height with `maxHeight` in `style` on `CodeBlockContent`; the code scrolls inside the block. `wrap` wraps long lines instead of scrolling them sideways, and suits output and errors.

```tsx
<CodeBlockContent wrap style={{ maxHeight: 256 }}>
  {output}
</CodeBlockContent>
```

### Show more [#show-more]

Show more is the app's state: cap the content while it is collapsed and put a ghost `Button` in the footer.

```tsx
const expanded = signal(false);

<CodeBlockContent style={expanded() ? undefined : { maxHeight: 256 }}>{code}</CodeBlockContent>
<CodeBlockFooter>
  <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onPress={() => expanded.set(!expanded())}>
    {expanded() ? "Show less" : "Show more"}
  </Button>
</CodeBlockFooter>
```

### In a tool call [#in-a-tool-call]

A `CodeBlock` in a card flush against its edges takes its surface off with `style`: the block's edge and corners go, a hairline stays above.

```tsx
<CodeBlock style={{ borderWidth: 0, borderTopWidth: 1, borderRadius: 0 }}>
  <CodeBlockContent wrap>{code}</CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through on every part but `CodeBlockTitle` (a [`nsh` Text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text)), `CodeBlockCopyButton` (an [`IconButton`](./button)) and `CodeBlockContent` (a [`nsh` Scroll](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll)); `style` goes over the look's. The text of the code is selectable.

| Part                  | Props                                                                                                                                                     | Description                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CodeBlock`           | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"` (default `"default"`); `size`: `"default" \| "sm"` (default `"default"`)                                          | The surface the other parts sit in; hands its variant and size down.                            |
| `CodeBlockHeader`     | —                                                                                                                                                         | A row above the code for a title and its actions, under a hairline.                             |
| `CodeBlockTitle`      | —                                                                                                                                                         | A filename or a label, one line, cut with an ellipsis.                                          |
| `CodeBlockActions`    | —                                                                                                                                                         | Buttons at the end of the header.                                                               |
| `CodeBlockCopyButton` | `value`: `string` (required); `size`: `IconButtonSize` (default `"sm"`); `onPress` is called before the copy                                              | A ghost icon button that copies `value` and shows a check for two seconds ("Copy" → "Copied").  |
| `CodeBlockContent`    | `children`: `string \| JSX.Element`; `lineNumbers`: `boolean` (default `false`); `startLine`: `number` (default `1`); `wrap`: `boolean` (default `false`) | The code: a string split at its newlines, or `CodeBlockLine`s. Scrolls sideways, without a bar. |
| `CodeBlockLine`       | `variant`: `"default" \| "highlighted" \| "added" \| "removed"` (default `"default"`); `lineNumber`: `number` (over the order the lines are drawn in)     | One line of code you draw yourself.                                                             |
| `CodeBlockFooter`     | —                                                                                                                                                         | A row below the code under a hairline: a result, a button. A string child is a muted note.      |

`codeBlockLook()` is exported for a block the app draws itself: its parts as the styles they wear (`root`, `header`, `title`, `actions`, `content`, `code`, `line`, `gutter`, `marker`, `footer`, `footerText`).

# Collapsible (/dev/docs/components/collapsible)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add collapsible
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger } from "@/components/ui/collapsible";
```

```tsx
<Collapsible defaultOpen>
  <CollapsibleTrigger first>Title</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>…</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Collapsible`:

```text
Collapsible
├── CollapsibleTrigger
└── CollapsibleContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Open by default [#open-by-default]

```tsx
<Collapsible defaultOpen>
  <CollapsibleTrigger first>Shipping details</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>Orders leave within a day.</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

### Closed [#closed]

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleTrigger first>Returns</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>Within 30 days, unused and in its box.</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>
```

### A chevron that turns over [#a-chevron-that-turns-over]

`chevron="down"` points the chevron down and turns it over as the row opens, the way an accordion's
turns, for a collapsible that reads as a section of one; `along` (the default) points it along the
row, the way a folder's does. The row takes more than one child, drawn in one line before the chevron.

```tsx
<CollapsibleTrigger chevron="down" first>
  Shipping details
</CollapsibleTrigger>
```

Every trigger but the `first` draws a divider above it, inside its row, so the hover fill meets the line; `start` lines the trigger and the panel up past a leading icon. A row in the panel (`listRow`) reaches past the content, and the revealed region clips it, so give the panel room on both sides: `panel={{ start: 12, end: 12 }}`.

## API [#api]

Uses `disclosureTriggerLook`, `DisclosureChevron`, and `disclosurePanel` from accordion. Composition: `Collapsible`, `CollapsibleTrigger`, `CollapsibleContent`.

| Part                 | Props                                                                                   | Description                                                                         |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Collapsible`        | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange({ open, reason })`, `children`                     | A disclosure row that reveals a panel beneath it.                                   |
| `CollapsibleTrigger` | `children`, `first`, `start`, `chevron` (`"along"` by default, or `"down"`), `disabled` | The title row; `first` drops its top divider, `start` lines it past a leading icon. |
| `CollapsibleContent` | `children`, `panel` (`start`, `end`, `gap`)                                             | The panel beneath, in `disclosurePanel` padding.                                    |

# CollapsingHeader (/dev/docs/components/collapsing-header)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add collapsing-header
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { createAnimatedValue } from "nsh";

import {
  CollapsingHeader,
  CollapsingHeaderBackdrop,
  CollapsingHeaderBar,
  CollapsingHeaderDescription,
  CollapsingHeaderTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/collapsing-header";
```

```tsx
const scroll = createAnimatedValue(0);

<Scroll scrollValue={scroll} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <CollapsingHeader scroll={scroll} expandedHeight={220} collapsedHeight={56}>
    <CollapsingHeaderBackdrop>{picture}</CollapsingHeaderBackdrop>
    <CollapsingHeaderDescription>160 entries, by week</CollapsingHeaderDescription>
    <CollapsingHeaderBar>
      <CollapsingHeaderTitle>Recent</CollapsingHeaderTitle>
    </CollapsingHeaderBar>
  </CollapsingHeader>
  {rows}
</Scroll>;
```

The header is the top of the page it stands in: at `expandedHeight` while the page is at its top,
down to `collapsedHeight` once the page has scrolled `expandedHeight - collapsedHeight`. Everything
follows `scroll` — the scroll view's `scrollValue` — in interpolated styles, so the collapse runs on
the UI thread with no JS per frame. The picture travels at half the scroll and stretches when the
page is pulled past its top, a cover in the header's fill fades over it, the title shrinks into the
bar and the description fades out above it. The header sticks to the top of the scroll view it is
the first child of, so it holds there once collapsed.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `CollapsingHeader`:

```text
CollapsingHeader
├── CollapsingHeaderBackdrop
├── CollapsingHeaderDescription
└── CollapsingHeaderBar
    └── CollapsingHeaderTitle
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A week's page [#a-weeks-page]

The scene of the demo: a header over a list whose week headings stick under the bar. The bar's
height is `collapsingHeaderLook().heights(expandedHeight, collapsedHeight).bar` — the height the
header draws, whole rows in a terminal — so `stickyHeaderOffset` takes it rather than the number
passed in.

```tsx
const OPEN = desktop ? 168 : 220;
const BAR = desktop ? 44 : 56;
const bar = collapsingHeaderLook().heights(OPEN, BAR).bar;

const scroll = createAnimatedValue(0);

<Scroll scrollValue={scroll} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <CollapsingHeader scroll={scroll} expandedHeight={OPEN} collapsedHeight={BAR}>
    <CollapsingHeaderBackdrop>
      <Each of={[1, 2, 3, 4]}>
        {(n) => <View style={ring(n())} />}
      </Each>
    </CollapsingHeaderBackdrop>
    <CollapsingHeaderDescription>18 entries, by week</CollapsingHeaderDescription>
    <CollapsingHeaderBar>
      <CollapsingHeaderTitle>Recent</CollapsingHeaderTitle>
    </CollapsingHeaderBar>
  </CollapsingHeader>
  <List
    viewport="parent"
    each={rows}
    estimatedItemSize={density.row}
    stickyHeaderIndices={weeks}
    stickyHeaderOffset={bar}
  >
    {(row) => (row().week ? <Heading … /> : <Row … />)}
  </List>
</Scroll>;
```

### An action in the bar [#an-action-in-the-bar]

The bar is a row, so what it holds can act: the title takes the room it needs and a button comes
after it, in reach at every height the header has.

```tsx
const starred = signal(false);

<CollapsingHeader scroll={scroll} expandedHeight={168} collapsedHeight={BAR}>
  <CollapsingHeaderBar>
    <CollapsingHeaderTitle>Inbox</CollapsingHeaderTitle>
    <Button
      size="sm"
      variant={starred() ? "default" : "secondary"}
      onPress={() => starred.set(!starred())}
    >
      {starred() ? "Starred" : "Star"}
    </Button>
  </CollapsingHeaderBar>
</CollapsingHeader>;
```

### A header with no picture [#a-header-with-no-picture]

Leave `CollapsingHeaderBackdrop` out: the header is its fill, the description and the title, and
still collapses. A terminal draws no picture either way.

```tsx
<CollapsingHeader scroll={scroll} expandedHeight={96} collapsedHeight={44}>
  <CollapsingHeaderDescription>12 drafts, waiting</CollapsingHeaderDescription>
  <CollapsingHeaderBar>
    <CollapsingHeaderTitle>Drafts</CollapsingHeaderTitle>
  </CollapsingHeaderBar>
</CollapsingHeader>
```

## API [#api]

`CollapsingHeader` is a [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) in the library's look; every
prop of View passes through, and `style` goes over the look's. `CollapsingHeaderBackdrop`,
`CollapsingHeaderDescription` and `CollapsingHeaderBar` take a View's too, and
`CollapsingHeaderTitle` a [`nsh` Text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text)'s; a string child of
`CollapsingHeaderDescription` is drawn as its text.

| Part                          | Props                                                                              | Description                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CollapsingHeader`            | `scroll`: `AnimatedValue`; `expandedHeight`: `number`; `collapsedHeight`: `number` | The page's header: sticks to the top of the scroll view, `expandedHeight` tall at the page's top, `collapsedHeight` once scrolled. |
| `CollapsingHeaderBackdrop`    | —                                                                                  | The picture, travelling at half the scroll and stretching on over-scroll, behind a cover that fades over it. `null` in a terminal. |
| `CollapsingHeaderDescription` | `children`                                                                         | The line above the title, gone by half the collapse.                                                                               |
| `CollapsingHeaderBar`         | —                                                                                  | The strip at the header's bottom, `collapsedHeight` tall: a row, so it holds actions beside the title.                             |
| `CollapsingHeaderTitle`       | —                                                                                  | The page's title, shrinking into the bar's type as the header collapses.                                                           |

The fill is `finish.accent` — the primary color, its ink from the finish's `foreground`, edged in the
hairline's `brand-edge`; the title is the display role open and the label role's size collapsed; the
description is the detail's size; the bar's room either side is `density.pad` and its gap
`density.gap`. In a terminal the heights snap to whole rows and the title does not scale. Reduced
motion drops the picture's travel and its stretch; the cover, the title and the description still
follow the scroll, since they are the collapse itself.

`collapsingHeaderLook()` is exported for a header an app draws itself: the heights as it draws them
(`heights`), the parts as the styles they wear (`root`, `backdrop`, `cover`, `description`,
`descriptionText`, `bar`, `title`, `titleClass`) and the ink the picture is drawn in (`ink`).

# ColorPicker (/dev/docs/components/color-picker)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add color-picker
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { ColorPicker } from "nsh/base";

import {
  ColorPanel,
  ColorPopover,
  colorAreaLook,
  colorSliderLook,
} from "@/components/ui/color-picker";
```

```tsx
<ColorPicker value={color()} onChange={({ value }) => color.set(value)}>
  <ColorPanel
    name="Fill color"
    value={color()}
    format="hex"
    onFormatChange={setFormat}
    alpha
    swatches={PRESETS}
  />
</ColorPicker>
```

`ColorPopover` wraps the same panel in a field trigger. Spread `colorAreaLook()` and `colorSliderLook()` on `ColorArea` / `ColorSlider` when composing your own layout.

## Examples [#examples]

### Panel [#panel]

`ColorPanel` lays out the area, the sliders, the fields and the swatches. It has to sit
inside [`nsh/base`'s `ColorPicker`](https://nsh.dev/elements/color-picker): the panel's
parts look their picker up from that root, and outside it they log
`` `<part>` is outside a `ColorPicker`: its color goes nowhere `` and take no input
(`references/nsh/crates/nsh-base/src/color_picker/mod.rs:59`).

```tsx
<ColorPicker value={fill()} onChange={({ value }) => fill.set(value)}>
  <ColorPanel name="Fill color" value={fill()} format={format()} onFormatChange={setFormat} />
</ColorPicker>
```

### Alpha [#alpha]

```tsx
<ColorPicker value={fill()} onChange={({ value }) => fill.set(value)}>
  <ColorPanel name="Fill color" value={fill()} alpha />
</ColorPicker>
```

### Swatches [#swatches]

```tsx
<ColorPicker value={fill()} onChange={({ value }) => fill.set(value)}>
  <ColorPanel
    name="Fill color"
    value={fill()}
    swatches={["#ef4444", "#22c55e", "#3b82f6", "#8b5cf6"]}
  />
</ColorPicker>
```

### Format [#format]

`format` is one of `hex`, `rgb`, `hsl`, `hsb`, `oklch`; the fields' menu reports the reader's pick with `onFormatChange`.

```tsx
<ColorPicker value={fill()} onChange={({ value }) => fill.set(value)}>
  <ColorPanel name="Fill color" value={fill()} format={format()} onFormatChange={setFormat} />
</ColorPicker>
```

## API [#api]

Look helpers: `colorAreaLook`, `colorSliderLook`, `colorChecker`, `ColorFields`, `ColorTrigger`, `ColorSwatches`, `ColorCopy`, `ColorDropper`, `colorFormats`. Behavior stays in [`nsh/base` ColorPicker](https://nsh.dev/elements/color-picker) parts.

| Part            | Props                                                                                    | Description                                                         |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ColorFields`   | `value`, `name`, `format`, `onFormatChange`, `alpha`                                     | The fields of a color, with the format's menu.                      |
| `ColorPanel`    | every `ColorFields` prop, `swatches`                                                     | The fields with a row of swatches under them; inside `ColorPicker`. |
| `ColorPopover`  | `name`, `value`, `format`, `alpha`, `style`, `onChange`, `onFormatChange`, `onChangeEnd` | The panel wrapped in a field trigger.                               |
| `ColorTrigger`  | `open`, `value`, `style`                                                                 | The field that shows the color and opens the panel.                 |
| `ColorSwatches` | `colors`                                                                                 | The row of swatches, one of them chosen.                            |
| `ColorCopy`     | `name`, `text`                                                                           | Copies the value; a check shows for a moment.                       |
| `ColorDropper`  | `name`                                                                                   | The system eyedropper, hidden where the platform has none.          |

# Combobox (/dev/docs/components/combobox)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add combobox
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Combobox, ComboboxContent, ComboboxItem, ComboboxTrigger } from "@/components/ui/combobox";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<Combobox value={value} onChange={({ value }) => setValue(value)}>
  <ComboboxTrigger />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxItem value="react">React</ComboboxItem>
    <ComboboxItem value="vue">Vue</ComboboxItem>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

Without `multiple`, `value` is the chosen item or `null` (`string | null`). With `multiple`, it is the chosen items (`string[]`).

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Combobox`:

```text
Combobox
├── ComboboxTrigger
├── ComboboxChips
│   └── ComboboxChip
└── ComboboxContent
    ├── ComboboxEmpty
    ├── ComboboxGroup
    │   ├── ComboboxLabel
    │   └── ComboboxItem
    └── ComboboxItem
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Disabled and clearable [#disabled-and-clearable]

```tsx
<Combobox disabled>…</Combobox>
<Combobox cleanable>…</Combobox>
```

### One value [#one-value]

Leave `multiple` out. A choice replaces the last one and closes the list. `onChange` receives `{ value: string | null }`.

```tsx
const assignee = signal<string | null>(null);

<Combobox value={assignee()} onChange={({ value }) => assignee.set(value)}>
  <ComboboxTrigger />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxItem value="ada">Ada Lovelace</ComboboxItem>
    <ComboboxItem value="grace">Grace Hopper</ComboboxItem>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>;
```

The trigger opens and closes the list. So does a press on the field's input, when the platform delivers it: `nsh/base` toggles on the input's press (`references/nsh/crates/nsh-base/src/combobox.rs`, the input's `on_press`). On macOS the field editor takes that click for the caret (`references/nsh/crates/nsh-platform-macos/src/text_input.rs`, `mouseDown`) and the press is never delivered, so a click focuses the field and does not open the list. Tabbing into the field does not open it either. Typing does.

### Several values [#several-values]

`multiple` toggles an item and keeps the list open; the field shows the chosen titles.

```tsx
<Combobox multiple value={tags} onChange={({ value }) => setTags(value)}>
  …
</Combobox>
```

### Chips in the field [#chips-in-the-field]

`ComboboxChips` draws the chosen values as chips at the start of the field — where NSH puts a
multiple combobox's `prefix` — so the input keeps the query and the field grows down as the chips
wrap. A chip's label is its item's title, and its remove button drops that value.

```tsx
<Combobox multiple value={tags} onChange={({ value }) => setTags(value)}>
  <ComboboxChips />
  <ComboboxContent>…</ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

A chip can take a mark at its start (`lead`) or keep its value against a stray press
(`showRemove={false}`); a function child draws each value's chip instead of the default one:

```tsx
<ComboboxChips>
  {(value) => (
    <ComboboxChip
      value={value}
      lead={<Avatar name={name} style={{ width: 18, height: 18 }} />}
      showRemove={value !== "ada"}
    />
  )}
</ComboboxChips>
```

The chips are that `prefix`, not a field of their own: typing beside them still filters through the
combobox's input, and a text field of its own beside the chips is a second control.

`ComboboxChip` and `ComboboxChips` render only inside `<Combobox>` — as `ComboboxChips` (the field's
prefix) or anywhere else under that root, including as a sibling of `ComboboxContent`. Outside the
root they throw. A chip drawn somewhere else, a summary beside the field, is the app's own: read
`value` and update it from the chip's press.

### Groups and an empty list [#groups-and-an-empty-list]

```tsx
<ComboboxContent>
  <ComboboxGroup>
    <ComboboxLabel>Front end</ComboboxLabel>
    <ComboboxItem value="react">React</ComboboxItem>
  </ComboboxGroup>
  <ComboboxEmpty>No matches</ComboboxEmpty>
</ComboboxContent>
```

### A trigger of your own [#a-trigger-of-your-own]

A string child is a `Button`; anything else is drawn as given. `testID` reaches the
button or the default toggle, and `accessibilityLabel` names it (the default toggle is a
chevron with no text of its own).

```tsx
<ComboboxTrigger>
  <Icon icon={ChevronRight} size={14} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
</ComboboxTrigger>
```

## API [#api]

The root owns the open flag and the chosen values; `ComboboxContent` mounts [`nsh/base` Combobox](https://nsh.dev/elements/combobox) and every base prop passes through except those. `comboboxLook`, `listboxProps` and `OptionRow` fill the field, the popup and the rows by default.

| Part              | Props                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Description                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Combobox`        | `value` / `defaultValue` (`string \| null`, or `string[]` with `multiple`), `multiple`, `open` / `defaultOpen`, `disabled`, `cleanable`, `placeholder`, `onChange`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel` | The root: one value, or several when `multiple` is set. `onChange` follows that: `{ value: string \| null }` or `{ value: string[] }`. |
| `ComboboxTrigger` | `children`, `variant`, `disabled`, `testID`, `accessibilityLabel`, `style`                                                                                                                                          | The disclosure at the field's end (a `ComboToggle` by default).                                                                        |
| `ComboboxContent` | `items` (instead of `ComboboxItem` children), `minWidth`, `children`                                                                                                                                                | The field and the list anchored to it; it mounts `nsh/base` Combobox.                                                                  |
| `ComboboxItem`    | `value`, `disabled`, `group`, `children` (a string is its title)                                                                                                                                                    | One choice in the list.                                                                                                                |
| `ComboboxChips`   | `children`: a `(value) => JSX.Element` that draws each one, a `ComboboxChip` by default                                                                                                                             | The chosen values as chips at the field's start (NSH's `prefix`).                                                                      |
| `ComboboxChip`    | `value`, `children` (its text, the item's title by default), `lead`, `showRemove` (default `true`), `style`                                                                                                         | One value's chip. It has to sit inside `<Combobox>`.                                                                                   |
| `ComboboxGroup`   | `children`                                                                                                                                                                                                          | A section of the list.                                                                                                                 |
| `ComboboxLabel`   | `children` (a string)                                                                                                                                                                                               | A section's name.                                                                                                                      |
| `ComboboxEmpty`   | `children` (the message)                                                                                                                                                                                            | What the list shows while the query matches nothing.                                                                                   |

# Command (/dev/docs/components/command)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add command
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Command } from "@/components/ui/command";
```

```tsx
<Command items={items} onSelect={({ id }) => {}} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Groups [#groups]

Rows with the same `group` gather under its heading, in the order given; `disabled` dims a row.

```tsx
const items: CommandItem[] = [
  { id: "new", label: "New File", group: "File", shortcut: "mod+n" },
  { id: "open", label: "Open File", group: "File", disabled: true },
  { id: "settings", label: "Settings", group: "View", shortcut: "mod+comma" },
];

<Command items={items} onSelect={({ id }) => run(id)} />;
```

### Shortcut and check [#shortcut-and-check]

`shortcut` is drawn with a pointer in `kbd`'s key cap, the library's one (`add command` brings it); `checked` marks the row in effect.

```tsx
const items: CommandItem[] = [
  { id: "theme", label: "Toggle Theme", group: "View", checked: true },
  { id: "settings", label: "Settings", group: "View", shortcut: "mod+comma" },
];
```

### Search [#search]

The field filters the rows as you type. The shell sets the search bar's row and the field's text
and placeholder color inline (`commandSearchBarStyle`, `commandSearchStyle`), over
`commandClasses`, so an icon in `searchPrefix` stays beside the field and the placeholder stays
the muted foreground — including when `searchable` turns the bar on after the palette has mounted.
A caller's `searchBarStyle` and `searchStyle` win over those.

```tsx
<Command
  items={items}
  accessibilityLabel="Commands"
  searchAccessibilityLabel="Search commands"
  onSelect={({ id }) => run(id)}
/>
```

### A long list [#a-long-list]

The rows are made as they come into view, so five thousand files cost what five do: `listClass`
gives the list its height and the rest scrolls. `keywords` let the query find a file by its
extension as well as by its name (`png` finds every image), `renderItem` draws the extension's
icon, and the ref's `matchedCount()` is what the query left — the count under the palette reads
it, never the app's guess at the filter.

```tsx
const EXTENSIONS = ["rs", "tsx", "md", "json", "png"] as const;

const FILES: CommandItem[] = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, index) => {
  const extension = EXTENSIONS[index % EXTENSIONS.length];
  const folder = `module-${String(Math.floor(index / 100) + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  return {
    id: `file-${index}`,
    label: `${folder}/file-${index + 1}.${extension}`,
    group: folder,
    keywords: [extension],
  };
});

const files = signal(FILES.length);
let palette: CommandRef | undefined;

<Command
  ref={(ref) => (palette = ref)}
  items={FILES}
  listClass="h-60"
  placeholder="Search files by name or extension…"
  searchAccessibilityLabel="Search files"
  empty={<CommandEmpty label="No file matches" />}
  onQueryChange={() => void palette?.matchedCount().then((count) => files.set(count))}
  renderItem={(entry) => <CommandRow entry={entry} icon={iconFor(entry.label)} />}
/>

<Text class="text-muted-foreground" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
  {`${files()} of ${FILES.length} files, 50 folders`}
</Text>
```

## API [#api]

Uses `commandClasses`, `CommandRow`, `CommandHeading`, and `CommandEmpty` by default. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Command](https://nsh.dev/elements/command) passes through.

| Part             | Props                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Command`        | —                                 | A command palette: a search field over virtualized, natively filtered rows, however many there are. `searchBarStyle` and `searchStyle` still pass through, over the shell's row and placeholder color. |
| `CommandRow`     | `entry`, `icon`, `detail`, `note` | A row's content: the icon, the label, a `note` at the end, the shortcut's keys and a check for the item in effect.                                                                                     |
| `CommandHeading` | `group`                           | A section's heading: small capitals in the faint color.                                                                                                                                                |
| `CommandEmpty`   | `label`                           | What the palette shows while nothing matches.                                                                                                                                                          |

# Context Menu (/dev/docs/components/context-menu)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add context-menu
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/context-menu";
```

```tsx
<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger>
    <View>Right click here</View>
  </ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent>
    <ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => {}}>Copy</ContextMenuItem>
  </ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `ContextMenu`:

```text
ContextMenu
├── ContextMenuTrigger
└── ContextMenuContent
    ├── ContextMenuGroup
    │   ├── ContextMenuLabel
    │   ├── ContextMenuItem
    │   │   └── ContextMenuShortcut
    │   ├── ContextMenuCheckboxItem
    │   └── ContextMenuRadioItem
    ├── ContextMenuSeparator
    └── ContextMenuSub
        ├── ContextMenuSubTrigger
        └── ContextMenuSubContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A surface [#a-surface]

Any view can be the trigger; the menu opens at the pointer on a secondary click or a long press.

```tsx
<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger>
    <View style={{ height: 150 }}>Right click or hold</View>
  </ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent margin={8}>
    <ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => copy()}>Copy</ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => paste()}>Paste</ContextMenuItem>
  </ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>
```

### Separator and a destructive item [#separator-and-a-destructive-item]

```tsx
<ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => cut()}>Cut</ContextMenuItem>
<ContextMenuSeparator />
<ContextMenuItem variant="destructive" onSelect={() => remove()}>
  Delete
</ContextMenuItem>
```

### Keep it open [#keep-it-open]

`closeOnSelect={false}` leaves the menu up for a toggle inside it.

```tsx
<ContextMenuItem closeOnSelect={false} onSelect={() => setPinned(!pinned())}>
  <Text style={menuItemLabel()}>{() => (pinned() ? "Unpin" : "Pin")}</Text>
</ContextMenuItem>
```

### A checkable row and its neighbours [#a-checkable-row-and-its-neighbours]

A checkable row keeps its mark's room whether it is checked or not, so its label stays put as it
is toggled. `inset` gives the plain rows of the same menu that room too, and their labels line up
with it. `ContextMenuLabel` and `ContextMenuSubTrigger` take it as well.

```tsx
<ContextMenuItem checked={pinned()} closeOnSelect={false} onSelect={() => setPinned(!pinned())}>
  Pin
</ContextMenuItem>
<ContextMenuItem inset onSelect={() => cut()}>Cut</ContextMenuItem>
<ContextMenuItem inset onSelect={() => copy()}>Copy</ContextMenuItem>
```

### Open change [#open-change]

```tsx
<ContextMenu onOpenChange={({ open, reason }) => log(open, reason)}>…</ContextMenu>
```

## API [#api]

Row and popup looks come from Menu. Items, separators, labels and submenus are re-exported as `ContextMenu*` parts. There is no radio-group part: a `ContextMenuGroup` holds the rows, and each `ContextMenuRadioItem` carries its own `checked`.

| Part                 | Props                                                                                                                                                    | Description                                                                            |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ContextMenu`        | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `disabled`, `onOpenChange({ open, reason })`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel`                                                     | Open state and the trigger slot                                                        |
| `ContextMenuTrigger` | `children`, `style`                                                                                                                                      | Secondary click or long press; wraps its children, in a `View` when it takes a `style` |
| `ContextMenuContent` | every `nsh/base` ContextMenu prop but open state, `disabled`, `trigger` and the lifecycle callbacks; `offset` (default 4), `popupStyle`, `backdropStyle` | The popup or sheet                                                                     |
| `ContextMenuItem` …  | as the Menu counterparts                                                                                                                                 | Rows, labels, separators and submenus                                                  |

# Coverage (/dev/docs/components/coverage)

Two official sets are worth answering for: the

<a href="https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components">shadcn/ui components</a>, whose parts and API names
this library follows, and the <a href="https://nsh.dev/elements">NSH elements</a> it is built on.
Each table lists every component of theirs and where it went here: a page under another name counts,
and a row with no page says why there is none.

This page is generated from `apps/website/src/lib/official.ts`; do not edit it. Add a component there,
then run `bun run docs:components`. Its NSH rows are also what makes a page _Official_ on 

<a href="/docs/components">Components</a>: a page named in one of them is aligned with an NSH
element, and a page named in none is this library's own. `bun run check:pages` fails when an
official component has no row, when a row names a page that does not exist, and when a row serves
nothing without saying why.

## shadcn/ui [#shadcnui]

<CoverageTable group="shadcn" />

## NSH base [#nsh-base]

<CoverageTable group="base" />

## NSH primitives [#nsh-primitives]

<CoverageTable group="primitives" />

# DataTable (/dev/docs/components/data-table)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add data-table
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { DataTable } from "@/components/ui/data-table";
```

```tsx
<DataTable columns={columns} data={rows} stripe />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Columns [#columns]

`width`, `align` and `sortable` are per column.

```tsx
const columns: DataTableColumn[] = [
  { key: "id", title: "ID", width: 56, align: "end", sortable: true },
  { key: "name", title: "Name", width: 120, sortable: true },
  { key: "score", title: "Score", width: 72, align: "end", sortable: true },
];
```

### Stripes [#stripes]

```tsx
<DataTable columns={columns} data={people} stripe />
```

### A fixed body [#a-fixed-body]

The table fills and scrolls in the box it is given.

```tsx
<View style={{ height: 200 }}>
  <DataTable columns={columns} data={people} style={{ flex: 1 }} />
</View>
```

### Fit padding [#fit-padding]

A column fitted to its content takes `fitPadding` for the room the drawing adds beside the text: a
column of this look sets **16** — 8 points before a cell's text, 4 after it, and the 4-point gap
before a header's sort button.

```tsx
columns.map((column) => ({ ...column, fitPadding: 16 }));
```

### Fixed columns [#fixed-columns]

`fixed: true` pins a column at the leading edge (`"left"` and `"right"` say which edge) while the
rest scroll horizontally under it. Fixed columns lead the row, take their width from `width`
(content cannot set it) and keep their place in the header too; the seam between a pinned column
and the scrolling body is `fixedEdge` in `dataTableClasses`. Give the table more columns than fit
the box to see it work.

```tsx
const columns: DataTableColumn[] = [
  { key: "id", title: "ID", width: 70, align: "end", fixed: true, sortable: true },
  { key: "name", title: "Name", width: 150, fixed: true, sortable: true },
  { key: "city", title: "City", width: 120, sortable: true },
  { key: "team", title: "Team", width: 110 },
  { key: "level", title: "Level", width: 90 },
  { key: "joined", title: "Joined", width: 110 },
  { key: "score", title: "Score", width: 90, align: "end", sortable: true },
  { key: "handle", title: "Handle", width: 140 },
];

<View style={{ height: 300 }}>
  <DataTable columns={columns} data={people} style={{ flex: 1 }} />
</View>;
```

### Selecting [#selecting]

Rows select by default; `columnSelectable` lets titles select columns and `cellSelectable` lets
cells select. `onSelectionChange` reports the `{ row, column }` selection (both zero-based), and
`selection` sets it back — a controlled selection, so what stays selected is the app's call. A
selection of a kind that does not select is cleared.

```tsx
const mode = signal<"row" | "cell" | "column">("row");
const selection = signal<DataTableSelection | null>(null);

const setMode = (next: "row" | "cell" | "column") => {
  mode.set(next);
  selection.set(null);
};

<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={people}
  rowSelectable={mode() === "row"}
  cellSelectable={mode() === "cell"}
  columnSelectable={mode() === "column"}
  selection={selection()}
  onSelectionChange={({ selection: next }) => selection.set(next)}
  onRowPress={({ row, column }) => log(`row ${row}, column ${column}`)}
/>;
```

A selection of several is the app's too: set `selectOnModifierPress={false}`, keep your own range or
set in `onRowPress` / `onColumnPress` (each reports Shift, Control, Option and the clicks), and paint
it with `rowClasses`, `cellClasses` or the columns' `headerClass` / `cellClass`.

## API [#api]

| Part        | Props                                                              | Description                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `DataTable` | every `nsh/base` DataTable prop; `classes` over `dataTableClasses` | A striped table, sortable and resizable |

Uses `dataTableClasses`. Every prop of [`nsh/base` DataTable](https://nsh.dev/elements/data-table) passes through.

# Date Picker (/dev/docs/components/date-picker)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add date-picker
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { DatePicker, DatePickerContent, DatePickerTrigger } from "@/components/ui/date-picker";
```

```tsx
<DatePicker value={value} onChange={({ value }) => setValue(value)}>
  <DatePickerTrigger />
  <DatePickerContent />
</DatePicker>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `DatePicker`:

```text
DatePicker
├── DatePickerTrigger
└── DatePickerContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A range [#a-range]

`range` on the content; the trigger shows both ends. After the first pick the band previews the
range to the day under the pointer or the keyboard, as the calendar's does.

```tsx
<DatePicker value={range} onChange={({ value }) => setRange(value)}>
  <DatePickerTrigger />
  <DatePickerContent range />
</DatePicker>
```

### The time of day [#the-time-of-day]

```tsx
<DatePickerContent timePrecision="minute" />
```

### Presets [#presets]

```tsx
<DatePickerContent
  presets={[
    { label: "Today", value: today },
    { label: "Last 7 days", value: lastWeek },
  ]}
/>
```

### Two months [#two-months]

```tsx
<DatePickerContent numberOfMonths={2} />
```

### Clearable, and a placeholder [#clearable-and-a-placeholder]

Without a value the trigger shows `placeholder` (default "Pick a date") muted.

```tsx
<DatePicker cleanable placeholder="Due date">
  <DatePickerTrigger />
  <DatePickerContent />
</DatePicker>
```

## API [#api]

| Part                | Props                                                                                                                                                 | Description                                                |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DatePicker`        | `value` / `defaultValue`, `open` / `defaultOpen`, `disabled`, `cleanable`, `placeholder`, `onChange`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel` | Open state and the value                                   |
| `DatePickerTrigger` | `title` (default the value), `placeholder`, `invalid`, `clearable`, `style`, `testID`, `accessibilityLabel`                                           | A `DateTrigger`, the pressed field that opens the calendar |
| `DatePickerContent` | `range`, `timePrecision`, `presets`, `numberOfMonths`, `firstDayOfWeek`, …                                                                            | The calendar in the popup                                  |

`testID` finds the trigger in UI tests, and `accessibilityLabel` names it when the
content does not name the field. The root owns the open flag and the value;
`DatePickerContent` mounts [`nsh/base` DatePicker](https://nsh.dev/elements/date-picker)
and every base prop passes through except those. `datePickerLook` fills the popup, the scrim, the calendar and the time's row by default.

# Dialog (/dev/docs/components/dialog)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add dialog
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/dialog";
```

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger variant="default">Delete item…</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogTitle>Delete this item?</DialogTitle>
    <DialogDescription>A press on the dimmed backdrop closes it.</DialogDescription>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose>Keep</DialogClose>
      <DialogClose variant="destructive" onPress={remove}>
        Delete
      </DialogClose>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Dialog`:

```text
Dialog
├── DialogTrigger
└── DialogContent
    ├── DialogTitle
    ├── DialogDescription
    └── DialogFooter
        └── DialogClose
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Width [#width]

The card is 360 points with a pointer and 320 on a touch screen; `width` sets another, never past 90% of the window.

```tsx
<DialogContent width={480}>…</DialogContent>
```

### Motion [#motion]

`animation` is `fade` (the card's default), `slide`, or `none`.

```tsx
<DialogContent animation="slide">…</DialogContent>
```

### Presentation [#presentation]

`presentation` hands the dialog to the system: `fullScreen` comes up over the window, `pageSheet` and `formSheet` come up as the system's sheet, with what is behind them still in sight (iOS). The system draws the card there — its edge, its radius, its shadow, its place and its height — so the content wears no card, and the app's `style` starts from a page (`dialogPage`) instead. Desktops and the web ignore `presentation`: there the card stands.

```tsx
<DialogContent presentation="fullScreen">…</DialogContent>
```

### Scrolling [#scrolling]

The card is never taller than the window holds inside the safe areas, 24 points clear of either edge, and its body scrolls under that cap. `DialogFooter` is drawn under the scrolling body, so the actions stay put; `DialogTitle` and `DialogDescription` are in the body and scroll with it (put them in their own block if the title has to stay).

```tsx
<DialogContent>
  <DialogTitle>Order ticket</DialogTitle>
  <View style={{ gap: 12 }}>{fields}</View>
  <DialogFooter>
    <DialogClose>Cancel</DialogClose>
    <DialogClose variant="default">Place order</DialogClose>
  </DialogFooter>
</DialogContent>
```

`scroll={false}` draws the children as given, with no scroll of the shell's: for a body that takes gestures of its own.

```tsx
<DialogContent scroll={false}>…</DialogContent>
```

### A page of its own [#a-page-of-its-own]

A dialog the app fills the window with — a lightbox, an editor — passes `dialogPage()` as `style`: it takes the card's edge, radius, shadow, padding, width and height cap off and fills what the dialog gives it.

```tsx
import { DialogContent, dialogPage } from "@/components/ui/dialog";

<DialogContent style={dialogPage()} scroll={false} animation="fade">
  {image}
</DialogContent>;
```

### Closing [#closing]

Escape, a backdrop press and a downward swipe close the dialog; turn any of them off on the content.

```tsx
<DialogContent closeOnEscape={false} closeOnBackdropPress={false} closeOnSwipe={false}>
  …
</DialogContent>
```

### Card and backdrop [#card-and-backdrop]

`style` goes over the card's chrome, `backdropStyle` over the scrim.

```tsx
<DialogContent
  style={{ padding: 32, maxWidth: 480 }}
  backdropStyle={{ backgroundColor: alpha(colors.foreground, 0.4) }}
>
  …
</DialogContent>
```

### Controlled [#controlled]

`open` owns the state; `onOpenChange` reports the next one and why.

```tsx
<Dialog open={open()} onOpenChange={({ open: next }) => setOpen(next)}>
  …
</Dialog>
```

## API [#api]

`Dialog` owns the open state. `DialogContent` mounts [`nsh/base` Dialog](https://nsh.dev/elements/dialog); every base prop passes through it, and base owns the backdrop, the popup host and Escape, back and swipe.

| Part                | Props                                                                                                                                                                     | Description                                                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Dialog`            | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange({ open, reason })`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel`                                                                                  | Open state                                                     |
| `DialogTrigger`     | `children`, `variant`, `disabled`, `style`                                                                                                                                | What opens the dialog                                          |
| `DialogContent`     | `width`, `scroll`, every `nsh/base` Dialog prop (`presentation`); `style` over `dialogCard` (or `dialogPage` when the system presents it), `backdropStyle` over the scrim | The card                                                       |
| `DialogTitle`       | `children`; a string takes `dialogTitle`                                                                                                                                  | The card's title                                               |
| `DialogDescription` | `children`; a string takes `dialogText`                                                                                                                                   | The muted line under the title                                 |
| `DialogFooter`      | `children`, `style`                                                                                                                                                       | The row of actions at the card's end, under the scrolling body |
| `DialogClose`       | As `DialogTrigger`, plus `onPress` before it closes                                                                                                                       | What closes the dialog                                         |

A string child of `DialogTrigger` or `DialogClose` is a `Button`; `variant` picks its look (`secondary` by default). Anything else is drawn as given.

# DiffView (/dev/docs/components/diff-view)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add diff-view
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { DiffView, diffViewStyles, DiffHunkActions, diffHunkTone } from "@/components/ui/diff-view";
```

```tsx
<DiffView
  oldValue={before}
  newValue={after}
  layout="unified"
  renderHunkActions={(hunk) => (
    <DiffHunkActions
      index={hunk.index}
      tone={diffHunkTone(hunk, "unified")}
      onRevert={() => ref?.revertHunk(hunk.index)}
      onKeep={() => ref?.acceptHunk(hunk.index)}
    />
  )}
/>
```

`DiffView` defaults `styles` to `diffViewStyles()`.

## Examples [#examples]

### Tone [#tone]

`DiffHunkActions` takes a `tone` for the backing it fades in over: `diffHunkTone` answers the change's own row (`up` for an added line, `down` for a deleted one), and any of the theme's tones works, read where the backing is drawn.

```tsx
<DiffHunkActions index={0} tone="up" onRevert={() => {}} onKeep={() => {}} />
<DiffHunkActions index={1} tone={() => (verdict() === "bad" ? "destructive" : "warn")} onRevert={() => {}} onKeep={() => {}} />
```

### Unified [#unified]

```tsx
<DiffView
  layout="unified"
  oldValue={'fn main() {\n    println!("alpha");\n}'}
  newValue={'fn main() {\n    println!("gamma");\n}'}
  language="rust"
/>
```

### Side by side [#side-by-side]

`layout="split"` puts the old text on the left and the new on the right.

```tsx
<DiffView layout="split" oldValue={before} newValue={after} language="rust" />
```

### Actions on a change [#actions-on-a-change]

`renderHunkActions` drops `DiffHunkActions` onto each change; `diffHunkTone` picks the tint its backing needs.

```tsx
<DiffView
  oldValue={before}
  newValue={after}
  renderHunkActions={(hunk) => (
    <DiffHunkActions
      index={hunk.index}
      tone={diffHunkTone(hunk, "unified")}
      onRevert={() => ref?.revertHunk(hunk.index)}
      onKeep={() => ref?.acceptHunk(hunk.index)}
    />
  )}
/>
```

### Theme colors [#theme-colors]

`DiffView` defaults `styles` to `diffViewStyles()`; pass your own to change only the parts you name.

```tsx
<DiffView oldValue={before} newValue={after} styles={diffViewStyles()} />
```

## API [#api]

| Part              | Props                                                            | Description                 |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `DiffView`        | every `nsh/base` DiffView prop; `styles` over `diffViewStyles()` | Two texts, or a patch       |
| `DiffHunkActions` | `index`, `iconOnly`, `tone`, `onRevert`, `onKeep`                | Revert and Keep on a change |

Every prop of [`nsh/base` DiffView](https://nsh.dev/elements/diff-view) passes through.

# DockArea (/dev/docs/components/dock-area)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add dock-area
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { DockArea, DockTab, dockClasses } from "@/components/ui/dock-area";
```

```tsx
<DockArea defaultLayout={layout} style={{ height: 240 }} />
```

Use `DockTab`, `dockTabCloseClass`, and `DockDragPreview` in `renderTab` / `renderDragPreview`, or rely on the defaults.

## Examples [#examples]

### Tabs [#tabs]

`defaultLayout` is the data; `renderTab` and `renderPanel` draw each tab and panel.

```tsx
const layout: DockAreaLayout = {
  center: { type: "tabs", panels: ["readme", "preview"], activeIndex: 0 },
};

<DockArea
  defaultLayout={layout}
  renderTab={(tab) => <DockTab title={tab.panel} active={tab.active} />}
  renderPanel={(panel) => <Text>{panel.id}</Text>}
/>;
```

### Default chrome [#default-chrome]

Leave the render props out and the area uses `DockTab` and `DockDragPreview`; `dockClasses` is the chrome of every part.

```tsx
<DockArea defaultLayout={layout} style={{ height: 240 }} />
```

## API [#api]

| Part              | Props                                                                                                                   | Description                 |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `DockArea`        | every `nsh/base` DockArea prop; `renderTab`, `renderDragPreview`, `renderEmpty` and the part classes over `dockClasses` | Tabs, splits and edge docks |
| `DockTab`         | `title`, `active`, `testID`, `children`                                                                                 | A tab's title and underline |
| `DockDragPreview` | `title`                                                                                                                 | A dragged tab's chip        |

`DockArea` spreads `dockClasses` and default tab/panel renderers. Every prop of [`nsh/base` DockArea](https://nsh.dev/elements/dock) passes through, and so do the types those props, its ref and its callbacks name — a call site reads them from this file, not from `nsh/base`: `DockAreaProps`, `DockAreaRef`, `DockAreaLayout`, `DockRegion`, `DockNode`, `DockPlacement`, `DockPanel`, `DockPanelOptions`, `DockTarget`, `DockDropIndicator` and `DockInfo`.

`groupClass` is applied after the look's `flex-1 bg-inset`. A later background utility replaces the fill, so `groupClass="bg-card"` draws card-colored groups without `groupStyle`.

A tab as `renderTab` and `renderDragPreview` receive it is `DockTabValue`: `nsh/base`'s `DockTab`, named so here because `DockTab` is the component the tab is drawn with.

```tsx
import { DockTab, type DockTabValue } from "@/components/ui/dock-area";

const tab = (value: DockTabValue) => <DockTab title={value.panel} active={value.active} />;
```

# Drawer (/dev/docs/components/drawer)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add drawer
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/drawer";
```

```tsx
<Drawer>
  <DrawerTrigger>Share…</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Share this photo</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>Anyone with the link can view it.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose>Cancel</DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Drawer`:

```text
Drawer
├── DrawerTrigger
└── DrawerContent
    ├── DrawerHeader
    │   ├── DrawerTitle
    │   └── DrawerDescription
    └── DrawerFooter
        └── DrawerClose
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A swipe closes it [#a-swipe-closes-it]

`closeOnSwipe` is on by default — unlike [`Sheet`](./sheet), which does not follow a drag: the drawer is
a phone's panel, so dragging its top edge down past a third of its height (or 800 points a second)
closes it, and a scroll inside it hands the drag over at its top. Escape, Android's back and a press
on the scrim close it too; all of them are `nsh/base`'s, and `closeOnEscape` /
`closeOnBackdropPress` / `closeOnSwipe` turn each one off.

```tsx
<DrawerContent closeOnSwipe={false}>…</DrawerContent>
```

### The grabber [#the-grabber]

The pill at the top edge is the drawer's (`drawerGrabber`: 100 by 8 points, fully round, in the muted
fill) and it shows on a bottom drawer only, the one it can be dragged from. `sheetGrabber` is the
sheet's narrower pill; a drawer that should not be dragged takes `DrawerContent` without the look —
the grabber is drawn by the component, not by the app.

### Another edge [#another-edge]

`side` takes any edge of the panel (`"bottom"` unless set). A drawer from the left or the right keeps
the panel's full height and its inner corners on the card's radius.

```tsx
<DrawerContent side="right">…</DrawerContent>
```

### A list of actions [#a-list-of-actions]

A drawer's actions stack — that is what a finger reaches on a phone — so `DrawerFooter` is a column
and each action is as wide as the drawer. A row of destinations is a `DrawerClose` each, so tapping
one closes the drawer after its `onPress`.

```tsx
<DrawerFooter>
  <DrawerClose variant="default">Copy link</DrawerClose>
  <DrawerClose>Cancel</DrawerClose>
</DrawerFooter>
```

### Against `Sheet` [#against-sheet]

Opening from the bottom by default, the grabber, the swipe, and the four parts around the panel
(`DrawerHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerFooter`). The panel, the scrim and the
title's type are shared: `sheetPanel(side)`, `backdrop()`, `dialogTitle()` and `dialogText()`, so a
drawer and the rest of the library wear one surface.

## API [#api]

| Part                | Props                                                                                                         | Description                                                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Drawer`            | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange({ open, reason })`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel`                      | Open state and lifecycle                                       |
| `DrawerTrigger`     | `children`, `variant`, `disabled`, `style`                                                                    | A `Button` for a string child, else a pressable of its own     |
| `DrawerContent`     | `side`, every `nsh/base` Sheet prop but open state and the lifecycle callbacks; `popupStyle`, `backdropStyle` | The panel                                                      |
| `DrawerHeader`      | `children`, `style`                                                                                           | A column holding the title and its description, 2 points apart |
| `DrawerTitle`       | `children`, `style`                                                                                           | The panel's title                                              |
| `DrawerDescription` | `children`, `style`                                                                                           | The muted line under it                                        |
| `DrawerFooter`      | `children`, `style`                                                                                           | The actions, stacked, each as wide as the drawer               |
