| `DrawerClose`       | As `DrawerTrigger`, plus `onPress`                                                                            | Closes it after its own `onPress`                              |

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Sheet](https://nsh.dev/elements/sheet) passes through on `DrawerContent`
except open state and the lifecycle callbacks, which the root owns. `popupStyle` and `backdropStyle`
go over the look's. Defaults: `side` `"bottom"`, `closeOnSwipe` `true`.

# Editor (/dev/docs/components/editor)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add editor
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Editor } from "@/components/ui/editor";
```

```tsx
<Editor defaultValue={source} language="typescript" style={{ height: 240 }} />
```

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Editor](https://nsh.dev/elements/editor) passes through: the text (`value` / `defaultValue`, `onChange`), the language and its highlighting, folding, soft wrap, search, the editing keys and the diagnostics. The shell adds the look (`editorClasses`) and the surface (`editorFrame()`).

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build an `Editor`:

```text
Editor
└── EditorFindBar
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Languages [#languages]

`language` takes a name, an extension or a file name; the editor highlights it and follows its editing rules (comments, brackets, indentation).

```tsx
<Editor defaultValue={json} language="json" style={{ height: 200 }} />
<Editor defaultValue={css} language="css.example" style={{ height: 200 }} />
```

### Diagnostics [#diagnostics]

Ranges the app marks, carried through edits until it sets new ones: an error is underlined in the theme's `destructive`, a warning in `warn`, information in `info`, a hint in `muted-foreground`.

```tsx
<Editor
  defaultValue={source}
  language="typescript"
  diagnostics={[
    {
      range: { start: { line: 2, column: 6 }, end: { line: 2, column: 12 } },
      severity: "warning",
      message: "'unused' is declared but its value is never read.",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Find and replace [#find-and-replace]

`search` is what the editor finds and highlights; `onSearchChange` says what it found — how many
matches, which of them the selection is on, or why a pattern is not a regular expression. The editor
never sets the search itself (`EditorRef` replaces a match, it does not find one), so the bar that
edits it is a part: `EditorFindBar` takes the editor's `ref`, **the same object the app hands the
editor's `search`**, and the `result` the editor reported. What is typed into the bar goes back
through `onSearchChange`; its buttons run the editor's own `findNext`, `findPrevious`, `replace` and
`replaceAll` (and the bar says how many a Replace all rewrote for a moment).

Where the bar is and whether it is open are the app's: it sits beside the editor in the same `View`
rather than inside it, since a part cannot leave the tree. The keys are the app's too — Escape and
`mod+f` belong to its `keymap`, as a part that captured them would take them from the editor while
the bar is closed. Because the search is one object, a query the app sets — from
`onFindWithSelection`, or from a keybinding — reads in the bar, and the bar's edits move the
editor's matches as it types.

```tsx
import { keymap, signal, View } from "nsh";

import {
  Editor,
  EditorFindBar,
  type EditorRef,
  type EditorSearch,
  type EditorSearchResult,
} from "@/components/ui/editor";

const search = signal<EditorSearch>({ query: "" });
const found = signal<EditorSearchResult | null>(null);
// The editor's ref, in a signal: the bar takes it as a prop, so it arrives with the editor.
const editor = signal<EditorRef | null>(null);
const finding = signal(false);
keymap.bind("mod+f", () => finding.set(true));

<View style={{ height: 280 }}>
  <Editor
    ref={(node) => editor.set(node)}
    defaultValue={source}
    language="typescript"
    search={finding() ? search() : null}
    onSearchChange={({ result }) => found.set(result)}
    style={{ flex: 1 }}
  />
  {finding() && editor() ? (
    <EditorFindBar
      editor={editor()}
      search={search()}
      onSearchChange={(next) => search.set(next)}
      result={found()}
      onClose={() => finding.set(false)}
      style={{ position: "absolute", top: 8, end: 8, width: 400 }}
    />
  ) : null}
</View>;
```

### Parts [#parts]

`classes` goes over `editorClasses` part by part (an app's classes come after ours; `null` drops ours), and `style` over `editorFrame()`. The font is set with `fontFamily`, `fontSize` and `lineHeight`, which the editor measures its rows in.

```tsx
<Editor
  defaultValue={source}
  language="typescript"
  classes={{ gutter: null, selection: "bg-brand/40" }}
  style={{ height: 240 }}
/>
```

### Hover and quick fixes [#hover-and-quick-fixes]

`onHover` reports where the pointer rests: the character, the word it is in, **the word's box on the
page** (`pageBounds`, what a popup is placed against) and the diagnostics there; `onHoverEnd` says
it left. The app answers with an `Overlay` anchored to that box, so the card follows the word as the
text scrolls and flips below it where there is no room. A card that carries buttons is kept alive
while the pointer is over it — `onMouseEnter` / `onMouseLeave` on the card, a timer that closes it a
moment after the pointer leaves — or it vanishes under the pointer on the way to them. A fix
rewrites the file, which the app owns (`value` / `onChange`).

```tsx
const source = signal(LINTED);
const card = signal<{ anchor: Bounds; diagnostics: EditorDiagnostic[] } | null>(null);
let overCard = false;
let closeTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
const closeSoon = () => {
  clearTimeout(closeTimer);
  closeTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    if (!overCard) card.set(null);
  }, 250);
};
cleanup(() => clearTimeout(closeTimer));

<Editor
  value={source()}
  onChange={({ value }) => source.set(value)}
  language="typescript"
  diagnostics={LINT}
  onHover={(event) => {
    clearTimeout(closeTimer);
    if (event.diagnostics.length === 0) {
      if (!overCard) card.set(null);
      return;
    }
    card.set({ anchor: event.pageBounds, diagnostics: event.diagnostics });
  }}
  onHoverEnd={closeSoon}
  style={{ height: 200 }}
/>;

{
  card() ? (
    <Overlay anchor={card()!.anchor} placement="top" align="start" offset={4} margin={8}>
      <View
        onMouseEnter={() => {
          overCard = true;
          clearTimeout(closeTimer);
        }}
        onMouseLeave={() => {
          overCard = false;
          closeSoon();
        }}
        style={{ ...popoverLook({ compact: true }), maxWidth: 300, gap: 10 }}
      >
        {card()!.diagnostics.map((diagnostic) => (
          <View style={{ gap: 6 }}>
            <Text
              style={{
                fontSize: 12,
                color: diagnostic.severity === "warning" ? colors.warn : colors.destructive,
              }}
            >
              {`${diagnostic.severity ?? "error"}: ${diagnostic.message}`}
            </Text>
            {fixesOf(diagnostic).map((fix) => (
              <Button
                variant="secondary"
                size="sm"
                style={{ alignSelf: "flex-start" }}
                onPress={() => source.set(fix.apply(source()))}
              >
                {fix.title}
              </Button>
            ))}
          </View>
        ))}
      </View>
    </Overlay>
  ) : null;
}
```

### Controlled text [#controlled-text]

Pass `value` and set it again in `onChange`; the app owns the file, as a formatter's output or a loaded file replaces it.

```tsx
import { signal } from "nsh";

const source = signal(SAMPLE);

<Editor value={source()} onChange={({ value }) => source.set(value)} language="typescript" />;
```

## API [#api]

| Part                 | Props                                                           | Description                                                                  |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Editor`             | every [`nsh/base` Editor](https://nsh.dev/elements/editor) prop | Themed `nsh/base` Editor on the field's well.                                |
| `EditorProps`        | —                                                               | `nsh/base`'s `EditorProps`, unchanged.                                       |
| `EditorFindBar`      | `EditorFindBarProps`                                            | The find bar: the query with its count, its modes, and replace.              |
| `EditorFindBarProps` | —                                                               | `editor`, `search`, `onSearchChange`, `result`, `onClose`, `class`, `style`. |
| `editorClasses`      | —                                                               | The look of the editor's parts (classes, by part).                           |
| `editorFrame`        | —                                                               | The surface's style: the field's fill, edge and control corners.             |

The session types the props name are re-exported from this file, so an app does not import them from `nsh/base`: `EditorRef`, `EditorDecoration`, `EditorDiagnostic`, `EditorPosition`, `EditorRange`, `EditorSelection`, `EditorSearchResult`, `EditorCommand`, `EditorCompletionItem`, and the rest of the editor's value types.

# Emoji picker (/dev/docs/components/emoji-picker)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add emoji-picker
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { EmojiPanel } from "@/components/ui/emoji-picker";
```

```tsx
<EmojiPanel onSelect={({ emoji }) => send(emoji)} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Recent emoji [#recent-emoji]

```tsx
<EmojiPanel recent={["👍", "🎉"]} onSelect={onPick} />
```

### In a composer [#in-a-composer]

A composer keeps the panel behind a `Popover` on the field's leading addon. Choosing closes the
panel and puts the emoji at the end of the draft; `base` (the emoji without its skin tone) is what
leads the recents, so the tab that holds it opens first the next time.

```tsx
const recent = signal<string[]>([]);
const draft = signal("");
const picking = signal(false);

const put = (emoji: string, base: string) => {
  draft.set(draft() + emoji);
  recent.set([base, ...recent().filter((e) => e !== base)].slice(0, 18));
  picking.set(false);
};

<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-start">
    <Popover open={picking()} onOpenChange={({ open }) => picking.set(open)}>
      <PopoverTrigger>
        <InputGroupButton size="icon-sm" variant="ghost" accessibilityLabel="Emoji">
          <Icon icon={Smile} size={16} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
        </InputGroupButton>
      </PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent placement="top" width={342} compact>
        <EmojiPanel
          class="h-[392px] w-full"
          recent={recent()}
          onSelect={({ emoji, base }) => put(emoji, base)}
        />
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  </InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput
    value={draft()}
    onChange={({ value }) => draft.set(value)}
    placeholder="Message"
  />
</InputGroup>;
```

The popover goes in the addon, where the smile goes: `PopoverContent` is what mounts the popover,
and it draws the trigger in its own place — a `PopoverContent` written outside the group leaves the
smile under the field. `placement="top"` puts the panel over the field, where a composer at the
bottom of a window has room; on a narrow frame give the panel a narrower `class` and the popover
the same `width`.

### Reactions [#reactions]

The counted chips are a row of pressables under the bubble: one tap adds yours or takes it back
off, and a count that reaches zero drops the chip. `BubbleReactions` draws a row of emoji alone —
its children are text, and the room it keeps is a line of it — so counted chips go in the
`MessageContent` below the bubble.

```tsx
type Reaction = { emoji: string; count: number; mine: boolean };

const reactions = signal<Reaction[]>([{ emoji: "🎉", count: 4, mine: false }]);

const react = (base: string) => {
  reactions.update((list) => {
    const found = list.find((r) => r.emoji === base);
    if (!found) return [...list, { emoji: base, count: 1, mine: true }];
    return list.flatMap((r) => {
      if (r.emoji !== base) return [r];
      if (r.mine) return r.count > 1 ? [{ ...r, count: r.count - 1, mine: false }] : [];
      return [{ ...r, count: r.count + 1, mine: true }];
    });
  });
};

<Message align="start">
  <MessageAvatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="muted">
      <BubbleContent>Ship it?</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 6, paddingLeft: 42 }}>
  {reactions().map((reaction) => (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityLabel={`${reaction.emoji} ${reaction.count}${reaction.mine ? ", yours" : ""}`}
      onPress={() => react(reaction.emoji)}
      style={{
        flexDirection: "row",
        alignItems: "center",
        gap: 4,
        height: 26,
        paddingHorizontal: 8,
        borderRadius: 13,
        borderWidth: 1,
        borderColor: reaction.mine ? alpha(colors.brand, 0.45) : colors.line,
        backgroundColor: reaction.mine ? alpha(colors.brand, 0.12) : colors.card,
      }}
    >
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14 }}>{reaction.emoji}</Text>
      <Text
        style={{
          fontSize: 12,
          fontWeight: 600,
          fontVariant: ["tabular-nums"],
          color: reaction.mine ? colors.brand : colors.mutedForeground,
        }}
      >
        {reaction.count}
      </Text>
    </Pressable>
  ))}
</View>;
```

A row of quick emoji beside the picker is the same pressables in a pill: six of them, a divider,
then a `Popover` whose trigger is a plus, with the same `EmojiPanel` inside it and `react` as its
`onSelect`.

## API [#api]

| Part           | Props                                                                                                                                                           | Description                                                  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `EmojiPanel`   | `onSelect` (required, `(e: { emoji: string; base: string })`), `onCancel`, `recent` (`string[]`, default `[]`), `fill`, `class`, `testID`, `accessibilityLabel` | The whole picker: tabs, search, skin tones, grid and preview |
| `EmojiHeading` | `group`                                                                                                                                                         | A group's heading                                            |
| `EmojiTabs`    | `group`, `groups`, `onPress`                                                                                                                                    | The group tabs                                               |
| `EmojiTones`   | `tone`, `onChange`                                                                                                                                              | The skin tone hand beside the search field                   |
| `EmojiPreview` | `entry`, `hint`                                                                                                                                                 | The emoji under the pointer, named                           |

`EmojiPanel` wraps [`nsh/base` EmojiPicker](https://nsh.dev/elements/emoji-picker) with gallery classes and chrome. Pass through any base picker prop via extending the shell later; today only the upstream panel props are supported.

Also exports `emojiGroups`, `emojiGroupLabels` and `emojiPickerClasses` for custom layouts.

# Empty (/dev/docs/components/empty)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add empty
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Inbox } from "lucide";

import {
  Empty,
  EMPTY_ICON,
  EmptyContent,
  EmptyDescription,
  EmptyHeader,
  EmptyMedia,
  EmptyTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/empty";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
import { colors } from "@/lib/ui/theme";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyMedia variant="icon">
      <Icon icon={Inbox} size={EMPTY_ICON} tint={colors.foreground} />
    </EmptyMedia>
    <EmptyTitle>No messages yet</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Messages you receive will show up here.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
</Empty>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build an `Empty`:

```text
Empty
├── EmptyHeader
│   ├── EmptyMedia
│   ├── EmptyTitle
│   └── EmptyDescription
└── EmptyContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### With what the reader can do [#with-what-the-reader-can-do]

`EmptyContent` holds the actions under the words: a button, a field, a link. The block takes the
room its parent leaves it (`flexGrow: 1`), so a list that ends in an empty state fills its pane.

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyMedia variant="icon">
      <Icon icon={Inbox} size={EMPTY_ICON} tint={colors.foreground} />
    </EmptyMedia>
    <EmptyTitle>No messages yet</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Start a conversation to see one.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyContent>
    <Button>New message</Button>
  </EmptyContent>
</Empty>
```

### The app's own art [#the-apps-own-art]

`variant="default"` is the media as the app draws it — an `Avatar`, an illustration, an `Icon`
drawn large — with no box around it. `variant="icon"` is the square of the muted fill with a
surface's corners, an icon of `EMPTY_ICON` (24 points) in it.

```tsx
<EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyMedia>
    <Icon icon={Search} size={32} tint={colors.faint} />
  </EmptyMedia>
  <EmptyTitle>Nothing matched that search</EmptyTitle>
  <EmptyDescription>Every field is required unless it is marked optional.</EmptyDescription>
</EmptyHeader>
```

### A block that says one thing [#a-block-that-says-one-thing]

The parts are optional: a line on its own is centered in the room the block has.

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyDescription>Nothing has been published to this space yet.</EmptyDescription>
</Empty>
```

### In the terminal [#in-the-terminal]

A terminal draws the block as its lines: no padding, one Cell row between the words and the
actions, the title and the description as plain text.

```tsx
<Empty>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyTitle>No messages yet</EmptyTitle>
  </EmptyHeader>
</Empty>
```

## API [#api]

| Part               | Props                                                               | Description                                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Empty`            | every `nsh` View prop; look `emptyLook().root()`                    | A centered block that takes the room it is given |
| `EmptyHeader`      | every `nsh` View prop; look `emptyLook().header()`                  | The media and the words under it                 |
| `EmptyMedia`       | `variant`; every `nsh` View prop; look `emptyLook().media(variant)` | The media's box                                  |
| `EmptyTitle`       | every `nsh` Text prop; look `emptyLook().title()`                   | The line that says there is nothing here         |
| `EmptyDescription` | every `nsh` Text prop; look `emptyLook().description()`             | The line under the title, a step quieter         |
| `EmptyContent`     | every `nsh` View prop; look `emptyLook().content()`                 | What the reader can do about it                  |

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through on `Empty`,
`EmptyHeader`, `EmptyMedia` and `EmptyContent`, and every prop of
[`nsh` Text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text) on `EmptyTitle` and `EmptyDescription`; `style` goes
over the look's on each.

| Prop      | Type                  | Default   |
| --------- | --------------------- | --------- |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "icon"` | `default` |

The block is a centered column padded 24, its header a step of 8 apart from its content, the words
and the actions no wider than 384 points. The title is medium at `body + 2` (15 points with a
pointer, 17 on a touch screen), the description the body's size in the muted ink, both centered.
`emptyLook()` is exported for a state the app lays out itself, and `EMPTY_ICON` is the size an
icon takes in the `icon` variant.

# Field (/dev/docs/components/field)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add field
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Field,
  FieldContent,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldGroup,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldLegend,
  FieldSeparator,
  FieldSet,
  FieldTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/field";
```

```tsx
<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend>Payment method</FieldLegend>
  <FieldDescription>All transactions are secure and encrypted.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldGroup>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>Name on card</FieldLabel>
      <Input placeholder="Evil Rabbit" />
    </Field>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>
```

`FieldSet` holds a legend and the fields under it; `FieldGroup` holds the fields themselves, 16
points apart. `Field` is one label and its control. A control that carries its own label (a
`Checkbox` with children, a `Switch` with children) needs no `Field`: put it in the group as it is.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `FieldSet`:

```text
FieldSet
├── FieldLegend
├── FieldDescription
└── FieldGroup
    ├── Field
    │   ├── FieldLabel
    │   ├── FieldContent
    │   │   ├── FieldTitle
    │   │   └── FieldDescription
    │   └── FieldError
    └── FieldSeparator
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Vertical and horizontal [#vertical-and-horizontal]

`orientation` defaults to `vertical`: the label over the control. `horizontal` puts them on one
row, the label as wide as its text and the control taking the rest.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Name on card</FieldLabel>
  <Input placeholder="Evil Rabbit" />
</Field>

<Field orientation="horizontal">
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <FieldContent>
    <Input invalid />
    <FieldError errors={[{ message: "Enter an email address like name@example.com." }]} />
  </FieldContent>
</Field>
```

`FieldContent` stacks a label and its description (or an input and its error) beside the control
of a horizontal field. A label inside `FieldContent` keeps the label's width rather than the
room left by the control, whatever the field's orientation.

A label is not associated with its control: NSH has no `<label for>`, so a screen reader hears the
control's own `accessibilityLabel`, then the `FieldLabel` as separate text. Give the control the
same words: `<Input accessibilityLabel="Email" />` beside `<FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>`. A
control that carries its own label (`<Checkbox>Hard disks</Checkbox>`) needs neither.

### Responsive [#responsive]

`orientation="responsive"` is `vertical` in a narrow window — a phone, or a narrow desktop
window, under 600 points — and `horizontal` above it (`narrowWindow`).

```tsx
<Field orientation="responsive">
  <FieldContent>
    <FieldTitle>Full name</FieldTitle>
    <FieldDescription>Provide your full name for identification.</FieldDescription>
  </FieldContent>
  <Input placeholder="Evil Rabbit" />
</Field>
```

### A group of choices [#a-group-of-choices]

A legend one step smaller over a group of checkboxes or switches: `variant="label"`.

```tsx
<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend variant="label">Show these items on the desktop</FieldLegend>
  <FieldDescription>Select the items you want to see there.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldGroup>
    <Checkbox>Hard disks</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox checked>External disks</Checkbox>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>
```

### Separators [#separators]

A `FieldSeparator` is a hairline between fields; with children it is a hairline broken by its word.

```tsx
<FieldSeparator />
<FieldSeparator>Billing address</FieldSeparator>
```

### Errors [#errors]

`FieldError` shows `errors`' messages — as many as there are, each distinct message once — or its
`children` when they say more. With neither it draws nothing.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <Input value={email()} onChange={({ value }) => email.set(value)} invalid={!valid()} />
  <FieldError errors={[{ message: "Enter an email address like name@example.com." }]} />
</Field>
```

An error is announced where the platform does it by itself. `FieldError` is a view with
`role="alert"` (macOS and the web read it when it appears) and TalkBack's live region
(`accessibilityLiveRegion: "assertive"` on Android). iOS has no live region: `UIAccessibility`'s
announcement is the app's call, and NSH does not expose it — put the message in the control's
`accessibilityHint` there as well if it must be heard the moment it appears. Mark the control
invalid, not just the field: pass `invalid` to the control (an `Input`, a `Select`'s trigger),
because `role="alert"` tells a reader that something is wrong, not which field.

## API [#api]

| Part               | Props                                                                          | Description                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FieldSet`         | every view prop                                                                | `role="group"`, named by its legend                       |
| `FieldLegend`      | `variant`: `"legend"` (default) or `"label"`; every text prop                  | The set's legend, one step smaller as a label             |
| `FieldGroup`       | every view prop                                                                | A column of fields, 16 points apart                       |
| `Field`            | `orientation`: `"vertical"`, `"horizontal"` or `"responsive"`; every view prop | One label and its control, `role="group"`                 |
| `FieldContent`     | every view prop                                                                | A column that takes the room left                         |
| `FieldLabel`       | every text prop                                                                | The control's visible name, in a row, as wide as its text |
| `FieldTitle`       | every text prop                                                                | A label over a group of choices                           |
| `FieldDescription` | every text prop                                                                | The word under the label (`density.note`, muted)          |
| `FieldSeparator`   | `children`: the word between the hairlines; every view prop                    | A hairline between fields                                 |
| `FieldError`       | `errors`, `role="alert"`; every view prop                                      | The messages, read out where the platform does it         |

Every view prop passes through the parts drawn as views, and every text prop the parts drawn as
texts. `style` goes over the look's, so a width or a gap on a part wins.

`FieldError`'s `errors` is `Array<{ message?: string } | undefined>`, as a form library reports them
(a field may collect several). `fieldFamilyLook()` is exported for a field the app draws itself —
the same look without the parts; it is not `fieldLook()`, which is the input's well.

# Hover Card (/dev/docs/components/hover-card)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add hover-card
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/ui/hover-card";
```

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger>@nsh</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent width={240}>
    <Text>Native Shell</Text>
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `HoverCard`:

```text
HoverCard
├── HoverCardTrigger
└── HoverCardContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Compact [#compact]

A line or two: 12 points of padding and 4 between rows.

```tsx
<HoverCardContent compact>A short note</HoverCardContent>
```

### Placement and delays [#placement-and-delays]

The base defaults are 600 ms before it opens and 300 ms before it closes.

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger>@nsh</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent placement="top" offset={8} openDelay={200} closeDelay={500}>
    …
  </HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

### A trigger of your own, or a disabled one [#a-trigger-of-your-own-or-a-disabled-one]

A string child is a `Button` (`variant`, `secondary` by default). A single element child is
the trigger itself: its look, `testID`, name and own press and hover styles stay, and
`nsh/base` adds the open state (`expandedStyle`) to it. `variant` and `disabled` shape a
string child; an element brings its own `disabled`, and the root's `disabled` still keeps
the card closed.

```tsx
<HoverCardTrigger variant="ghost">@nsh</HoverCardTrigger>
<HoverCardTrigger disabled>@nsh</HoverCardTrigger>
<HoverCardTrigger>
  <Text class="underline">@nsh</Text>
</HoverCardTrigger>
```

## API [#api]

| Part               | Props                                                                                  | Description                                       |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `HoverCard`        | `open` / `defaultOpen`, `openDelay`, `closeDelay`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpen`, `onClose` | Open state, the delays and the trigger slot       |
| `HoverCardTrigger` | `children`, `variant` (a string child's `Button`), `disabled`, `style`                 | What the card previews; an element is the trigger |
| `HoverCardContent` | `compact`, `width`, and base's `placement`, `align`, `offset`, `margin`                | The preview card                                  |

The root owns the open flag and the two delays (`openDelay`, 600 ms by default; `closeDelay`, 300):
`Infinity` in either makes the card wait for the app, which is how a card a press opens keeps still
under the pointer. `HoverCardContent` mounts
[`nsh/base` HoverCard](https://nsh.dev/elements/hover-card) and every base prop passes through
except the open state, the delays and the lifecycle callbacks, which the root owns. Its children
come in on a `PopIn` with `popoverLook`.

# ImageViewer (/dev/docs/components/image-viewer)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add image-viewer
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { ImageViewer } from "@/components/ui/image-viewer";
```

```tsx
const image = signal<ImageViewerImage | null>(null);

<ImageViewer image={image()} onClose={() => image.set(null)} />;
```

The viewer is open while `image` is set; `onClose` is where it asks to close (the close button, Escape, the back button, a press on the ground, a swipe down), so set `image` back to `null` there. A pinch zooms to 4×, a double tap or click to 2.5× at the point, a drag pans the zoomed image, and at 1× a drag down closes it. The `alt` text is the caption and the image's name for screen readers.

## Examples [#examples]

### An image viewer [#an-image-viewer]

A row of photographs, each a [`Pressable`](./pressable) that sets the image; one viewer serves them all.

```tsx
const image = signal<ImageViewerImage | null>(null);

<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
  <Each of={photos}>
    {(photo) => (
      <Pressable
        accessibilityLabel={photo().alt}
        onPress={() => image.set({ src: photo().large, alt: photo().alt })}
      >
        <Image src={photo().thumbnail} style={{ width: "100%", height: 96, objectFit: "cover" }} />
      </Pressable>
    )}
  </Each>
</View>
<ImageViewer image={image()} onClose={() => image.set(null)} />;
```

### From a text view [#from-a-text-view]

[`TextView`](./text-view) reports the image that was pressed (`onImagePress`) in the shape the viewer takes; see **Images that open** there.

## API [#api]

`ImageViewer` is a [`Dialog`](./dialog) as a page (`dialogPage`) with its body given whole (`scroll={false}`), so every prop of `DialogContent` passes through but `width`, `scroll` and `children`; `style` goes over the page's, and `animation` defaults to `fade`. Gestures are [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view)'s `pinch` and `pan`; behavior and accessibility are [`nsh/base` Dialog](https://nsh.dev/elements/dialog)'s.

| Part          | Props                                                                     | Description                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ImageViewer` | `image`: `{ src: string; alt?: string } \| null`; `onClose`: `() => void` | The viewer, open while `image` is set. The image stays while the dialog fades out. |

`imageViewerLook()` is exported for a viewer the app draws itself: its parts as the styles they wear (`page`, `ground`, `caption`, `captionText`, `closeCorner`, `close`, `closeHover`).

There are no `ImageViewerClose` or `ImageViewerCaption` parts. The close button is always there and the caption is always the `alt`, so a part would only be a place to put what the viewer already draws; a viewer with other chrome draws it from `imageViewerLook()`. A gallery of several images in one viewer is the app's: set `image` to the next one.

The ink is `on-media` and the ground is the theme's `media`, the pair that stays dark in either appearance and in every theme; the caption strip and the close chip carry a wash of that ink so they read over any photograph.

# InputGroup (/dev/docs/components/input-group)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add input-group
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { InputGroup, InputGroupInput } from "@/components/ui/input-group";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="Search" accessibilityLabel="Search" />
</InputGroup>
```

The group draws the field: its fill, its edge and, while the input inside has the keys, the focus edge and its ring. The input inside draws none of that, so a group has one frame, not two.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build an `InputGroup`:

```text
InputGroup
├── InputGroupInput
├── InputGroupTextarea
└── InputGroupAddon
    ├── InputGroupText
    └── InputGroupButton
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Invalid and disabled [#invalid-and-disabled]

```tsx
<InputGroup invalid>
  <InputGroupInput value={email()} placeholder="you@example.com" />
</InputGroup>
<InputGroup disabled>
  <InputGroupInput value="ada@example.com" />
</InputGroup>
```

A disabled group disables what it holds and dims it.

### An addon before and after the input [#an-addon-before-and-after-the-input]

`InputGroupAddon` holds an icon, a word or a button at the start or at the end of the group's line (`align`: `inline-start`, `inline-end`). A press on an addon puts the keys in the input, so the magnifier works as part of the field; a press on a button in it is the button's alone.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-start">
    <InputGroupText>
      <Icon icon={Search} size={16} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
    </InputGroupText>
  </InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupInput
    value={query()}
    onChange={({ value }) => query.set(value)}
    placeholder="Search plugins"
  />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupButton
      size="icon-xs"
      accessibilityLabel="Clear"
      disabled={!query()}
      onPress={() => query.set("")}
    >
      <Icon icon={CircleX} {...buttonGlyph("ghost", { size: "sm" })} />
    </InputGroupButton>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### A unit after the control [#a-unit-after-the-control]

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput
    value={amount()}
    onChange={({ value }) => amount.set(value)}
    placeholder="0.00"
  />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupText>USD</InputGroupText>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### A radius of your own [#a-radius-of-your-own]

Write the radius and the padding on the group. The focus ring is drawn on the group's edge, so it follows the radius: a composer on 22 points lights a 22-point ring, with the input and its button inside it.

```tsx
<InputGroup style={{ borderRadius: 22, padding: 6 }}>
  <InputGroupTextarea
    value={message()}
    onChange={({ value }) => message.set(value)}
    placeholder="Ask anything"
  />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupButton size="icon-sm" variant="default" accessibilityLabel="Send" onPress={send}>
      <Icon icon={Send} {...buttonGlyph("default")} />
    </InputGroupButton>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Addons over and under the control [#addons-over-and-under-the-control]

`block-start` and `block-end` take a line of their own, above or below the input's: a word over a note, a count under it.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupAddon align="block-start">
    <InputGroupText>Release note</InputGroupText>
  </InputGroupAddon>
  <InputGroupTextarea value={note()} onChange={({ value }) => note.set(value)} />
  <InputGroupAddon align="block-end">
    <InputGroupText>{`${note().length} / 200`}</InputGroupText>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Buttons in a group [#buttons-in-a-group]

`InputGroupButton` sizes a button inside a group: `xs` is a `sm` button (24 points high with a
pointer), `sm` a `default` one (28), and `icon-xs` / `icon-sm` a square of that height. `variant`
is a button's, `ghost` unless set.

```tsx
<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="Filter the list" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupButton size="xs" accessibilityLabel="Apply the filter">
      <Icon icon={Search} {...buttonGlyph("ghost", { size: "sm" })} />
    </InputGroupButton>
    <InputGroupButton size="sm" accessibilityLabel="Clear the filter">
      <Icon icon={X} {...buttonGlyph("ghost", { size: "default" })} />
    </InputGroupButton>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>
```

### A search field [#a-search-field]

A magnifier before the control, the work after it: a spinner while the query settles, then a button
that clears it. Search on what the field settles on, not on every key — 300 ms after the last one
is enough, and the spinner says the search is under way. Put the matches under the field, with the
letters that matched in the accent, so the answer reads as the field's.

```tsx
const query = signal("");
const settled = signal("");
const pending = signal(false);
let wait: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;

const search = (value: string) => {
  query.set(value);
  if (wait !== undefined) clearTimeout(wait);
  if (value.trim() === "") {
    pending.set(false);
    settled.set("");
    return;
  }
  pending.set(true);
  wait = setTimeout(() => {
    settled.set(value);
    pending.set(false);
  }, 300);
};
cleanup(() => {
  if (wait !== undefined) clearTimeout(wait);
});

<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <InputGroup>
    <InputGroupAddon align="inline-start">
      <InputGroupText>
        <Icon icon={Search} size={16} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
      </InputGroupText>
    </InputGroupAddon>
    <InputGroupInput
      value={query()}
      onChange={({ value }) => search(value)}
      placeholder="Search cities"
      returnKeyType="search"
      autoCapitalize="none"
    />
    <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
      {pending() ? <Spinner side={14} tint={colors.faint} /> : null}
      {query().length > 0 ? (
        <InputGroupButton
          size="icon-xs"
          accessibilityLabel="Clear the search"
          onPress={() => search("")}
        >
          <Icon icon={CircleX} {...buttonGlyph("ghost", { size: "sm" })} />
        </InputGroupButton>
      ) : null}
    </InputGroupAddon>
  </InputGroup>
  {/* The panel of matches is the app's, not the group's: Pressable rows, or a List. */}
  <View style={{ ...sectionSurface(), overflow: "hidden" }}>
    <Each of={matches()}>
      {(city) => <Pressable onPress={() => search(city().name)}>{city().name}</Pressable>}
    </Each>
  </View>
</View>;
```

### A message composer [#a-message-composer]

The composer of a chat: a `block-end` addon under the textarea holds a round button that opens
what can be added, the key hint, and the send button. Give the group the composer's radius and
padding (`borderRadius: 22`, `padding: 6`), and let the textarea grow to five lines with
`grownFieldHeight` — an `Input` takes the lines' height from `onContentSizeChange`. Return sends
and Shift-Return breaks the line under a keyboard (`submitBehavior="submit"` on desktop); on a
touch screen Return breaks the line, and the button sends.

```tsx
const message = signal("");
const grown = signal(0);
const replying = signal(false);
const attaching = signal(false);

<InputGroup style={{ borderRadius: 22, padding: 6 }}>
  <InputGroupTextarea
    value={message()}
    onChange={({ value }) => message.set(value)}
    onContentSizeChange={({ size }) => grown.set(size.height)}
    style={grown() > 0 ? { height: grownFieldHeight(grown(), 5) } : undefined}
    placeholder="Ask anything"
    submitBehavior={desktop ? "submit" : "newline"}
    onSubmit={send}
  />
  <InputGroupAddon align="block-end" style={{ paddingHorizontal: 0, paddingBottom: 0, gap: 8 }}>
    <RoundButton
      variant="secondary"
      size="sm"
      accessibilityLabel="Add an attachment"
      style={attaching() ? { transform: "rotate(45deg)" } : undefined}
    >
      <Icon icon={Plus} {...roundButtonGlyph("secondary", { size: "sm" })} />
    </RoundButton>
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }} />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, color: colors.faint }}>
      {desktop ? "Return sends · Shift-Return breaks the line" : "Return breaks the line"}
    </Text>
    {replying() ? (
      <RoundButton size="sm" accessibilityLabel="Stop the reply" onPress={stop}>
        <Icon icon={Square} {...roundButtonGlyph("default", { size: "sm" })} />
      </RoundButton>
    ) : (
      <RoundButton
        size="sm"
        accessibilityLabel="Send"
        disabled={message().trim().length === 0}
        onPress={send}
      >
        <Icon icon={Send} {...roundButtonGlyph("default", { size: "sm" })} />
      </RoundButton>
    )}
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>;
```

While a reply streams, the send button becomes a stop: the same press that sent the message stops
the answer. The plus turns a quarter as the menu under it opens, so the same button shows it can be
closed.

### When to use a group, and when an `Input` [#when-to-use-a-group-and-when-an-input]

A frame of your own around an input is a group. Do not wrap a `variant="ghost"` `Input` in a `View` with a border: the ghost input keeps its own focus edge and ring, so the frame ends up with a second edge inside it that does not follow the frame's radius.

```tsx
{
  /* Not this: the ghost input draws its own focus edge inside your frame. */
}
<View style={{ borderRadius: 22, padding: 6, borderWidth: 1 }}>
  <Input variant="ghost" placeholder="Search" />
</View>;

{
  /* This: the group draws the frame, and the input draws nothing. */
}
<InputGroup style={{ borderRadius: 22, padding: 6 }}>
  <InputGroupInput placeholder="Search" />
</InputGroup>;
```

### Focus from code [#focus-from-code]

A ref on the control focuses it from code — a shortcut, a request to focus a draft. The ref is the control's, not the group's.

```tsx
let search: InputRef | undefined;

<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput ref={search} placeholder="Search" />
</InputGroup>
<Button onPress={() => search?.focus()}>Find</Button>
```

### The look alone [#the-look-alone]

`inputGroupLook` is the frame's props and `inputGroupControlLook` the control's, for a `nsh/base` control of your own; `inputGroupAddonLook` and `inputGroupTextLook` are the addon's and its text's. This is what the reference page draws, and what `InputGroup` wraps.

```tsx
<View {...inputGroupLook({ invalid: true, style: { borderRadius: 22, padding: 6 } })}>
  <BaseInput {...inputGroupControlLook()} placeholder="Search" />
</View>
```

## API [#api]

| Part                 | Props                                                                                                                                                                         | Description                                    |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `InputGroup`         | `invalid`; every `View` prop; `class`, `style` and `disabledStyle` over the look's                                                                                            | The field's frame around its parts             |
| `InputGroupAddon`    | `align`: `"inline-start" \| "inline-end" \| "block-start" \| "block-end"` (default `"inline-start"`); every `View` prop                                                       | An icon, a word or a button beside the control |
| `InputGroupText`     | `children`; every `View` prop                                                                                                                                                 | A word or an icon in the field's type          |
| `InputGroupButton`   | `size`: `"xs" \| "sm" \| "icon-xs" \| "icon-sm"` (default `"xs"`), `variant`: `"default" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "destructive"` (default `"ghost"`); every `Button` prop | A button sized for a group                     |
| `InputGroupInput`    | every `nsh/base` Input prop, `ref` included                                                                                                                                   | The group's single-line control                |
| `InputGroupTextarea` | every `nsh/base` Input prop, `ref` included                                                                                                                                   | The group's multiline control                  |

`InputGroup` is a view: every `View` prop passes through. `class`, `style` and `disabledStyle` go over its look's.

| Prop      | Type        | Default | What it does                                                         |
| --------- | ----------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid` | `boolean`   |         | Edged in the danger tone, its focus edge too.                        |
| `style`   | `ViewStyle` |         | Over the look's: the radius, the padding and the width of the group. |

`InputGroupInput` and `InputGroupTextarea` take every prop of [`nsh/base` Input](https://nsh.dev/elements/input), `ref` included: `value`, `onChange`, `placeholder`, `keyboardType`, `maxLength`, `readonly`, `disabled` and the rest. `InputGroupTextarea` is the multiline one. Their `style` goes over the look's. A `ref` is the control's `InputRef`: `ref.focus()` puts the keys in it from code (a shortcut, a request to focus a draft).

# Input (/dev/docs/components/input)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add input
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";
```

```tsx
<Input value={name()} onChange={({ value }) => name.set(value)} placeholder="Ada Lovelace" />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Variant [#variant]

No fill and no edge until the keys are in it, with the text, the placeholder and the focus ring as they are: a search field, a title that turns into a field. Disabled still dims, and invalid still shows the danger edge.

```tsx
<Input variant="ghost" placeholder="Search" accessibilityLabel="Search" />
<Input variant="ghost" value="Untitled note" style={{ fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" }} />
```

A ghost input is the field itself: it keeps its own focus edge and ring, so it is not what a frame you draw around it wants. For an input in a frame of your own — a search field with a magnifier, a composer with a send button — use [`InputGroup`](./input-group) instead: the group draws the frame and the input in it draws nothing, so the focus ring follows the group's radius.

### Invalid [#invalid]

```tsx
<Input invalid value={email()} />
```

### Read-only and disabled [#read-only-and-disabled]

```tsx
<Input value="Ada" readonly />
<Input value="Ada" disabled />
```

### Multiline [#multiline]

`multiline` makes the same field several lines: the content starts at the top, the box is at least one line tall, and Return writes a line break.

```tsx
<Input multiline value={notes()} onChange={({ value }) => notes.set(value)} />
```

`invalid`, `readonly` and `disabled` are the single-line field's, and a multiline one takes them the same way. A composer that sends on Return takes `submitBehavior="submit"` and keeps Shift + Return for a break:

```tsx
<Input multiline submitBehavior="submit" onSubmit={() => send()} />
```

The box grows only as the app sizes it: [`nsh/base`'s multi-line input](https://nsh.dev/elements/input) reports the size of its text (`onContentSizeChange`) rather than sizing itself to it, and the look keeps only a least height — one line's, so a multiline field sits as tall as a one-line input until the app says otherwise. Keep the reported height plus the room the look keeps inside the box:

```tsx
import { signal } from "nsh";

import { fieldText, Input } from "@/components/ui/input";

const note = signal("");
const content = signal(0);
/** The room inside the box: its two edges and the padding above and below. */
const room = () => {
  const text = fieldText({ multiline: true });
  return (text.paddingTop as number) + (text.paddingBottom as number) + 2;
};

<Input
  multiline
  value={note()}
  onChange={({ value }) => note.set(value)}
  onContentSizeChange={({ size }) => content.set(size.height)}
  style={{ height: content() === 0 ? undefined : content() + room() }}
/>;
```

A least height of your own is how the box starts taller than one line, since `style` goes over the look's — 64 points:

```tsx
<Input multiline value={notes()} style={{ minHeight: 64 }} />
```

### A password with a strength meter [#a-password-with-a-strength-meter]

A password field that says what it asks for and how far the reader has got: four segments, one for
each rule the password meets, the word for the score, and the rules under the field — a dot until
it is met, a tick on the tone that says it is. Score the field as it is typed, and score nothing as
nothing: an empty field asks for a password rather than calling it weak.

```tsx
const PASSWORD_RULES = [
  { label: "8 or more characters", test: (value: string) => value.length >= 8 },
  {
    label: "Upper and lower case",
    test: (value: string) => /[a-z]/.test(value) && /[A-Z]/.test(value),
  },
  { label: "A number", test: (value: string) => /\d/.test(value) },
  { label: "A symbol", test: (value: string) => /[^\w\s]/.test(value) },
];
const WORDS = ["Empty", "Weak", "Fair", "Good", "Strong"];

const score = (value: string) =>
  value === "" ? 0 : PASSWORD_RULES.filter((rule) => rule.test(value)).length;
const tones = [colors.faint, colors.destructive, colors.warn, colors.info, colors.up];

const strength = score(password());

<View style={{ gap: 6 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, color: colors.mutedForeground }}>Password</Text>
  <Input masked value={password()} onChange={({ value }) => password.set(value)} />
  <View style={{ gap: 8, paddingTop: 2 }}>
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
      <View style={{ flex: 1, flexDirection: "row", gap: 4 }}>
        <Each of={[0, 1, 2, 3]}>
          {(step) => (
            <View
              style={{
                flex: 1,
                height: 6,
                borderRadius: 3,
                backgroundColor:
                  step() < strength ? tones[strength] : alpha(colors.foreground, 0.1),
              }}
            />
          )}
        </Each>
      </View>
      <Text
        style={{
          width: 52,
          textAlign: "right",
          fontSize: 13,
          fontWeight: "500",
          color: tones[strength],
        }}
      >
        {WORDS[strength]}
      </Text>
    </View>
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", columnGap: 14, rowGap: 6 }}>
      <Each of={PASSWORD_RULES}>
        {(rule) => {
          const met = rule().test(password());
          return (
            <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 5, minWidth: 140 }}>
              {met ? (
                <Icon icon={Check} size={12} tint={colors.up} />
              ) : (
                <View
                  style={{
                    width: 4,
                    height: 4,
                    borderRadius: 2,
                    backgroundColor: colors.faint,
                  }}
                />
              )}
              <Text
                style={{ fontSize: 12, color: met ? colors.foreground : colors.mutedForeground }}
              >
                {rule().label}
              </Text>
            </View>
          );
        }}
      </Each>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>;
```

The segments keep the field's own width — a bar of four parts, each a share of it — and the word
keeps a column at the end, so the meter does not reflow as the word changes from `Empty` to
`Strong`.

### The look alone [#the-look-alone]

```tsx
<Input {...inputLook({ invalid: true })} />
<Input {...inputLook({ variant: "ghost" })} />
```

## API [#api]

| Part    | Props                                                                                                                                                                                    | Description                                                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Input` | `variant`: `"default" \| "ghost"` (default `"default"`), `invalid`: `boolean`, `multiline`: `boolean`; every `nsh/base` Input prop; `class`, `style` and `disabledStyle` over the look's | A text field — `default` or `ghost`, single-line or multiline |

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Input](https://nsh.dev/elements/input) passes through. `class`, `style` and `disabledStyle` go over the look's. Focus and hover edges are classes on the look.

| Prop        | Type                | Default     | What it does                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `InputVariant`      | `"default"` | `ghost` draws no fill and no edge until the keys are in it; the text, the placeholder and the focus ring stay.             |
| `invalid`   | `boolean`           |             | Edged in the danger tone, its focus edge too.                                                                              |
| `multiline` | `boolean`           | `false`     | Several lines: the content starts at the top, the box is at least one line tall, and Return writes a line break.           |
| `grow`      | `boolean \| number` |             | Multiline only. `true` grows with the text up to five lines; a number is that cap. No transition. A `style` `height` wins. |
| `reject`    | `number`            |             | Shakes the field each time this becomes a new number. `invalid` only recolours the edge. Less motion plays nothing.        |

# Item (/dev/docs/components/item)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add item
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Bell } from "lucide";

import {
  Item,
  ItemActions,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemFooter,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemHeader,
  ItemMedia,
  ItemSeparator,
  ItemTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/item";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
import { colors } from "@/lib/ui/theme";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<ItemGroup>
  <Item>
    <ItemMedia variant="icon">
      <Icon icon={Bell} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
    </ItemMedia>
    <ItemContent>
      <ItemTitle>New comment</ItemTitle>
      <ItemDescription>Mira replied to your post in #design.</ItemDescription>
    </ItemContent>
    <ItemActions>
      <Button size="sm">Open</Button>
    </ItemActions>
  </Item>
  <ItemSeparator />
  <Item>…</Item>
</ItemGroup>
```

`ItemGroup` is a `role="list"` column of rows, `density.gap` apart; `ItemSeparator` is the hairline
between them. `Item` is the row: `ItemMedia` before its content, `ItemContent` for the title and
the note, `ItemActions` for its controls. `ItemHeader` and `ItemFooter` are lines across the whole
row — a header above the content, a footer under it.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build an `Item`:

```text
ItemGroup
├── Item
│   ├── ItemHeader
│   ├── ItemMedia
│   ├── ItemContent
│   │   ├── ItemTitle
│   │   └── ItemDescription
│   ├── ItemActions
│   └── ItemFooter
└── ItemSeparator
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Variant [#variant]

`default` draws no surface, for rows split by a separator. `outline` edges the row, for one that
stands alone. `muted` puts it on a muted fill (`token("muted")`, shadcn's `bg-muted`): a well
that reads on a card and on the page, in either appearance, and is still lighter than an edge.

```tsx
<Item variant="outline">
  <ItemHeader>
    <ItemTitle>Outline</ItemTitle>
    <Badge variant="outline">variant</Badge>
  </ItemHeader>
  <ItemContent>
    <ItemDescription>A hairline edge, for a row that stands alone.</ItemDescription>
  </ItemContent>
  <ItemFooter>
    <ItemDescription>Updated 2 hours ago</ItemDescription>
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">
      Details
    </Button>
  </ItemFooter>
</Item>
```

### Size [#size]

`size="default"` has room for a title, a note and a control; `size="sm"` takes four points off each
side for a single line.

```tsx
<Item size="sm">
  <ItemContent>
    <ItemTitle>Small</ItemTitle>
    <ItemDescription>One line tighter: a title and a note.</ItemDescription>
  </ItemContent>
  <ItemActions>
    <Badge variant="outline">size</Badge>
  </ItemActions>
</Item>
```

### Media [#media]

`ItemMedia` holds what comes before the content: `default` the app's own (an avatar), `icon` a
square tile with a surface's edge for an icon, `image` a square frame that clips what is put in it.
An `Avatar` names its person; an `Icon` is a canvas a reader does not stop at, so the title must
say what the icon means.

```tsx
<ItemMedia>
  <Avatar name="Mira Lund" style={{ width: 36, height: 36 }} />
</ItemMedia>
<ItemMedia variant="icon">
  <Icon icon={Bell} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
</ItemMedia>
<ItemMedia variant="image">
  <Image source={cover} style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }} />
</ItemMedia>
```

### A row that takes presses [#a-row-that-takes-presses]

An `Item` is layout only: it draws a row and takes no presses, so the container decides what a row
does. For a row that is a control — hover fill, keyboard focus, disabled — use the same content on
`listRow` instead, or wrap it in a view with `onPress` and `role="button"`. `ItemGroup` is
`role="list"`, but NSH has no `listitem` role, so an `Item` is a plain view and a reader moves
through its text element by element: when the rows can be pressed, mark the pressable view
`role="button"` and give it an `accessibilityLabel` that says the whole row (or use `listRow`,
which does).

```tsx
<View role="button" onPress={() => open(item)} {...listRow()}>
  <ItemMedia variant="icon">
    <Icon icon={Bell} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
  </ItemMedia>
  <ItemContent>
    <ItemTitle>{item.title}</ItemTitle>
    <ItemDescription>{item.note}</ItemDescription>
  </ItemContent>
</View>
```

### A long list [#a-long-list]

Contacts as `ItemGroup` rows inside a `List` (`nsh`'s virtualized list), with a heading per letter that sticks to the top until the next one pushes it out. Rows are made as they scroll in, so the list can be as long as the data. `stickyHeaderIndices` names the heading rows; a heading needs an opaque background (the surface's own), or the rows show through it while it sticks.

```tsx
const rows: Row[] = [];
const headings: number[] = [];
for (const letter of letters) {
  headings.push(rows.length);
  rows.push({ heading: letter, count: byLetter[letter].length });
  rows.push(...byLetter[letter]);
}

<ItemGroup style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <List each={rows} stickyHeaderIndices={headings} estimatedItemSize={60} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
    {(row) => (
      <If when={"heading" in row()} else={<ContactItem contact={row() as Contact} />}>
        <Heading heading={row() as Heading} />
      </If>
    )}
  </List>
</ItemGroup>;

function ContactItem(props: { contact: Contact }) {
  return (
    <Item>
      <ItemMedia>
        <Avatar name={props.contact.name} style={{ width: 36, height: 36 }} />
      </ItemMedia>
      <ItemContent>
        <ItemTitle>{props.contact.name}</ItemTitle>
        <ItemDescription>{props.contact.note}</ItemDescription>
      </ItemContent>
    </Item>
  );
}
```

The heading is the app's: a row of the letter and its count on `colors.card`, 34 points tall. To pull the list down to reload it, put a [`RefreshIndicator`](./refresh-indicator) over it.

## API [#api]

| Part              | Props                                                                           | Description                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ItemGroup`       | every view prop                                                                 | `role="list"`, a column `density.gap` apart                                             |
| `ItemSeparator`   | every view prop                                                                 | A hairline, 4 points above and below                                                    |
| `Item`            | `variant`: `"default"`, `"outline"` or `"muted"`; `size`: `"default"` or `"sm"` | The row                                                                                 |
| `ItemMedia`       | `variant`: `"default"`, `"icon"` or `"image"`                                   | What sits before the content                                                            |
| `ItemContent`     | every view prop                                                                 | A column that takes the room the row leaves                                             |
| `ItemTitle`       | every text prop                                                                 | The label's size, medium, in the text colour                                            |
| `ItemDescription` | every text prop                                                                 | A step quieter, muted, two lines (`numberOfLines: 2`); a reader hears the text it shows |
| `ItemActions`     | every view prop                                                                 | A row, 8 points apart                                                                   |
| `ItemHeader`      | every view prop                                                                 | A line across the row, above the content                                                |
| `ItemFooter`      | every view prop                                                                 | A line across the row, under the content                                                |

Every view prop passes through the parts drawn as views, and every text prop the parts drawn as
texts. `style` goes over the look's.

An icon's tile is `controlSize.control + 12` square and an image's frame `controlSize.row - 8`,
both of the theme's control corners, so both grow on a touch screen. `itemLook()` is exported for a
row the app draws itself: the same look without the parts. `muted`'s fill is the theme's `muted`
token (`token("muted")`); `default` and `outline` draw what they always did.

# Kbd (/dev/docs/components/kbd)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add kbd
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/ui/kbd";
```

```tsx
<Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Kbd`:

```text
Kbd

KbdGroup
├── Kbd
└── Kbd
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A group of keys [#a-group-of-keys]

`KbdGroup` puts keys side by side, a small gap apart; `Kbd` is one cap — a modifier, a letter, a
word (`Esc`, `Ctrl`).

```tsx
<KbdGroup>
  <Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
  <Kbd>⇧</Kbd>
  <Kbd>⌥</Kbd>
  <Kbd>⌃</Kbd>
</KbdGroup>
```

### In a sentence [#in-a-sentence]

A cap is a view, not a span of a paragraph: in running text the sentence is a row of `Text` and
`KbdGroup`, wrapping together.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 6 }}>
  <Text>Press</Text>
  <KbdGroup>
    <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
    <Kbd>B</Kbd>
  </KbdGroup>
  <Text>to open the sidebar.</Text>
</View>
```

### Beside a button's label [#beside-a-buttons-label]

A key cap in a button says what its shortcut is; the label is the button's own type
(`buttonLabel`), the caps are the keys.

```tsx
<Button variant="secondary">
  <Text style={buttonLabel("secondary")}>Search</Text>
  <KbdGroup>
    <Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
    <Kbd>K</Kbd>
  </KbdGroup>
</Button>
```

### The terminal [#the-terminal]

A terminal draws no cap: a key is its name in the monospaced face, one Cell row high, with no fill
and no edge.

```tsx
<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

## API [#api]

| Part       | Props                                                                            | Description         |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `Kbd`      | `children`: `string \| JSX.Element`; every `nsh` View prop; look `kbdLook().kbd` | A key of a shortcut |
| `KbdGroup` | every `nsh` View prop; look `kbdLook().group`                                    | Keys side by side   |

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through on both parts (`style`, `accessibilityLabel`, …); `style` goes over the look's.

| Prop       | Type                    | Default |
| ---------- | ----------------------- | ------- |
| `children` | `string \| JSX.Element` |         |

A `Kbd` is one line high with a minimum width (20 points with a pointer, one Cell row in the
terminal), a hairline edge and the `muted` fill; its name is small type in the muted ink. There is
no axis. `kbdLook()` is exported — `kbd`, `text` and `group` — for a cap or a row the app draws
itself.

# Label (/dev/docs/components/label)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add label
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Label } from "@/components/ui/label";
```

```tsx
<Label>Accept terms and conditions</Label>
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Disabled [#disabled]

A label beside a control that cannot be used dims to half. Set `disabled` where the control's own
`disabled` is set.

```tsx
<Checkbox disabled accessibilityLabel="Weekly digest" />
<Label disabled>Weekly digest</Label>
```

### Beside a choice [#beside-a-choice]

A label is a row, so an icon or a switch can sit before its text; a control beside it is the
caller's own view, a gap of the caller's `style` apart.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Checkbox accessibilityLabel="Accept terms and conditions" />
  <Label>Accept terms and conditions</Label>
</View>
```

The label does not press the control: nsh has no `for` to hang the pair on. A row that toggles its
control is a `listRow` of the app's, as the `Checkbox` page shows.

### Over a group [#over-a-group]

The caption of a set of choices, a column's first line.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 10 }}>
  <Label>Notify me about</Label>
  <Checkbox accessibilityLabel="Comments">Comments on my posts</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox accessibilityLabel="Mentions">Mentions of my name</Checkbox>
</View>
```

### Naming the control [#naming-the-control]

This `Label` is the visible name, and nothing more: it names nothing for a screen reader. nsh has
no `htmlFor` and no `labelledBy`, so the control's own `accessibilityLabel` is its name — the same
words, said twice:

```tsx
<Checkbox accessibilityLabel="Accept terms and conditions" />
<Label>Accept terms and conditions</Label>
```

`lib/ui/as-text.tsx` compiles into the app beside it and is a different thing: a `Label` draws
type, while a control's name for screen readers is its own `accessibilityLabel`, or the text it
draws — the string child `AsText` hands to a `Text`.

## API [#api]

| Part    | Props                                                                                                                        | Description                   |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `Label` | `disabled`: `boolean` (default `false`), `children`: `string \| JSX.Element`; every `nsh` View prop; `style` over the look's | The visible name of a control |

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through (`style`, `role`, …); `style` goes over the look's.

| Prop       | Type                    | Default |
| ---------- | ----------------------- | ------- |
| `disabled` | `boolean`               | `false` |
| `children` | `string \| JSX.Element` |         |

There is no other axis: the text is `controlSize.label` (14 points with a pointer, 15 on a touch
screen) and medium, in the theme's text color, a row with a gap of 8. `labelLook({ disabled })` is
exported — `root` and `text` — for a label the app draws itself.

# Link (/dev/docs/components/link)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add link
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Link } from "@/components/ui/link";
```

```tsx
<Link href="https://nsh.dev">Native Shell</Link>
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Quiet [#quiet]

A quiet link sits in a footer: muted, with no resting underline.

```tsx
<Link href="#docs" quiet>
  Documentation
</Link>
```

### Current [#current]

The page a link names is the one shown.

```tsx
<Link href="#here" current>
  Current page
</Link>
```

### External [#external]

`icon` adds the arrow a site outside the app gets.

```tsx
<Link href="https://example.com" icon>
  External
</Link>
```

### Names for screen readers [#names-for-screen-readers]

A string child is the link's name for screen readers too, so `<Link href="/docs">Documentation</Link>` needs nothing else; `accessibilityLabel` wins when the name should differ from the text. Children drawn as given are named by the texts inside them.

## API [#api]

| Part   | Props                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Description                           |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `Link` | `quiet`: `boolean` (muted footer style), `current`: `boolean` (current page), `visited`: `boolean` (muted once opened), `inline`: `boolean` (in a paragraph), `icon`: `boolean` (external arrow); every `nsh/base` Link prop | A text link with the underline motion |

Uses `linkLook` and `LinkText`. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Link](https://nsh.dev/elements/link) passes through.

# Marker (/dev/docs/components/marker)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add marker
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Marker, MarkerContent, MarkerIcon } from "@/components/ui/marker";
```

```tsx
<Marker>
  <MarkerIcon icon={Search} />
  <MarkerContent>Explored 4 files</MarkerContent>
</Marker>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Marker`:

```text
Marker
├── MarkerIcon
└── MarkerContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Inline [#inline]

`Marker` is one muted line at the body's size, at least 16 points tall, an icon 8 points before
the text. `MarkerIcon` takes a lucide node (`icon`) or a part of its own as children — a `Spinner`,
for a status.

```tsx
<Marker>
  <MarkerIcon icon={GitBranch} />
  <MarkerContent>Switched to a new branch</MarkerContent>
</Marker>
```

### Separator [#separator]

`variant="separator"` centers the label between two hairlines, each taking the room left on its
side. Use it for a date, a compaction, or the start of a section.

```tsx
<Marker variant="separator">
  <MarkerContent>Today</MarkerContent>
</Marker>
```

### Border [#border]

`variant="border"` keeps the inline layout and closes the line with a hairline 8 points under it,
for a row that separates what follows.

```tsx
<Marker variant="border">
  <MarkerIcon icon={FileText} />
  <MarkerContent>Opened implementation notes</MarkerContent>
</Marker>
```

### Status [#status]

A marker that is still going takes a `Spinner` in `MarkerIcon`. NSH has no `status` role and no
live-region prop, so a marker whose change must be announced takes `role="alert"`, the one it has
for this.

```tsx
<Marker role="alert">
  <MarkerIcon>
    <Spinner size="sm" tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
  </MarkerIcon>
  <MarkerContent>Thinking…</MarkerContent>
</Marker>
```

### A marker that acts [#a-marker-that-acts]

Give the marker `onPress` and `role="button"`: its line is underlined and the pointer over it is a
hand.

```tsx
<Marker role="button" onPress={() => open("https://github.com/…/pull/1")}>
  <MarkerIcon icon={ExternalLink} />
  <MarkerContent>View the pull request</MarkerContent>
</Marker>
```

## API [#api]

| Part            | Props                                                                   | Description                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `Marker`        | `variant`; every `nsh` View prop; look `markerLook().root(variant)`     | A line in a conversation that is not a message |
| `MarkerIcon`    | `icon`, `children`; every `nsh` View prop; look `markerLook().icon`     | The icon beside the line                       |
| `MarkerContent` | `children`; every `nsh` Text prop; look `markerLook().content(variant)` | The line's words                               |

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through on `Marker` and
`MarkerIcon` (`role`, `onPress`, `accessibilityLabel`, …), and every prop of
[`nsh` Text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text) on `MarkerContent`. Style props go over the look's:
`style` on a `View` or `Text` part.

| Prop       | On              | Type                                   | Default   |
| ---------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `variant`  | `Marker`        | `"default" \| "border" \| "separator"` | `default` |
| `icon`     | `MarkerIcon`    | `IconNode` (from `lucide`)             |           |
| `children` | `MarkerContent` | `string \| JSX.Element`                |           |

The line is in the muted ink at the body's size (13 points with a pointer, 15 on a touch screen),
its icon 16 points in the same ink; a marker's icon box is never shrunk by a tight row. In a
terminal the icon is drawn as NSH draws icons there (a check is `✓`, the others show nothing) and
the rules are hairlines. `markerLook()` is exported for a line an app draws itself.

# Menu (/dev/docs/components/menu)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add menu
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuTrigger } from "@/components/ui/menu";
```

```tsx
<Menu>
  <MenuTrigger>File ▾</MenuTrigger>
  <MenuContent>
    <MenuItem onSelect={() => {}}>New</MenuItem>
  </MenuContent>
</Menu>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Menu`:

```text
Menu
├── MenuTrigger
└── MenuContent
    ├── MenuGroup
    │   ├── MenuLabel
    │   ├── MenuItem
    │   │   └── MenuShortcut
    │   ├── MenuCheckboxItem
    │   └── MenuRadioItem
    ├── MenuSeparator
    └── MenuSub
        ├── MenuSubTrigger
        └── MenuSubContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Checkbox and radio [#checkbox-and-radio]

```tsx
<MenuCheckboxItem checked={on} closeOnSelect={false} onSelect={toggle}>
  Show sidebar
</MenuCheckboxItem>
<MenuLabel>Sort by</MenuLabel>
<MenuRadioItem checked={sort === "Name"} onSelect={() => setSort("Name")}>
  Name
</MenuRadioItem>
```

### A line under the label [#a-line-under-the-label]

A row's height in the size table is its least: give it a `View` holding its label and a note under it (`menuItemNote`) and the row grows to hold both, growing over the theme's row inset so it never touches the row after it. A neighbour with one line keeps the one-line height.

```tsx
<MenuItem onSelect={() => {}}>
  <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, gap: 2 }}>
    <Text style={menuItemLabel()}>Open…</Text>
    <Text style={menuItemNote()}>A file, a folder or a link</Text>
  </View>
</MenuItem>
```

### A destructive item [#a-destructive-item]

`variant="destructive"` puts the danger tone on the row's label, its note and its icon; `default` is the row as it is.

```tsx
<MenuItem variant="default" onSelect={() => {}}>New</MenuItem>
<MenuItem variant="destructive" onSelect={() => remove()}>Delete</MenuItem>
```

`MenuItemVariant` is `"default" | "destructive"`, and `menuItemLabel`, `menuItemNote` and `menuItemGlyph` take the same word.

### Submenu [#submenu]

```tsx
<MenuSub>
  <MenuSubTrigger lead={<Icon icon={Share2} {...menuItemGlyph()} />}>Share</MenuSubTrigger>
  <MenuSubContent>
    <MenuItem onSelect={() => {}}>Mail</MenuItem>
  </MenuSubContent>
</MenuSub>
```

`lead` is what sits before the label — an icon, or a mark of the app's. A string child is the row's
label, and the label the touch sheet's back row shows above the nested menu; children drawn as given
are laid out between the lead and the chevron, which stays either way.

### The system's menu [#the-systems-menu]

`MenuButton` is the platform's pull-down menu — `UIContextMenu` on iOS, the context menu a pointer
opens on the desktops — with its items as data (`MenuButtonItem`: `id`, `label`, `icon`, `checked`,
