`disabled`, `destructive`, `items`, `inline`). The app decides that is the better menu there; a phone
without one (Android) draws `Menu` instead. On the web a menu is always the app's own drawing, so
`Menu` and its parts are.

```tsx
<MenuButton
  title="Arrange"
  accessibilityLabel="Arrange"
  items={[
    {
      id: "sort",
      label: "Sort by",
      inline: true,
      items: [{ id: "name", label: "Name", checked: true }],
    },
    { id: "share", label: "Share", icon: "square.and.arrow.up" },
  ]}
  onSelect={({ id }) => choose(id)}
>
  Sorted by name
</MenuButton>
```

A string child is drawn as the button's label in the theme's look (`variant`, `ghost` by default;
`size` as `Button`'s). It is not a `Button` inside: `nsh/base` makes the button's own view the
pressable on the desktops, and a nested one would take the press. A single element child is the
trigger itself, with no wrapper: its look, `testID`, name, own press and hover styles stay, and
`nsh/base` adds the open state to it (`expandedStyle`, `expanded:` classes).

### Names for screen readers [#names-for-screen-readers]

A string child is the row's label and its name for screen readers; `accessibilityLabel` wins when it should differ. Children drawn as given are named by the texts inside them.

## API [#api]

Looks are `menuItemLook`, `menuItemLabel`, `menuItemNote`, `menuItemGlyph`, `menuPopup`, `menuSeparator` and `menuHighlight`; `menuItemSize.height` is a row's least height, not its height; `SubmenuRow` and `SubmenuBack` draw a submenu's row and its touch back row. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Menu](https://nsh.dev/elements/menu) on `MenuContent` passes through except open state and `trigger`. There is no radio-group part: a `MenuGroup` holds the rows, and each `MenuRadioItem` carries its own `checked`.

| Part               | Props                                                                                                                        | Description                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Menu`             | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange({ open, reason })`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel`                                     | Open state and the trigger slot                                                |
| `MenuTrigger`      | every `Button` prop but `children`                                                                                           | Registers the trigger; a string child is a `Button`, an element is the trigger |
| `MenuContent`      | every `nsh/base` Menu prop but open state and `trigger`; defaults bottom / start / 4                                         | The popup or sheet                                                             |
| `MenuItem`         | every `nsh/base` MenuItem prop; `variant`, `inset`; a string child is the label                                              | A row                                                                          |
| `MenuCheckboxItem` | as `MenuItem`, plus `checked`                                                                                                | A checkable row                                                                |
| `MenuRadioItem`    | as `MenuItem`, plus `checked`                                                                                                | One of a group                                                                 |
| `MenuLabel`        | `children`, `inset`; every `nsh` text prop                                                                                   | A group's title                                                                |
| `MenuSeparator`    | every `nsh/base` MenuSeparator prop                                                                                          | A hairline                                                                     |
| `MenuShortcut`     | `children`; every `nsh` view prop (`style` is type, a `TextStyle`)                                                           | A trailing note                                                                |
| `MenuSub`          | `children`, `disabled`                                                                                                       | A nested menu's root                                                           |
| `MenuSubTrigger`   | `SubmenuRow`'s props (`children`, `lead`, `inset`, `disabled`, `style`, every view prop)                                     | The row that opens a submenu                                                   |
| `MenuSubContent`   | every `nsh/base` Submenu prop but `trigger`; `back` on a touch screen                                                        | The nested menu's popup                                                        |
| `MenuButton`       | `items`, `title`, `disabled`, `accessibilityLabel`, `onSelect({ id })`, `variant`, `size`; the rest of `nsh/base` MenuButton | The platform's pull-down menu; a string child is its label                     |

Every part that draws a view takes `nsh`'s view props and spreads them on it after its own look, so an app's `testID`, `accessibilityLabel`, `onLongPress` or `class` reaches the row it passes them to; `style` goes over the look's, and the states an app passes (`hoverStyle`, `focusStyle`, `activeStyle`, `disabledStyle`) are merged after the look's own. `Menu` and `MenuSub` draw no view of their own (they own the open state and the trigger slot), so they take none: an app gives those props to the trigger or the content.

# Menubar (/dev/docs/components/menubar)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add menubar
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Menubar,
  MenubarContent,
  MenubarItem,
  MenubarMenu,
  MenubarSeparator,
  MenubarTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/menubar";
```

```tsx
<Menubar>
  <MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
    <MenubarContent>
      <MenubarItem>New document</MenubarItem>
      <MenubarSeparator />
      <MenubarItem>Close</MenubarItem>
    </MenubarContent>
  </MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Menubar`:

```text
Menubar
└── MenubarMenu
    ├── MenubarTrigger
    └── MenubarContent
        ├── MenubarGroup
        │   ├── MenubarLabel
        │   ├── MenubarItem
        │   │   └── MenubarShortcut
        │   ├── MenubarCheckboxItem
        │   └── MenubarRadioItem
        ├── MenubarSeparator
        └── MenubarSub
            ├── MenubarSubTrigger
            └── MenubarSubContent
```

## Examples [#examples]

### The bar [#the-bar]

`Menubar` is a row a step over its triggers — the theme's height step under a row, the room either
side of them and its own 1-point edge — inside a 1-point edge with the card's fill, its triggers 8
points either side (`menubarLook().bar`). It places nothing itself: a `MenubarMenu` gives a trigger
and its popup, and the trigger stands in the bar, not in a box of its
own.

### The trigger that is open [#the-trigger-that-is-open]

The trigger of the menu that is open wears the neutral `accent` fill — the modal-less bar says which
menu it belongs to without the bar changing — and the pointer over another trigger whispers the same
fill. A press opens one menu and a press closes it; once one is open, the pointer moves between
menus. A disabled trigger takes no presses and dims to 50%; a string child is the trigger's name, in
the menu's type; anything else (an icon and a name) is drawn as given.

### A row with its key equivalent [#a-row-with-its-key-equivalent]

A string child is a row's label; a label and a note at the row's trailing edge (`MenubarShortcut`,
which is `MenuShortcut`) are written out — the note takes the rest of the row:

```tsx
import { menuItemLabel } from "@/components/ui/menu";

<MenubarItem>
  <>
    <Text style={menuItemLabel()}>New document</Text>
    <MenubarShortcut>⌘N</MenubarShortcut>
  </>
</MenubarItem>;
```

### The rows are the menu's [#the-rows-are-the-menus]

`MenubarItem`, `MenubarCheckboxItem`, `MenubarRadioItem`, `MenubarLabel`, `MenubarSeparator`,
`MenubarShortcut`, `MenubarGroup` and `MenubarSub` / `MenubarSubTrigger` / `MenubarSubContent` are
[`Menu`](./menu)'s parts under the bar's names: a row of a bar wears what a row of a menu wears, down
to its danger tone, its check and its dot. `MenubarShortcut` is `MenuShortcut` (the row's trailing
note), and `MenubarLabel` is `MenuLabel`: its child is the title. There is no radio-group part:
`MenubarGroup` is a `View`, and each `MenubarRadioItem` carries its own `checked`.

```tsx
<MenubarMenu>
  <MenubarTrigger>View</MenubarTrigger>
  <MenubarContent>
    <MenubarCheckboxItem checked={sidebar()} closeOnSelect={false} onSelect={toggle}>
      Show sidebar
    </MenubarCheckboxItem>
    <MenubarSeparator />
    <MenubarLabel>Zoom</MenubarLabel>
    <MenubarRadioItem checked={zoom() === "125%"} onSelect={() => zoom.set("125%")}>
      125%
    </MenubarRadioItem>
  </MenubarContent>
</MenubarMenu>
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Menu](https://nsh.dev/elements/menu) passes through on `MenubarContent`
except the trigger, the open state and the lifecycle callbacks, which the root owns. `popupStyle`,
`backdropStyle` and `popupStartingStyle` go over `menuPopup`'s. Defaults: `placement` `"bottom"`,
`align` `"start"`, `offset` `8` — a menu under the trigger it belongs to, whatever the bar's width.

| Part                  | Props                                         | Description                                            |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Menubar`             | every `nsh` view prop                         | The bar; a row holding its menus                       |
| `MenubarMenu`         | `onOpenChange`                                | Open state + lifecycle; reports `{ open, reason }`     |
| `MenubarTrigger`      | `children`, `disabled`; every `nsh` view prop | A string is the name; wears the chosen fill while open |
| `MenubarContent`      |                                               | The popup, over the menu surface                       |
| `MenubarItem`         | `variant`                                     | A row; `"destructive"` is the danger tone              |
| `MenubarCheckboxItem` | `closeOnSelect`                               | A row with a check; `false` to stay open               |
| `MenubarRadioItem`    |                                               | A row with a dot                                       |
| `MenubarLabel`        |                                               | A group's name (`text`)                                |
| `MenubarSeparator`    |                                               | A hairline between rows                                |
| `MenubarShortcut`     |                                               | The row's trailing note (a key equivalent)             |
| `MenubarGroup`        |                                               | A block grouping rows                                  |
| `MenubarSub`          |                                               | A submenu: `MenubarSubTrigger` and `MenubarSubContent` |
| `MenubarSubTrigger`   |                                               | The row that opens it (a chevron with a string)        |
| `MenubarSubContent`   |                                               | Its popup; a back row on a touch screen                |

The bar and its triggers spread the view props they are given on the row they draw, after the look
(`style` included), and merge a given `hoverStyle`, `activeStyle`, `expandedStyle` or `disabledStyle`
after the look's own. The rows, labels, notes and groups are `menu.tsx`'s, so they take what a menu's
parts take.

# Message scroller (/dev/docs/components/message-scroller)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add message-scroller
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  MessageScroller,
  MessageScrollerButton,
  MessageScrollerItem,
  MessageScrollerViewport,
} from "@/components/ui/message-scroller";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<MessageScroller style={{ height: 320 }}>
  <MessageScrollerViewport each={turns()} keyExtractor={(turn) => String(turn.id)}>
    {(item) => (
      <MessageScrollerItem>
        <Message align={item().mine ? "end" : "start"}>
          <MessageAvatar name={item().from} />
          <MessageContent>
            <Bubble variant={item().mine ? "default" : "muted"}>
              <BubbleContent>{item().text}</BubbleContent>
            </Bubble>
          </MessageContent>
        </Message>
      </MessageScrollerItem>
    )}
  </MessageScrollerViewport>
  <MessageScrollerButton />
</MessageScroller>
```

The viewport is `nsh`'s [`List`](https://nsh.dev/elements/list): `each` is the conversation in reading
order, oldest first, and the child renders one row. It is called once per cell, not once per turn —
read `item()` where the turn is used (`item().text`), because the cell is reused for another turn as
the reader scrolls.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `MessageScroller`:

```text
MessageScroller
├── MessageScrollerViewport
│   └── MessageScrollerItem
└── MessageScrollerButton

MessageScrollerProvider
└── MessageScroller
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Following [#following]

The scroller opens at the end, on the newest turn, and keeps itself there: when the content grows
— a turn is sent, a stream answers — the list keeps the end in view. Scroll up and it stops
following; the view stays where the reader put it while new turns arrive below. Scroll back to the
end and it follows again.

Give the frame a height (`style={{ height: 320 }}`): it fills what it is in, and its viewport takes
the room left. Four hundred turns cost what four do: the list mounts only the rows near the screen.

### Opening elsewhere [#opening-elsewhere]

`initialScroll="start"` opens at the oldest turn and does not follow, for a thread read from the
top. Anything else (the default, `end`) opens on the newest.

```tsx
<MessageScroller initialScroll="start" style={{ height: 220 }}>
  <MessageScrollerViewport each={turns()} keyExtractor={(turn) => String(turn.id)}>
    {(item) => <MessageScrollerItem>{item().content}</MessageScrollerItem>}
  </MessageScrollerViewport>
  <MessageScrollerButton direction="end" />
</MessageScroller>
```

### Keys [#keys]

`keyExtractor` names a turn's row. The default reads the turn's `key`, then its `id`, then its
index; give it one when the data has nothing to name a turn by. A key does two things: it keeps a
row's cell and its size as rows come and go, and it is the name `scrollToMessage` takes — a turn
with the same id on screen and in the command find each other. Keys must be unique and stable: with
an index, every append that shifts a row makes the list rebuild it.

### Buttons [#buttons]

`MessageScrollerButton` floats 16 points above the newest turn (or below the oldest) in the middle
of the viewport, and shows only while there is somewhere to go that way. It says "Scroll to end" or
"Scroll to start" to screen readers; give it `accessibilityLabel` to say something else.

```tsx
<MessageScrollerButton />

<MessageScrollerButton direction="start">
  <Icon icon={ArrowUp} {...buttonGlyph("secondary", { size: "sm" })} />
</MessageScrollerButton>
```

### A short thread, and an arrival [#a-short-thread-and-an-arrival]

`alignment="bottom"` on the viewport passes through to the list, so a conversation shorter than the frame sits at the bottom. `indicator` is a mark at the button's top-end corner; `variant` and `size` are the button's (default `secondary` and `sm`).

```tsx
<MessageScrollerViewport each={turns()} alignment="bottom" keyExtractor={(turn) => turn.id}>
  {(item) => <MessageScrollerItem>{item().content}</MessageScrollerItem>}
</MessageScrollerViewport>
<MessageScrollerButton
  indicator={
    <View
      style={{
        width: 10,
        height: 10,
        borderRadius: 5,
        backgroundColor: colors.brand,
        borderWidth: 2,
        borderColor: colors.background,
      }}
    />
  }
/>
```

### A chat [#a-chat]

A conversation starts with an empty frame: keep the greeting and its suggestions inside the
`MessageScroller` until the first turn arrives, so the frame holds its height and the composer under
it never jumps. `MessageScrollerProvider` shares the scroller with that composer, and the send
button is a `RoundButton` beside an `Input`.

```tsx
const chat = signal<Turn[]>([]);
const draft = signal("");

const send = (prompt?: string) => {
  const text = (prompt ?? draft()).trim();
  if (text === "") return;
  chat.set([...chat(), { id: next(), text, mine: true }]);
  draft.set("");
  reply(text); // the answer arrives a moment later
};

<MessageScrollerProvider>
  <View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
    <MessageScroller initialScroll="end" style={{ height: 380, borderRadius: 10 }}>
      {chat().length === 0 ? (
        <EmptyChat onPick={send} />
      ) : (
        <>
          <MessageScrollerViewport
            each={chat()}
            keyExtractor={(turn) => String(turn.id)}
            estimatedItemSize={68}
          >
            {turnRow}
          </MessageScrollerViewport>
          <MessageScrollerButton direction="start" />
        </>
      )}
    </MessageScroller>
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
      <Input
        value={draft()}
        onChange={({ value }) => draft.set(value)}
        placeholder="Message"
        submitBehavior={desktop ? "submit" : "newline"}
        onSubmit={() => send()}
        style={{ flex: 1, height: 40, borderRadius: 20 }}
      />
      <RoundButton
        side={40}
        accessibilityLabel="Send"
        disabled={draft().trim().length === 0}
        onPress={() => send()}
      >
        <Icon icon={ArrowUp} {...roundButtonGlyph("default", { side: 40 })} />
      </RoundButton>
    </View>
  </View>
</MessageScrollerProvider>;
```

`EmptyChat` takes the whole viewport (`flex: 1`, centered) and calls `send` with a starter prompt;
`turnRow` draws a turn with `Message`, `MessageAvatar` and `Bubble`. While the reader is at the end
the viewport follows a new turn; while they are not, it waits where they are.

### Older turns [#older-turns]

`onLoadMoreAtStart` is the list's own, passed through the viewport: while the reader is within
`loadMoreAtStartThreshold` viewports of the first row, the scroller asks for an older page and
prepends it. Rows on screen keep their place, so the reading position does not jump. Guard the call
with a signal — it can fire again while a page is in flight.

```tsx
const loading = signal(false);

const loadOlder = () => {
  if (loading()) return;
  loading.set(true);
  fetchOlderPage().then((page) => {
    history.set([...page, ...history()]);
    loading.set(false);
  });
};

<MessageScrollerViewport
  each={history()}
  keyExtractor={(turn) => String(turn.id)}
  estimatedItemSize={68}
  onLoadMoreAtStart={loadOlder}
>
  {(item) => <MessageScrollerItem>{turnRow(item)}</MessageScrollerItem>}
</MessageScrollerViewport>;
```

The trigger fires on the frame's start side — the top of a normal list — so the same call also
works over an inverted list, where older turns sit at the top.

### Selecting across turns [#selecting-across-turns]

`MessageScroller` is a `View`, so `selectable` passes straight through: a drag over the frame is one
selection over the rows that are mounted, instead of one per bubble.

```tsx
<MessageScroller selectable initialScroll="end" style={{ height: 200 }}>
  <MessageScrollerViewport each={excerpt} keyExtractor={(turn) => String(turn.id)}>
    {(item) => <MessageScrollerItem>{turnRow(item)}</MessageScrollerItem>}
  </MessageScrollerViewport>
</MessageScroller>
```

### Commands [#commands]

`MessageScrollerProvider` shares the scroller with controls outside the frame, such as a list of
message titles: under it, `useMessageScroller()` returns `scrollToMessage`, `scrollToStart` and
`scrollToEnd`, plus `atStart` and `atEnd` (read those in a binding, like any signal). The turn
targeted by `scrollToMessage` is the one whose key is that name; without a matching row the call
does nothing. `MessageScroller` works without the provider, with the hook reading the scroller it is
inside.

```tsx
import type { ListRef } from "nsh";
import { View } from "nsh";

import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import {
  MessageScroller,
  MessageScrollerItem,
  MessageScrollerProvider,
  MessageScrollerViewport,
  useMessageScroller,
} from "@/components/ui/message-scroller";

let scroller: ListRef | undefined;

<MessageScrollerProvider>
  <View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
    <MessageScroller style={{ height: 320 }}>
      <MessageScrollerViewport
        ref={(node) => (scroller = node)}
        each={turns()}
        keyExtractor={(turn) => String(turn.id)}
      >
        {(item) => <MessageScrollerItem>{item().content}</MessageScrollerItem>}
      </MessageScrollerViewport>
    </MessageScroller>
    <CommandBar />
  </View>
</MessageScrollerProvider>;

function CommandBar() {
  const { scrollToMessage, scrollToStart, scrollToEnd } = useMessageScroller();
  return (
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
      <Button variant="secondary" onPress={() => scrollToStart()}>
        Oldest
      </Button>
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        onPress={() => scrollToMessage("3", { align: "center", animated: true })}
      >
        Turn 3
      </Button>
      <Button variant="secondary" onPress={() => scrollToEnd()}>
        Newest
      </Button>
    </View>
  );
}
```

`MessageScrollerViewport` calls its `ref` with the [`ListRef`](https://nsh.dev/elements/list) beside
the one the scroller keeps, so the app can reach the list directly — `scroller?.scrollToIndex({ index: 0 })`,
for example.

### Turns [#turns]

`MessageScrollerItem` is the box one turn sits in, sized by what is in it; `MessageScrollerViewport`
is the list the turns are in, 32 points apart. What a turn is, is `Message`'s business.

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through on `MessageScroller` and
`MessageScrollerItem`; `MessageScrollerViewport` takes a [`List`](https://nsh.dev/elements/list)'s
(`keyExtractor`, `estimatedItemSize`, `onViewableItemsChange`, `scrollbar`, …) less the state the
scroller keeps (`inverted`, `initialScrollIndex`, `initialScrollAtEnd`,
`maintainVisibleContentPosition`, …), plus `each`, `alignment` and `onLoadMoreAtStart` (all passed to
the list — the last one loads older turns) and the child that renders a row; and `MessageScrollerButton` takes this library's
[`Button`](https://nsh.dev/elements/button) props (`variant` defaults to `secondary`, `size` to
`sm`). `alignment="bottom"` pins a short conversation to the bottom of the viewport. `indicator`
is a mark at the button's top-end corner (an arrival dot); the arrow stays.

| Part                      | Props                                                                       | Description                                                             |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MessageScroller`         | `initialScroll`                                                             | Renders `View` (`messageScrollerLook().root`)                           |
| `MessageScrollerViewport` | `each`, `children`, `keyExtractor`, `alignment`, `onLoadMoreAtStart`, `ref` | Renders `List` (`messageScrollerLook().viewport`); `ref` is a `ListRef` |
| `MessageScrollerItem`     |                                                                             | Renders `View` (`messageScrollerLook().item`)                           |
| `MessageScrollerButton`   | `direction`, `variant`, `size`, `indicator`                                 | Renders `Button` (`messageScrollerLook().slot(direction)`)              |

| Prop            | On                        | Type                                                  | Default       |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `initialScroll` | `MessageScroller`         | `"start" \| "end"`                                    | `end`         |
| `each`          | `MessageScrollerViewport` | `readonly T[]`                                        |               |
| `alignment`     | `MessageScrollerViewport` | `"top" \| "bottom"`                                   | the list's    |
| `children`      | `MessageScrollerViewport` | `(item: () => T, index: () => number) => JSX.Element` |               |
| `keyExtractor`  | `MessageScrollerViewport` | `(item: T, index: number) => string`                  | the item's id |
| `direction`     | `MessageScrollerButton`   | `"start" \| "end"`                                    | `end`         |
| `variant`       | `MessageScrollerButton`   | `Button` variant                                      | `secondary`   |
| `size`          | `MessageScrollerButton`   | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`                           | `sm`          |
| `indicator`     | `MessageScrollerButton`   | `JSX.Element`                                         |               |

| Export                    | Props / returns                                          | Description                                                       |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MessageScrollerProvider` | `children`                                               | Shares the `MessageScroller` inside it; one provider per scroller |
| `useMessageScroller()`    | `scrollToMessage`, `scrollToStart`, `scrollToEnd`, edges | The commands and edge state (`atStart`, `atEnd`) of that scroller |

| Command option | Type                           | Default |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ | ------- |
| `align`        | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `start` |
| `animated`     | `boolean`                      | `true`  |

The frame fills its parent, clips what is in it, and holds its viewport and its buttons; the list's
content is 32 points apart; a button floats 16 points from its edge. `messageScrollerLook()` is
exported for a frame an app draws itself.

# Message (/dev/docs/components/message)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add message
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Bot } from "lucide";

import { Bubble, BubbleContent } from "@/components/ui/bubble";
import { Message, MessageAvatar, MessageContent } from "@/components/ui/message";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
import { colors } from "@/lib/ui/theme";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<Message>
  <MessageAvatar name="Oliver Reed" />
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="muted">
      <BubbleContent>How can I help you today?</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Message`:

```text
Message
├── MessageAvatar
└── MessageContent
    ├── MessageHeader
    └── MessageFooter

MessageGroup
├── Message
└── Message
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Alignment [#alignment]

`align="end"` mirrors the row for what you sent: the avatar moves to the end and the column with
it, so the bubbles inside follow the message — a `Bubble` takes its place from the column unless
you give it an `align` of its own.

```tsx
<Message align="end">
  <MessageAvatar name="Mia Chen" />
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="default">
      <BubbleContent>Deploying to prod real quick.</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

### Avatar [#avatar]

`MessageAvatar` is 32 points round (36 on a touch screen), at the bottom of the row. With no
`children` it is this library's `Avatar`: `name` gives it initials on an identity hue, `src` a
picture. An avatar with neither keeps the muted circle that holds the row's alignment.

```tsx
<Message>
  <MessageAvatar name="Jason Lee" />
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="muted">
      <BubbleContent>The build failed during dependency installation.</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

Give it `children` and it is that same circle as a muted slot — a bot's glyph, or an `Avatar` of
your own — centered and clipped to the round. `name` and `src` are not used then. The glyph here
is 16 points, in the muted ink.

```tsx
<Message>
  <MessageAvatar accessibilityLabel="Assistant">
    <Icon icon={Bot} size={16} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
  </MessageAvatar>
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="muted">
      <BubbleContent>The build failed during dependency installation.</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

### Group [#group]

`MessageGroup` stacks messages from one sender 8 points apart. Render an empty `MessageAvatar` on
the earlier ones to keep them aligned with the avatar on the last.

```tsx
<MessageGroup>
  <Message>
    <MessageAvatar />
    <MessageContent>
      <MessageHeader>Olivia</MessageHeader>
      <Bubble variant="muted">
        <BubbleContent>I checked the registry addresses.</BubbleContent>
      </Bubble>
    </MessageContent>
  </Message>
  <Message>
    <MessageAvatar name="Oliver Reed" />
    <MessageContent>
      <Bubble variant="muted">
        <BubbleContent>They now live under the UI registry.</BubbleContent>
      </Bubble>
    </MessageContent>
  </Message>
</MessageGroup>
```

### Header and footer [#header-and-footer]

`MessageHeader` names the sender above the turn, at the start of the row; `MessageFooter` carries
what is under it — a delivery status — on the message's side. A string child is drawn in the look's
type.

```tsx
<Message align="end">
  <MessageAvatar name="Mia Chen" />
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="default">
      <BubbleContent>It's a one-line change.</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
    <MessageFooter>Delivered</MessageFooter>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

### A reply that is still arriving [#a-reply-that-is-still-arriving]

A reply arrives a few characters at a time. While it does, `TextView` takes
`options={{ streaming: true }}` and a `streamingCaret` — a `View` with `textViewCaretClass`, the
theme's brand-colored block that pulses — where the next word will land. Before the first word
there is no text to hang the caret on, so draw the caret alone in a line as tall as the reply's
text and leave the view out.

Stopping is the app's: it keeps the words already received, replaces the `Assistant` name in the
header with `Stopped` (a warn `Badge`) and adds a faint row saying what happened. `Resume` streams
the rest through the same signals.

```tsx
<Message>
  <MessageAvatar accessibilityLabel="Assistant">
    <Icon icon={Bot} size={16} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
  </MessageAvatar>
  <MessageContent>
    <If when={phase() === "stopped"} else={<MessageHeader>Assistant</MessageHeader>}>
      <MessageHeader>
        <Badge tone="warn" size="sm">
          Stopped
        </Badge>
      </MessageHeader>
    </If>
    <If
      when={phase() === "waiting"}
      else={
        <TextView
          markdown={reply()}
          options={{ streaming: phase() === "streaming" }}
          streamingCaret={phase() === "streaming" ? <View class={textViewCaretClass} /> : undefined}
          styles={{ root: { fontSize: 15, lineHeight: 22 } }}
        />
      }
    >
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", height: 22 }}>
        <View class={textViewCaretClass} />
      </View>
    </If>
    <If when={phase() === "stopped"}>
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
        <Icon icon={Square} size={12} tint={colors.faint} />
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, color: colors.faint }}>You stopped this reply</Text>
      </View>
    </If>
    <MessageFooter>
      <If when={phase() === "waiting" || phase() === "streaming"}>
        <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" onPress={stop}>
          Stop
        </Button>
      </If>
      <If when={phase() === "done" || phase() === "stopped"}>
        <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" onPress={phase() === "done" ? restart : resume}>
          {phase() === "done" ? "Stream it again" : "Resume"}
        </Button>
      </If>
    </MessageFooter>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

### A failed turn [#a-failed-turn]

A turn that fails leaves two marks. The sent turn keeps its place, with a `Spinner` and
`Waiting for a connection` in its footer while the app retries. The assistant's turn holds a
destructive `Alert`: an `AlertCircle`, `AlertTitle` naming the failure, and an `AlertDescription`
whose `Retry` button asks for the turn again.

```tsx
<Message align="end">
  <MessageAvatar name="Mia Chen" />
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble variant="default">
      <BubbleContent>Run the migration on staging.</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
    <If when={turn() === "waiting"}>
      <MessageFooter>
        <Spinner size="sm" tint={colors.warn} />
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, color: colors.mutedForeground }}>
          Waiting for a connection
        </Text>
      </MessageFooter>
    </If>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>

<Message>
  <MessageAvatar accessibilityLabel="Assistant">
    <Icon icon={Bot} size={16} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
  </MessageAvatar>
  <MessageContent>
    <MessageHeader>Assistant</MessageHeader>
    <If when={turn() === "failed"}>
      <Alert variant="destructive">
        <Icon icon={AlertCircle} size={ALERT_ICON} tint={colors.destructive} />
        <AlertTitle>The reply failed</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>
          <View style={{ alignItems: "flex-start", gap: 10 }}>
            <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: colors.destructive }}>
              The connection dropped before the first word. Your turn is safe.
            </Text>
            <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" onPress={retry}>
              Retry
            </Button>
          </View>
        </AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
    </If>
    <If when={turn() === "answered"}>
      <TextView markdown={answer()} />
    </If>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

### Rating a reply [#rating-a-reply]

What a reply carries under it is the app's: a copy that flips to a check for a moment, and two
thumbs. `IconButton` takes `selected`, so a pressed thumb shows the brand ink and reports
`accessibilityState={{ selected: true }}`; the rating itself is only the app's state until the app
sends it.

```tsx
const copied = signal(false);
const rating = signal<"up" | "down" | null>(null);

const copy = () => {
  void Clipboard.writeText(reply);
  copied.set(true);
  setTimeout(() => copied.set(false), 1600);
};

<MessageFooter>
  <IconButton
    variant="ghost"
    size="sm"
    selected={copied()}
    accessibilityLabel={copied() ? "Copied" : "Copy reply"}
    onPress={copy}
  >
    <Icon
      icon={copied() ? Check : Copy}
      {...iconButtonGlyph({ variant: "ghost", size: "sm", selected: copied() })}
    />
  </IconButton>
  <IconButton
    variant="ghost"
    size="sm"
    selected={rating() === "up"}
    accessibilityLabel="Good reply"
    onPress={() => rating.set(rating() === "up" ? null : "up")}
  >
    <Icon
      icon={ThumbsUp}
      {...iconButtonGlyph({ variant: "ghost", size: "sm", selected: rating() === "up" })}
    />
  </IconButton>
  <IconButton
    variant="ghost"
    size="sm"
    selected={rating() === "down"}
    accessibilityLabel="Bad reply"
    onPress={() => rating.set(rating() === "down" ? null : "down")}
  >
    <Icon
      icon={ThumbsDown}
      {...iconButtonGlyph({ variant: "ghost", size: "sm", selected: rating() === "down" })}
    />
  </IconButton>
</MessageFooter>;
```

### Actions [#actions]

Anything else in `MessageFooter` is drawn as given: a row of `IconButton`s, a retry, an error.

```tsx
<MessageFooter>
  <IconButton variant="ghost" size="sm" accessibilityLabel="Copy" onPress={copy}>
    <Icon icon={Copy} {...iconButtonGlyph({ variant: "ghost", size: "sm" })} />
  </IconButton>
  <IconButton variant="ghost" size="sm" accessibilityLabel="Like" onPress={like}>
    <Icon icon={ThumbsUp} {...iconButtonGlyph({ variant: "ghost", size: "sm" })} />
  </IconButton>
</MessageFooter>
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through on `MessageGroup`,
`Message` and `MessageContent` (`role`, `accessibilityLabel`, `style`, …). With no `children`,
`MessageAvatar` is this library's [`Avatar`](https://nsh.dev/elements/avatar): `name`, `src`,
`fallback`, `onStatusChange` and the rest of its props pass through. With `children` it renders a
`View` (`style`, `accessibilityLabel` and the other host props still pass through; `name`, `src`
and the image props are not used). A string child of `MessageFooter` and of `MessageHeader` is
drawn as [`nsh` Text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text).

| Part             | Props                     | Description                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MessageGroup`   |                           | Renders `View` (`messageLook().group`)                                                              |
| `Message`        | `align`                   | Renders `View` (`messageLook().row(align)`)                                                         |
| `MessageAvatar`  | `name`, `src`, `children` | Renders `Avatar` (`messageLook().avatar`), or a `View` (`messageLook().avatarSlot`) with `children` |
| `MessageContent` |                           | Renders `View` (`messageLook().content(align)`)                                                     |
| `MessageHeader`  | `children`                | Renders `View` (`messageLook().header`)                                                             |
| `MessageFooter`  | `children`                | Renders `View` (`messageLook().footer(align)`)                                                      |

| Prop       | On              | Type                    | Default |
| ---------- | --------------- | ----------------------- | ------- |
| `align`    | `Message`       | `"start" \| "end"`      | `start` |
| `name`     | `MessageAvatar` | `string`                |         |
| `src`      | `MessageAvatar` | `string`                |         |
| `children` | `MessageAvatar` | `JSX.Element`           |         |
| `children` | `MessageHeader` | `string \| JSX.Element` |         |
| `children` | `MessageFooter` | `string \| JSX.Element` |         |

The row is its avatar and its content 8 points apart, the content a column 10 points apart in the
body's size; the header and the footer are small (12 with a pointer, 13 on a touch screen), medium
and in the muted ink, 12 points in from the turn's edge. `messageLook()` is exported for a row an
app draws itself.

# NavStack (/dev/docs/components/nav-stack)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add nav-stack
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { createNavStack, NavPage, NavStack } from "@/components/ui/nav-stack";
```

```tsx
type Route = { id: "settings" } | { id: "general" };

const nav = createNavStack<Route>([{ id: "settings" }]);

<NavStack state={nav}>
  {(route) => (
    <NavPage title={route.id === "settings" ? "Settings" : "General"}>{/* the page */}</NavPage>
  )}
</NavStack>;
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `NavStack`:

```text
NavStack
└── NavPage
```

## Examples [#examples]

shadcn/ui has no navigation stack, and no page of its own; the behavior is NSH's
[`NavStack`](https://nsh.dev/elements/nav-stack) — the pages, the transitions, the back gestures
and the pages kept mounted with their state. This component is that stack and its pages, plus the
header a page shows on the desktops and the web, where NSH draws none.

### The stack and its routes [#the-stack-and-its-routes]

`createNavStack` is `nsh/base`'s, re-exported so a page's navigation is one import; the routes are
its state, and `routes` is an accessor, so what reads it follows a push or a pop.

```tsx
const nav = createNavStack<Route>([{ id: "settings" }]);

nav.push({ id: "general" }); // a page on top of the one shown
nav.pop(); // and back; the first page stays
nav.popToRoot(); // to the bottom in one step
nav.replace({ id: "general" }); // the top page becomes another

<Text>{() => `depth ${nav.routes().length}`}</Text>;
```

`setRoutes` swaps the whole list — a route that stays keeps its page and its state — and `remove`
takes the topmost page of a route out. `onChange` reports the routes after a page is added.

### The header on a desktop [#the-header-on-a-desktop]

A page's `title` is the system header's on iOS and Android, and on the desktops and the web — which
have no system header — it is the one `NavPage` draws: a bar's height (the theme's tallest height
step, and never under 48 points — shadcn's `h-12`), on the page's fill, a hairline under it, the
title the theme's `title` type role semibold and the room between the back button and the trailing
slot. It takes the roles the theme keeps for a header wherever it comes from
(`header.headerStyle`: the page's fill, the text color, the accent for the back button's tint).

```tsx
<NavPage
  title="General"
  headerRight={
    <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onPress={reset}>
      Reset
    </Button>
  }
>
  {/* the page */}
</NavPage>
```

`headerRight` is the system header's trailing item, and this header's: on a desktop it is where the
page's own action goes, drawn as given. A page with nothing to put in the header — its stack's first
one, no title, no trailing action — shows none, and its content starts at the top.

### The back button [#the-back-button]

The header's back button appears while there is a page below it, on the leading edge: this library's
ghost `IconButton` with a `ChevronLeft`, named "Back". It does what a platform's back does — calls
`onBackPress`, then pops unless `popOnBack` is `false`:

```tsx
<NavPage
  title="Appearance"
  popOnBack={false}
  onBackPress={askToDiscard} // the press is reported either way
>
  {/* … */}
</NavPage>
```

The platform's own back works beside it: Escape, Alt+Left, the mouse's back button and the browser's
back on the desktops, the swipe on iOS and predictive back on Android. `nsh/base` takes those, calls
`onBackPress`, and removes the route from the stack's state, so `routes()` follows without the app
doing anything.

### Your own header [#your-own-header]

`header` is `nsh/base`'s slot: give one and `NavPage` draws that instead, as wide as the page and as
tall as it lays out, with the content below it. `navPageLook()` has the words to build one that
matches — `header()`, `title()`, `backGlyph()` and `page()`.

```tsx
<NavPage title="General" header={(page) => <MyTitleBar page={page} title="General" />}>
  {/* the page */}
</NavPage>
```

A header of the app's own still answers Back, and knows where in the stack it is: `header` takes a
function of the page, which is handed the slot the drawn header reads. `back()` is what that header's
back button does — `onBackPress`, then `pop()` unless `popOnBack` is `false`; `pages()` is how many
routes the stack holds, so a header can show a back button only when there is one to go to.

A header that is the one `NavPage` draws with something added to it composes `PageHeader` instead of
drawing the bar again: it keeps the back button, the title and the trailing slot in the header's
look, and Back still calls `onBackPress` before it pops.

```tsx
import { PageHeader } from "@/components/ui/nav-stack";

<NavPage
  title="General"
  header={(page) => (
    <PageHeader
      title="General"
      above={() => page.pages() > 1}
      back={() => page.back()}
      right={
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onPress={reset}>
          Reset
        </Button>
      }
    />
  )}
>
  {/* the page */}
</NavPage>;
```

A header that is not this one at all is still built from `navPageLook()`'s words — `header()`,
`title()` and `backGlyph()` — as any content of the app's is:

```tsx
import type { NavPageSlot } from "@/components/ui/nav-stack";

function MyTitleBar(props: { page: NavPageSlot; title: string }) {
  const page = props.page;
  return (
    <View style={navPageLook().header()}>
      <If when={page.pages() > 1}>
        <IconButton accessibilityLabel="Back" onPress={() => page.back()}>
          <Icon icon={ChevronLeft} {...navPageLook().backGlyph()} />
        </IconButton>
      </If>
      <Text style={navPageLook().title()}>{props.title}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

It is a function, not a bare element, because `nsh/base` mounts the header in the page's own header
host: what the page provides around its content does not reach there, so an element passed as
`header` could not read the page it heads.

### On a phone [#on-a-phone]

iOS shows `UINavigationController`'s header and Android its toolbar, with the system's transitions,
the swipe back and predictive back; this component draws nothing of the header there, and `title`,
`headerLeft`, `headerRight`, `headerStyle`, `headerLargeTitle`, `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed` and
`statusBar` are the platform's. The header does not follow the theme unless the app says so: pass
`headerStyle={header.headerStyle}` from `@shadcn-nsh/theme` for the page's fill, the text color and
the accent, which is what the desktop header wears already.

### A large title [#a-large-title]

On iOS `headerLargeTitle` is the platform's: a large title in the content that shrinks into the bar
as the page scrolls. The desktops and the web have no such header, so the page draws one: the large
title is the first thing in the `Scroll`, and a header of the app's own keeps the small title in the
bar once the large one has scrolled past.

```tsx
const offset = signal(0);

<NavPage
  title="Library"
  header={() => (
    <View style={navPageLook().header()}>
      <IconButton accessibilityLabel="Back" onPress={() => nav.pop()}>
        <Icon icon={ChevronLeft} {...navPageLook().backGlyph()} />
      </IconButton>
      <Text style={navPageLook().title()}>{() => (offset() > 40 ? "Library" : "")}</Text>
    </View>
  )}
>
  <Scroll onScroll={(event) => offset.set(Math.round(event.offset.y))}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 34, fontWeight: "700" }}>Library</Text>
    <Text style={{ color: colors.mutedForeground }}>24 titles · synced today</Text>
    {/* the list */}
  </Scroll>
</NavPage>;
```

The header keeps its height and only its title changes, so the content starts under the bar at every
offset — which is what the platform's large title does there too. The header is a function so the
page closes its own offset over it, and the title's child is an accessor, so the title re-reads the
offset as the page moves.

### Asking before leaving [#asking-before-leaving]

`popOnBack` says whether the back button pops; `onBackPress` hears every back — the header's button
and the platform's (Escape, Alt+Left, the mouse's back button, the swipe). A page with unsaved text
turns the first off, asks in an alert, and pops only when the answer discards:

```tsx
const draft = signal("");
const ask = signal(false);

<NavPage
  title="A draft"
  popOnBack={draft().length === 0}
  onBackPress={() => {
    if (draft().length > 0) ask.set(true);
  }}
>
  <Input value={draft()} onChange={({ value }) => draft.set(value)} />
</NavPage>;

<AlertDialog
  open={ask()}
  onOpenChange={({ open }) => ask.set(open)}
  onAction={({ action }) => {
    ask.set(false);
    if (action === "discard") nav.pop();
  }}
>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Discard your changes?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>The draft is not saved.</AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogAction id="keep" role="cancel">
        Keep editing
      </AlertDialogAction>
      <AlertDialogAction id="discard" role="destructive">
        Discard
      </AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;
```

With nothing to lose (`popOnBack` true) the same back press pops without the alert, so the guard
disappears the moment the text does.

## API [#api]

`NavStack` and `NavPage` take every prop of
[`nsh/base`'s NavStack and NavPage](https://nsh.dev/elements/nav-stack); `style` goes over the look's. `createNavStack`,
`NavStackState` and `NavStackChangeEvent` are `nsh/base`'s, re-exported.

| Part             | Props                                                                  | Description                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NavStack`       | `state`, `children`, `onChange`                                        | `state` from `createNavStack`; `children(route, index)`; `onChange({ routes })`          |
| `NavPage`        | `title`, `headerRight`, `header`, `onBackPress`, `popOnBack`           | The page's header on the desktops and the web; `header` takes a function of the page     |
| `PageHeader`     | `title`, `right`, `back`, `above`                                      | The drawn header, for a `header` that adds to it; `above()` says whether a page is below |
| `createNavStack` | `routes`, `push`, `pop`, `popToRoot`, `replace`, `setRoutes`, `remove` | `nsh/base`'s, re-exported                                                                |

The looks — spread them on the views they name, or read their words for content of your own:
`navStackLook()` (`root`) and `navPageLook()` (`page`, `header`, `title`, `backGlyph`).
`navPageSize` has the header's numbers.

# Navigation Menu (/dev/docs/components/navigation-menu)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add navigation-menu
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  NavigationMenu,
  NavigationMenuContent,
  NavigationMenuItem,
  NavigationMenuLink,
  NavigationMenuList,
  NavigationMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/navigation-menu";
```

```tsx
<NavigationMenu>
  <NavigationMenuList>
    <NavigationMenuItem value="start">
      <NavigationMenuTrigger>Getting started</NavigationMenuTrigger>
      <NavigationMenuContent width={320}>
        <NavigationMenuLink onPress={() => open("introduction")}>Introduction</NavigationMenuLink>
      </NavigationMenuContent>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuLink active onPress={() => open("docs")}>
        Docs
      </NavigationMenuLink>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
  </NavigationMenuList>
</NavigationMenu>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `NavigationMenu`:

```text
NavigationMenu
└── NavigationMenuList
    ├── NavigationMenuItem
    │   ├── NavigationMenuTrigger
    │   └── NavigationMenuContent
    │       └── NavigationMenuLink
    └── NavigationMenuItem
        └── NavigationMenuLink
```

## Examples [#examples]

### The bar [#the-bar]

`NavigationMenu` is a navigation landmark (`role="navigation"`, named `"Navigation"` unless
`accessibilityLabel` says otherwise) as wide as the app gives it, holding a `NavigationMenuList`: a
row of items 4 points apart with a pointer (6 on a touch screen), wrapping onto a second line when
the window is narrow. An item is its trigger, or a link of its own. A trigger is drawn by its
item's content, which is what places it in the bar: a `NavigationMenuTrigger` declared after its
`NavigationMenuContent` draws nothing.

A trigger is the theme's tallest height step high and 16 points in either side
(`navigationMenuSize`), its name in the bar's type and a chevron after it — the theme's smallest
icon, an indicator's.

### What a trigger opens [#what-a-trigger-opens]

A panel: `NavigationMenuContent` mounts [`nsh/base` Popover](https://nsh.dev/elements/popover) on the
shared popup surface (`popupSurface`: one edge, the menu tier's shadow, the theme's radius) 10 points
of room inside (12 on a touch screen), placed against its trigger — `bottom` and `start` unless
`placement`, `align` and `offset` say otherwise — so it takes that trigger's width unless `width`
names another. What goes in it is the app's: a grid of links, a card
with a description, a form.

```tsx
<NavigationMenuContent width={480}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 4 }}>{/* a card and three described links */}</View>
</NavigationMenuContent>
```

Only one panel is open at a time, and the root owns which: `value` (controlled) or `defaultValue`,
reported by `onValueChange({ value, reason })`. The open trigger wears the `accent` fill at half and
its chevron turns 180° — at once under reduced motion, in 200 ms otherwise.

A press opens and closes a panel (Return or Space with the keyboard on the trigger), and on a desktop
the pointer's rest opens one too: 200 ms on a trigger (`delayDuration`), and the panel closes 300 ms
after the pointer has left both the trigger and the panel (`closeDelay`) — time to cross from one to
the other, not to browse. `Infinity` turns that off: only presses and the keyboard, or only Escape and
a press outside. A touch screen has no pointer to rest, so a tap opens and closes there.

### A link in a panel [#a-link-in-a-panel]

`NavigationMenuLink` is [`nsh/base` Link](https://nsh.dev/elements/link) in the bar's look: a name 13
points medium (15 on a touch screen) and, under it, a description in the muted ink. `active` is the
page the app is on — the `accent` fill at half, and announced as the current page.

```tsx
const look = navigationMenuLook();

<NavigationMenuLink onPress={() => go("installation")}>
  <Text style={look.linkText}>Installation</Text>
  <Text style={look.linkHint}>How to add a component and what it needs.</Text>
</NavigationMenuLink>;
```

It goes somewhere with `href` and `openWith`, or reports a press — and on the web a link with an
`href` shows no hover of its own, so a navigation menu's links are usually `onPress`. A `style` goes
over the look's: the demo's leading card is one link on the inset surface of
`lib/ui/surface` (`insetSurface()`).

### A bar item that is a link [#a-bar-item-that-is-a-link]

The current page is often a plain link standing where a trigger would:

```tsx
const bar = navigationMenuTriggerLook();

<NavigationMenuLink active onPress={() => go("docs")} style={bar.style} hoverStyle={bar.hoverStyle}>
  Docs
</NavigationMenuLink>;
```

A `NavigationMenuTrigger` or `NavigationMenuLink` that is not a string is drawn as given, so an icon
can lead a name.

## API [#api]

The root owns the open item and the two delays; a panel mounts [`nsh/base` Popover](https://nsh.dev/elements/popover)
and every base prop passes through except the trigger, the open state and the lifecycle callbacks.

| Part                    | Props                                                                   | Description                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NavigationMenu`        | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `delayDuration`, `closeDelay` | `onValueChange` reports `{ value, reason }`                               |
| `NavigationMenuList`    |                                                                         | The wrapping row                                                          |
| `NavigationMenuItem`    | `value`; every `nsh` view prop                                          | `value` is what the root opens; a trigger and its content, or a link      |
| `NavigationMenuTrigger` | `disabled`; every `nsh` view prop                                       | A string is the name, a chevron follows it                                |
| `NavigationMenuContent` | `width`, `placement`, `align`, `offset`, `margin`, `closeOnEscape`      | The panel; `margin` and `closeOnEscape` are base's, and more pass through |
| `NavigationMenuLink`    | `href`, `openWith`, `onPress`, `active`, `disabled`, `style`            | A link                                                                    |

`NavigationMenuItem` and `NavigationMenuTrigger` spread the view props they are given on their own
view, after the look (`style` included), and merge a given `hoverStyle`, `activeStyle`,
`focusVisibleStyle` or `disabledStyle` after the look's own; the trigger keeps the pointer's enter
and leave, which drive the item's delays. `NavigationMenu` and `NavigationMenuList` do the same on the root and the
row.

The look is `navigationMenuLook()` — `root`, `list`, `item`, `panel`, `link`, `linkText`,
`linkHint` — and `navigationMenuTriggerLook({ open })` and
`navigationMenuLinkLook({ active, disabled })` for the parts that open and go. Spread them on the
part they name; `navigationMenuSize` has the numbers.

# Number Input (/dev/docs/components/number-input)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add number-input
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from "@/components/ui/number-input";
```

```tsx
<NumberInput value={n()} onChange={({ value }) => n.set(value)} min={0} max={10} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Split steppers [#split-steppers]

```tsx
<NumberInput steps="split" value={n()} onChange={({ value }) => n.set(value)} />
```

### Pair steppers [#pair-steppers]

```tsx
<NumberInput steps="pair" value={n()} onChange={({ value }) => n.set(value)} />
```

Default `pair`: chevrons stacked at the end. `split`: − before the field and + after it.

### The look alone [#the-look-alone]

```tsx
<NumberInput
  class={numberInputClasses.frame}
  inputStyle={numberInputText()}
  {...numberInputSteps("pair", "w-8", 14)}
/>
```

### A rolling figure [#a-rolling-figure]

The field draws its own glyphs, and the caret lives in them, so the digits inside the field do not roll. `Roll` (`@/lib/ui/motion`, the `motion` registry item, which `input` installs) is the figure beside it — upstream's ticker. It rolls on the theme's `control` spring. The first value is already there. Less motion replaces it in place.

```tsx
import { Roll } from "@/lib/ui/motion";

<Roll value={total()} style={{ fontVariant: ["tabular-nums"] }}>
  {money(total())}
</Roll>;
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh/base` NumberInput](https://nsh.dev/elements/number-input) passes through. `class`, `inputStyle` and the step props go over the look's.

| Part          | Props                                           | Description                                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `NumberInput` | `steps` (`"split" \| "pair"`, default `"pair"`) | Every prop of `nsh/base` NumberInput passes through |

# OTP Input (/dev/docs/components/otp-input)

```npm

```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { OtpInput } from "@/components/ui/otp-input";
```

```tsx
<OtpInput length={6} value={code()} onChange={({ value }) => code.set(value)} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Tone [#tone]

```tsx
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="neutral" />
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="accent" />
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="info" />
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="warn" />
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="destructive" />
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="up" />
<OtpInput length={1} value="7" tone="down" />
```

### Verdict [#verdict]

A verdict tints every cell of the whole code.

```tsx
<OtpInput length={6} value="123456" tone="up" />
```

## API [#api]
