| Part       | Props                                                                                                     | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OtpInput` | `cells` (`string`, default `otpCells`), `tone` (`Tone \| (() => Tone \| undefined)`), `reject` (`number`) | Cell and caret props go over the look's. `reject` shakes the cells each time it becomes a new number; less motion plays nothing |

# Pagination (/dev/docs/components/pagination)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add pagination
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@/components/ui/pagination";
```

```tsx
<Pagination page={page()} totalPages={pages()} onChange={({ page }) => page.set(page)} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Compact [#compact]

A `compact` pager keeps Previous, a child label, and Next on one row.

```tsx
<Pagination compact variant="outline" page={chapter()} totalPages={12}>
  <Text>Chapter {chapter()} of 12</Text>
</Pagination>
```

### Custom items [#custom-items]

```tsx
import { paginationArrows, paginationItemClass } from "@/components/ui/pagination";

<Pagination
  itemClass={paginationItemClass({ variant: "outline" })}
  renderItem={paginationArrows}
/>;
```

### A jump menu [#a-jump-menu]

`renderItem` draws every item, the ellipsis included, and an ellipsis is handed the run it hides:
`start`, the first page left out, and `end`, the page after the last. Drawing that item as a `Menu`
is what makes a ten-thousand-page archive navigable — the pages of the run nearest the one shown,
a First page and a Last page, the rest through the arrows. `disabled` (an offline archive) makes
every item inert, the ellipsis with them.

```tsx
import { Menu, MenuContent, MenuItem, MenuLabel, MenuTrigger } from "@/components/ui/menu";

const ARCHIVE = 10000;

/** The 25 pages of a run at the end nearest the page shown. */
const nearPages = (start: number, end: number, current: number) => {
  const [from, to] =
    end - start <= 25 ? [start, end] : start > current ? [start, start + 25] : [end - 25, end];
  return Array.from({ length: to - from }, (_, i) => from + i);
};

<Pagination
  page={current()}
  totalPages={ARCHIVE}
  visiblePages={7}
  accessibilityLabel="Archive pages"
  onChange={({ page }) => setCurrent(page)}
  renderItem={(item) => {
    if (item.kind !== "ellipsis") return paginationArrows(item);
    const start = item.start ?? 1;
    const end = item.end ?? start + 1;
    return (
      <Menu>
        <MenuTrigger>
          <View
            accessibilityLabel={`Pages ${start} to ${end - 1}`}
            style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: "center" }}
          >
            <Text>…</Text>
          </View>
        </MenuTrigger>
        <MenuContent>
          <MenuLabel>{`Pages ${start}–${end - 1}`}</MenuLabel>
          {nearPages(start, end, current()).map((at) => (
            <MenuItem onSelect={() => setCurrent(at)}>{at}</MenuItem>
          ))}
        </MenuContent>
      </Menu>
    );
  }}
/>;
```

## API [#api]

Uses `paginationItemClass` and `paginationArrows` by default. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Pagination](https://nsh.dev/elements/pagination) passes through.

| Part         | Props                                                                                                                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Pagination` | `variant` (`PaginationVariant`; `default`, or `outline` on the ends), `compact` (`boolean`; label slot between ends), `page` (`number`; current page, 1-based) | Uses `paginationItemClass` and `paginationArrows` by default; `renderItem` draws every item, an ellipsis' `start` and `end` the run it hides |

`PaginationVariant` is `"default" | "outline"`; `paginationItemClass` takes the same word, as
`PaginationItemClassOptions`' `variant`.

# Plot (/dev/docs/components/plot)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add plot
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Bar, Grid } from "nsh/base/plot";

import { Plot, seriesColor, plotGrid } from "@/components/ui/plot";
```

```tsx
<Plot data={rows} band style={{ height: 160 }}>
  <Grid y={[0, 50, 100]} style={plotGrid()} />
  <Bar value="online" style={{ fill: seriesColor(0) }} />
</Plot>
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Legend [#legend]

```tsx
<Legend color={seriesColor(0)} label="Revenue" value="42%" />
<Legend color={seriesColor(1)} label="Costs" />
```

### Line and area [#line-and-area]

`Plot` takes the rows and the axis; `Area`, `Line` and `Grid` are the marks.

```tsx
<Plot data={rows} y="price" yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [40, 55] }}>
  <Grid style={plotGrid()} />
  <Grid style={plotBaseline()} />
  <Area backgroundStyle={plotWash(seriesColor(0))} style={{ fill: "transparent" }} />
  <Line
    style={{ stroke: seriesColor(0), strokeWidth: 2 }}
    hoverDotStyle={plotHoverDot(seriesColor(0))}
  />
</Plot>
```

### Cross line [#cross-line]

```tsx
<Plot data={rows} y="price" {...plotCrossLine()} dotClass={plotDotClass}>
  <Line />
</Plot>
```

### Axis labels [#axis-labels]

```tsx
<PlotAxis placement="right" tickValues={[40, 48, 55]} labelStyle={plotAxisText()} />
```

### A label on a tile [#a-label-on-a-tile]

A `Treemap` or `Bar` tile filled with a chart role takes two inks: a light tile reads a dark
label, a dark one a light label. `nsh/base/plot` sets `data-dark` on a label whose cell's colour
is dark, so `labelClass` names both:

```tsx
<Treemap labelClass="text-foreground data-dark:text-on-media" … />
```

`foreground` stays out of the appearance (dark in light and dark alike); `on-media` is the
white the theme keeps for a dark ground. Keep the scale's midpoint opaque: a fill mixed with the
background reads as a dark cell, and every label then wears the light ink, pale tiles included.

### A sparkline [#a-sparkline]

A row's chart is a `Plot` with `interactive={false}`: no cross line, no hover dot, just the line. The
wash under it is `plotWash`, the previous close a dashed `Grid` at that value with
`plotReference`, and the newest point a second `Plot` over the first — only the last row in it — so
its `Dot` can be a ring around a solid centre.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 104, height: 38 }}>
  <Plot
    data={rows}
    y="price"
    yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [lo, hi] }}
    interactive={false}
    style={{ width: 104, height: 38 }}
  >
    <Area curve="natural" backgroundStyle={plotWash(tone, 0.2)} />
    <Grid y={[previousClose]} style={plotReference(colors.mutedForeground)} />
    <Line curve="natural" style={{ stroke: tone, strokeWidth: 1.75 }} />
  </Plot>
  <View
    style={{ position: "absolute", top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0, pointerEvents: "none" }}
  >
    <Plot
      data={[rows[rows.length - 1]]}
      y="price"
      yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [lo, hi] }}
      interactive={false}
      style={{ width: 104, height: 38 }}
    >
      <Dot
        value="price"
        r={5.5}
        style={{ fill: "transparent", stroke: alpha(tone, 0.4), strokeWidth: 1.5 }}
      />
      <Dot value="price" r={2.5} style={{ fill: tone }} />
    </Plot>
  </View>
</View>
```

The domain is padded by a fifth of the range so the ring is not clipped at the top or the bottom;
`tone` is the theme's `up` or `down`, the same role the figure beside it uses.

### Bars and a donut [#bars-and-a-donut]

A grouped or stacked bar chart keeps its bands on the x scale and its baseline in the theme's
border: `paddingInner` and `paddingOuter` set the gap, `maxBandWidth` stops a wide window from
stretching a bar.

```tsx
<Plot
  data={sales}
  band
  xScale={{ paddingInner: 0.3, paddingOuter: 0.15, maxBandWidth: 56 }}
  yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [0, 130] }}
  style={{ height: 200 }}
>
  <Grid y={[40, 80, 120]} style={plotGrid()} />
  <Grid y={[0]} style={plotBaseline()} />
  <Bar value="online" stack="sales" />
  <Bar value="store" stack="sales" />
</Plot>
```

A donut is a `Pie` with an `innerRadius` in percent and a small `padAngle`; the figure in its hole
is a view placed over the plot, not a label the plot writes:

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 132, height: 132 }}>
  <Plot data={regions} style={{ width: 132, height: 132 }}>
    <Pie
      value="revenue"
      innerRadius="62%"
      outerRadius={58}
      padAngle={2 / 58}
      cornerRadius={3}
      sliceClass={(_, i) => fills[i % fills.length]}
    />
  </Plot>
  <View
    style={{
      position: "absolute",
      top: 0,
      right: 0,
      bottom: 0,
      left: 0,
      alignItems: "center",
      justifyContent: "center",
    }}
  >
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, color: colors.mutedForeground }}>Total</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" }}>{money(total)}</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Candles with volume [#candles-with-volume]

A candle is a `Bar` from the open to the close and a `Rule` from the low to the high, both colored
by a `"dir"` category. The volume is a second `Plot` under the price one, sharing its band scale so
the bars line up, with its own right axis:

```tsx
<Plot
  data={days}
  xScale={bands}
  yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [low, high] }}
  style={{ height: 150, marginRight: 40 }}
>
  <Grid y={[low + (high - low) / 3, low + ((high - low) * 2) / 3]} style={plotGrid()} />
  <Grid y={[low]} style={plotBaseline()} />
  <Rule value="high" base="low" color="dir" />
  <Bar value="close" base="open" color="dir" cornerRadii={1} />
  <PlotAxis placement="right" tickValues={[low, (low + high) / 2, high]} labelStyle={plotAxisText()} />
</Plot>

<Plot
  data={days}
  xScale={bands}
  yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [0, volumeTop] }}
  style={{ height: 46, marginRight: 40 }}
>
  <Bar value="volume" color="dir" cornerRadii={1} />
  <PlotAxis placement="right" tickValues={[0, volumeTop / 2, volumeTop]} format={(v) => `${v}M`} labelStyle={plotAxisText()} />
  <PlotAxis tickValues={[0, 7, 15, 23]} format={(i) => `Day ${i + 1}`} labelStyle={plotAxisText()} />
</Plot>
```

Give both plots the same `colorScale` (`{ type: "ordinal", domain: ["up", "down"], range: [up, down] }`)
so a day's candle and its volume bar are one color.

## API [#api]

Uses `plotCrossLine` and `plotDotClass` by default. Every prop of [`nsh/base/plot` Plot](https://nsh.dev/elements/plot) passes through.

`Plot` does not expose its scales or a canvas the app can paint on. The geometry, including the insets the axis labels take, is computed in `nsh/base` (`references/nsh/crates/nsh-base/src/plot/mod.rs`: the plot around line 800, the y insets around 803–812, the y map around 902–926, and `.child` around 1361; `axis.rs` `label_insets` around line 474). Copying that inset in JavaScript would drift from the line, so this library does not add an overlay hook. A wash over a band is `plotWash`.

Also export `Legend` for a colored square and label beside a chart.

| Part     | Props              | Description                                        |
| -------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `Plot`   | `band` (`boolean`) | Uses `plotCrossLine` and `plotDotClass` by default |
| `Legend` |                    | A colored square and label beside a chart          |

# Popover (/dev/docs/components/popover)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add popover
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger } from "@/components/ui/popover";
```

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger>Order 1024</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent width={260}>Shipped yesterday</PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Popover`:

```text
Popover
├── PopoverTrigger
└── PopoverContent
    └── PopoverHeader
        ├── PopoverTitle
        └── PopoverDescription
```

## Examples [#examples]

### With a header [#with-a-header]

`PopoverHeader`, `PopoverTitle` and `PopoverDescription` are layout and text: upstream writes a
popover's content inline, so give them the app's type with `style`.

```tsx
<PopoverContent width={260}>
  <PopoverHeader style={{ gap: 2 }}>
    <PopoverTitle style={{ fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: colors.foreground }}>
      Shipped yesterday
    </PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription style={{ fontSize: 12, color: colors.mutedForeground }}>
      Arriving Friday.
    </PopoverDescription>
  </PopoverHeader>
</PopoverContent>
```

### Compact [#compact]

A line or two: 12 points of padding and 4 between rows.

```tsx
<PopoverContent compact>Saved</PopoverContent>
```

### Content with its own frame [#content-with-its-own-frame]

`style` goes over the surface: a panel that brings its own padding, such as an emoji panel, drops the
popover's.

```tsx
<PopoverContent style={{ padding: 0, overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <EmojiPanel onSelect={choose} />
</PopoverContent>
```

### Placement [#placement]

```tsx
<PopoverContent placement="top" offset={8}>
  …
</PopoverContent>
```

### A trigger of your own [#a-trigger-of-your-own]

A string child is a `Button` (`variant`, `secondary` by default). A single element child is
the trigger itself, with no wrapper: its look, `testID`, name, own press, hover, active and
focus styles all stay, and `nsh/base` adds the open state to it, so `expandedStyle` and
`expanded:` classes answer the popup. `variant`, `disabled` and `style` shape a string
child; an element brings its own (its `disabled` is the one that counts).

```tsx
<PopoverTrigger variant="default">Filters</PopoverTrigger>
<PopoverTrigger>
  <Badge>New</Badge>
</PopoverTrigger>
<PopoverTrigger>
  <View accessibilityLabel="Filters" expandedStyle={{ backgroundColor: colors.brand }}>
    <Icon icon={SlidersHorizontal} size={14} />
    <Text>Filters</Text>
  </View>
</PopoverTrigger>
```

## API [#api]

The root owns the open flag; `PopoverContent` mounts [`nsh/base` Popover](https://nsh.dev/elements/popover) and every base prop passes through except those. Its children come in on a `PopIn` with `popoverLook` (the surface, 14 points of padding with a pointer and 16 on a touch screen); `class` and `style` go over that surface.

| Part                 | Props                                                                                                                  | Description                                                     |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Popover`            | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel`                                                 | The root owns the open flag                                     |
| `PopoverTrigger`     | `variant`, `disabled`, `style`                                                                                         | A string child's `Button`; an element child is the trigger      |
| `PopoverContent`     | `compact`, `width`, `class`, `style`, `placement`, `align`, `offset`, `margin`, `closeOnEscape`, `closeOnPressOutside` | The panel; `placement` through `closeOnPressOutside` are base's |
| `PopoverHeader`      | `style`, `class`                                                                                                       | A `View` around a title and its description                     |
| `PopoverTitle`       | `style`, `class`                                                                                                       | A string is `Text`                                              |
| `PopoverDescription` | `style`, `class`                                                                                                       | As `PopoverTitle`                                               |

# Pressable (/dev/docs/components/pressable)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add pressable
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Pressable } from "@/components/ui/pressable";
```

```tsx
<Pressable onPress={open}>Open the note</Pressable>
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Disabled [#disabled]

```tsx
<Pressable disabled onPress={open}>
  Open the note
</Pressable>
```

### A region with its own look [#a-region-with-its-own-look]

`Pressable` draws nothing of its own: no fill, no padding, no height. It is its content, and a `style` adds whatever geometry the region needs. The theme's lightest hover fill, the press's sink and the keyboard's ring are the whole of its look.

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityLabel="Comment from Ada"
  onPress={open}
  style={{ padding: 10, borderRadius: 10, backgroundColor: surface() }}
>
  <Item>…</Item>
</Pressable>
```

### A picture [#a-picture]

```tsx
<Pressable accessibilityLabel="Photo of the launch site" onPress={enlarge}>
  <Image src={photo} style={{ width: "100%", height: 132, objectFit: "cover" }} />
</Pressable>
```

### A stretch of text [#a-stretch-of-text]

A string child is plain text, and its text is the region's name for screen readers unless `accessibilityLabel` says otherwise. Children drawn as given are named by the texts inside them; one that draws no text needs an `accessibilityLabel` (the icon-only case is an `IconButton`, where it is required). `accessibilityHint` says what a press does, read after the name.

```tsx
<Pressable onPress={read}>A whole paragraph can be the region.</Pressable>
```

### The role it reads as [#the-role-it-reads-as]

A region says what it is with `role` (`role="button"` is the default, `role="link"`, `role="tab"`, …): that is NSH's own name for it, and React Native's `accessibilityRole` is not it. What a region _is_ — a link, a key in a toolbar — is the `role`; its state is `selected` and `disabled`, the base button's own props, which screen readers say. There is no `accessibilityState` prop: React Native's state names are not NSH's.

A pressable is not an on / off control: `role="switch"` does not make one a switch, and it has no
`checked` — its state is `selected`. For a setting, use `Switch`, which owns the switch role and
its value for screen readers — either the whole row (the switch's children are its label, so a tap
anywhere toggles it) or a `Field` with the switch at the end of the row. See [`Switch`](./switch).

```tsx
{
  /* Not this: a region that reads as a selected button, not as a switch. */
}
<Pressable selected={on()} onPress={toggle}>
  Extract text from images
</Pressable>;

{
  /* This: the control that is on or off, and its name. */
}
<Switch
  accessibilityLabel="Extract text from images"
  checked={on()}
  onChange={({ checked }) => on.set(checked)}
/>;
```

### Press scale [#press-scale]

A press sinks a pressable to 98%. `scale` is that much and nothing else: `0.8` for a dot that gives under a thumb, `1` for a row that should not move. Nothing sinks with reduced motion, or in a theme that draws no press (`press.scale` of 1).

```tsx
<Pressable scale={0.8} hitSlop={30} accessibilityLabel="Tiny dot" onPress={tap} />
<Pressable scale={1} onPress={open}>
  A row that stays put
</Pressable>
```

### The look alone [#the-look-alone]

The look is a function, for a `nsh/base` control of your own. Its `shape.control` corners shape the focus ring; a `style` with its own radius moves the ring with it.

```tsx
<Button {...pressableLook()}>Open the note</Button>
<Button {...pressableLook({ style: { padding: 12 } })}>Open the note</Button>
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Button](https://nsh.dev/elements/button) passes through (`onPress`, `disabled`, `selected`, `role`, `hitSlop`, `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityHint`, …). `style`, `hoverStyle`, `activeStyle` and `focusVisibleStyle` go over the look's. `scale` is the sink of a press.

| Part        | Props                                | Description                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Pressable` | `children` (`string \| JSX.Element`) | One look — the hover, the sink and the ring — and its appearance is its content's |

There is no axis: a pressable has one look — the hover, the sink and the ring — and its appearance
is its content's. `pressableLook` takes `disabled` (no hover or press feedback), `scale` (how far a
press sinks it) and `style` (geometry over the look's), and is what the reference page spreads on
`nsh/base`'s Button.

# Progress (/dev/docs/components/progress)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add progress
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressStep, ProgressSteps } from "@/components/ui/progress";
```

```tsx
<Progress value={35} />
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Progress` with steps:

```text
Progress
└── ProgressSteps
    └── ProgressStep
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Tone [#tone]

```tsx
<Progress value={72} tone="neutral" />
<Progress value={72} tone="accent" />
<Progress value={72} tone="info" />
<Progress value={72} tone="warn" />
<Progress value={72} tone="destructive" />
<Progress value={72} tone="up" />
<Progress value={72} tone="down" />
```

### Thin rail [#thin-rail]

```tsx
<Progress value={60} height={4} style={{ width: 240 }} />
```

### Indeterminate [#indeterminate]

Pass a shared `progressSweep()` from the look and set `indeterminate`.

```tsx
const sweep = progressSweep();
<Progress indeterminate sweep={sweep} style={{ width: 240 }} />;
```

### Marker [#marker]

`marker` is where a limit stands, a percentage along the bar: a hairline crossing the rail and
standing past it. The hairline is drawn on the bar's own frame, so the rail comes first in the
bar's row and a label goes after it.

```tsx
<Progress value={83} marker={90} />
<Progress value={92} marker={85} tone="warn" />
```

### Steps [#steps]

`ProgressSteps` draws step marks on the bar, a `ProgressStep` each, with `state` `done`, `current` or `upcoming`. The bar runs from the first mark's middle to the last's, so the row hangs half a mark (`progressStepSize()`) past each end: give the `Progress` that room at its sides. `value` stays the app's (0 at the first step, 100 at the last), as do Back and Next. A done step shows a check that pops in; the current one a ring and a dot; reduced motion lands each at once. A string child is the label under the mark and, with the state, its name for screen readers. Middle labels are centred under their marks; the first starts at its mark's outer edge and the last ends at its, so no label hangs past the half mark. The row is laid out left to right whatever the reading direction, as the bar fills.

```tsx
<View style={{ paddingHorizontal: progressStepSize() / 2 }}>
  <Progress value={(step() / 3) * 100} height={4} accessibilityLabel="Setup">
    <ProgressSteps>
      <ProgressStep state="done">Account</ProgressStep>
      <ProgressStep state="current">Profile</ProgressStep>
      <ProgressStep state="upcoming">Team</ProgressStep>
      <ProgressStep state="upcoming">Review</ProgressStep>
    </ProgressSteps>
  </Progress>
</View>
```

## API [#api]

Uses `progressLook`. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Progress](https://nsh.dev/elements/progress) passes through.
The rail is the theme's track form: a sunk groove 6 points high with the inset shade, an accent-tinted
band 4 points high, or WinUI's 1-point input line under a 3-point run; `height` overrides the height,
never the form.

| Part            | Props                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                         |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Progress`      | `height` (`number`, default the track form's: 6 sunk, 4 tint, 3 hairline), `tone` (`Tone \| (() => Tone)`, default citrus), `sweep` (`ProgressSweep`), `marker` (`number`, 0 to 100) | Uses `progressLook`; `marker` stands a hairline at the limit        |
| `ProgressSteps` | every `nsh` View prop                                                                                                                                                                | The row of marks over the bar, centred on it; a child of `Progress` |
| `ProgressStep`  | `state` (`"done" \| "current" \| "upcoming"`, default `upcoming`), `children` (a string is the label)                                                                                | One mark, its label under it                                        |

`progressStepsLook()`, `ProgressStepMark` and `progressStepSize()` are the look's parts, for a row of your own.

# Radio (/dev/docs/components/radio-group)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add radio-group
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from "@/components/ui/radio-group";
```

```tsx
<RadioGroup>
  <Radio checked={plan() === "pro"} onChange={() => plan.set("pro")}>
    Pro
  </Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `RadioGroup`:

```text
RadioGroup
└── Radio
    └── RadioRing
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Size [#size]

```tsx
<Radio size="sm">Small</Radio>
<Radio size="default">Regular</Radio>
<Radio size="lg">Large</Radio>
```

`size` is `ChoiceSize` (`"sm" | "default" | "lg"`: 0.8, 1 or 1.25 times the page's control size), shared with `Checkbox`.

### Disabled [#disabled]

```tsx
<Radio checked disabled>
  Team
</Radio>
```

### Tile [#tile]

```tsx
<Radio variant="tile" checked={on()} onChange={() => on.set(true)}>
  Option A
</Radio>
```

### The look alone [#the-look-alone]

`choiceTileLook` is the checkbox module's, shared by the tile radio: import it from
`@/components/ui/checkbox`.

```tsx
import { choiceTileLook } from "@/components/ui/checkbox";

<Radio class="group" checked={on()} {...choiceTileLook(() => on())}>
  <RadioRing on={on()} />
  Option A
</Radio>;
```

### Names for screen readers [#names-for-screen-readers]

A string child is the row's label and its name for screen readers; `accessibilityLabel` wins when it should differ. Children drawn as given are named by the texts inside them.

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Radio](https://nsh.dev/elements/radio) and [`RadioGroup`](https://nsh.dev/elements/radio) passes through. Style props go over the look's. The row is the `group` the ring sinks with while pressed. `RadioGroupItem` is an alias of `Radio`.

| Part             | Props                                                                                                                                                                      | Description                                             |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Radio`          | `variant` (`RadioVariant`, default `"default"`), `indicator` (`boolean`, default `true`), `size` (`ChoiceSize`, default `"default"`), `children` (`string \| JSX.Element`) | The ring of the theme's choice recipe, or a choice tile |
| `RadioGroup`     |                                                                                                                                                                            | Every prop of `nsh/base` RadioGroup passes through      |
| `RadioGroupItem` |                                                                                                                                                                            | An alias of `Radio`                                     |

`RadioVariant` is `"default"` (the sunk ring) or `"tile"` (the whole surface is the control, this library's own value).

# RefreshIndicator (/dev/docs/components/refresh-indicator)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add refresh-indicator
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { RefreshIndicator } from "@/components/ui/refresh-indicator";
```

```tsx
const pull = createAnimatedValue(0);

<View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <Scroll
    refreshing={refreshing()}
    onRefresh={refresh}
    pullValue={pull}
    refreshIndicator={{ height: 72 }}
  >
    {rows}
  </Scroll>
  <RefreshIndicator pull={pull} refreshing={refreshing()} />
</View>;
```

The scroll view (or `List`) keeps `onRefresh`, `refreshing`, `pullValue` and `refreshIndicator`: `refreshIndicator` hides the system's spinner, makes a pull refresh once it reaches `height`, and keeps `height` above the content while refreshing; `pullValue` is the animated value it feeds with how far it is pulled. `RefreshIndicator` only draws that value, over the top of the scroll view: its opacity, travel and scale follow `pull` on the UI thread, with no JS per frame. The arrow turns over once the pull is past half of `height`; while `refreshing` it gives way to a ring that spins. The strip takes no presses, so it sits above the scroll view without blocking it. Pass the same `height` to both.

## Examples [#examples]

### Pull to refresh [#pull-to-refresh]

A list that reloads when it is pulled. `refreshing` is the app's: it is set in `onRefresh` and cleared when the reload ends, and the indicator draws it.

```tsx
const refreshing = signal(false);
const pull = createAnimatedValue(0);
const refresh = () => {
  refreshing.set(true);
  reload().then(() => refreshing.set(false));
};

<View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <Scroll
    style={{ flex: 1 }}
    refreshing={refreshing()}
    onRefresh={refresh}
    pullValue={pull}
    refreshIndicator={{ height: 72 }}
  >
    <ItemGroup>
      <Each of={rows}>{(row) => <Item>…</Item>}</Each>
    </ItemGroup>
  </Scroll>
  <RefreshIndicator pull={pull} refreshing={refreshing()} />
</View>;
```

### The system spinner [#the-system-spinner]

Leave `refreshIndicator` and `pullValue` off and the platform draws its own spinner; there is nothing to mount. Use this when the platform's look is what you want.

```tsx
<Scroll refreshing={refreshing()} onRefresh={refresh}>
  {rows}
</Scroll>
```

## API [#api]

`RefreshIndicator` is a [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) in the library's look; every prop of View passes through but `children`, and `style` goes over the look's. The pull itself (`refreshIndicator`, `pullValue`, `onRefresh`, `refreshing`) is [`nsh` Scroll](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll)'s. There is no pull on the web, so the chip stays hidden there.

| Part               | Props                                                                                                 | Description                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `RefreshIndicator` | `pull`: `AnimatedValue`; `refreshing`: `boolean`; `height`: `number` (72, `REFRESH_INDICATOR_HEIGHT`) | The chip over the top of a scroll view. `height` is the scroll view's `refreshIndicator` height, read once at make time. |

`refreshIndicatorLook()` is exported for an indicator the app draws itself: its parts as the styles they wear (`root`, `chip`, `arrow`, `ring`, `glyph`, `tint`). Reduced motion stops the ring's spin; the pull still moves the chip, since it is the user's own hand.

shadcn/ui has no counterpart (the web has no pull), so there is nothing to compare; the name follows the `refreshIndicator` prop it is drawn for.

| Part                  | Props | Description                                              |
