# Rich Editor (/dev/docs/components/rich-editor)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add rich-editor
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  createRichEditor,
  RichEditor,
  richEditorClasses,
  StarterKit,
} from "@/components/ui/rich-editor";
```

```tsx
const session = createRichEditor({ extensions: [StarterKit], content: doc, format: "markdown" });

<RichEditor editor={session} style={{ height: 240 }} />;
```

`RichEditor` defaults `classes` to `richEditorClasses` and merges yours into them: a part you leave out keeps the look's, `null` drops it, and a part that is a map of node or mark classes (`nodes`, `marks`) merges name by name, so `classes={{ nodes: { heading: "text-xl" } }}` overrides that node and keeps the look's others. Every prop of [`nsh/base` RichEditor](https://nsh.dev/elements/rich-editor) passes through.

The file re-exports the session's API beside the view, so an app imports the editor once: `createRichEditor` and the kits a session starts from (`StarterKit`, `TableKit`), the commands, `defineSchema` / `defineExtension` / `richExtension` and `RichEditorPlugin` for a session of its own, and the types of the session, its parts, its commands, its extensions and its node views. `command("<name>")` runs any Tiptap command by name; `chain`, `undo`, `redo`, `extendMarkRange` and `insertContent` are the named builders a toolbar usually needs.

## Examples [#examples]

### Rich document [#rich-document]

`RichEditor` wears `richEditorClasses`; the session comes from `createRichEditor`.

```tsx
const session = createRichEditor({ extensions: [StarterKit], content: doc, format: "markdown" });

<RichEditor editor={session} accessibilityLabel="Notes" style={{ height: 180 }} />;
```

### A formatting toolbar [#a-formatting-toolbar]

A bar over the document, every control reading the caret: the block it stands in, the marks it
carries, the list around it. The session re-reads on each `revision`, so `isActive` and `can` are
current when the bar draws; a control whose command cannot run where the caret stands is `disabled`
(`can`), and a press runs the command and puts the caret back with `focus()` — or the document loses
it to the button. `command` builds the Tiptap commands by name; the list indents are
`sinkListItem` and `liftListItem` over `listItem`.

```tsx
import {
  command,
  type RichCommand,
  type RichEditorSession,
  undo,
  redo,
} from "@/components/ui/rich-editor";

function bar(session: RichEditorSession, revision: () => number) {
  const on = (name: string, attrs?: Record<string, unknown>) => (
    revision(),
    session.isActive(name, attrs)
  );
  const can = (cmd: RichCommand) => (revision(), session.can(cmd));
  const run = (cmd: RichCommand) => {
    session.run(cmd);
    session.focus();
  };
  return { on, can, run };
}

<Toolbar accessibilityLabel="Formatting" style={{ flexWrap: "wrap", alignSelf: "flex-start" }}>
  <ToolbarGroup accessibilityLabel="Block">
    <Toggle
      pressed={on("heading", { level: 2 })}
      onChange={() => run(command("toggleHeading", { level: 2 }))}
    >
      H2
    </Toggle>
  </ToolbarGroup>
  <ToolbarSeparator />
  <ToolbarGroup accessibilityLabel="Marks">
    <Toggle
      disabled={!can(command("toggleBold"))}
      pressed={on("bold")}
      onChange={() => run(command("toggleBold"))}
    >
      Bold
    </Toggle>
  </ToolbarGroup>
  <ToolbarSeparator />
  <Button
    variant="ghost"
    accessibilityLabel="Undo"
    disabled={!can(undo())}
    onPress={() => run(undo())}
  >
    Undo
  </Button>
</Toolbar>;
```

### A link bubble [#a-link-bubble]

`bubbleMenu` is Tiptap's bubble menu, filled by the app: it sits over the selection, flips below it
where there is no room, and follows the text as it scrolls. **The app decides when it is there** —
this one while the caret stands in a link (`isActive("link")`) or while its address is being
written — and draws what it holds. `extendMarkRange("link")` first, then `setLink` or `unsetLink`,
so the whole link changes and not just the character under the caret; an address written at an empty
caret is `insertContent` of a node marked `link`. Closing the field waits a turn (`setTimeout(…,
0)`) before `focus()`: on the web the Return that submitted it is still being handled, and an editor
focused now would take it and write a line break into the link.

```tsx
const session = createRichEditor({ extensions: [StarterKit], content: doc, format: "markdown" });
const inLink = () => (revision(), session.isActive("link"));
const address = () => {
  revision();
  const href = (session.getAttributes("link") as { href?: unknown } | null)?.href;
  return typeof href === "string" ? href : "";
};

<RichEditor
  editor={session}
  accessibilityLabel="Reading list"
  bubbleMenu={
    inLink() ? (
      <View
        style={{
          flexDirection: "row",
          alignItems: "center",
          gap: 2,
          ...popoverLook({ compact: true }),
        }}
      >
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, color: colors.info }} numberOfLines={1}>
          {address()}
        </Text>
        <IconButton accessibilityLabel="Edit link" size="sm" onPress={() => draft.set(address())}>
          <Icon icon={Pencil} {...iconButtonGlyph({ size: "sm" })} />
        </IconButton>
        <IconButton
          accessibilityLabel="Open link"
          size="sm"
          onPress={() => void openUrl(address())}
        >
          <Icon icon={ExternalLink} {...iconButtonGlyph({ size: "sm" })} />
        </IconButton>
        <IconButton
          accessibilityLabel="Remove link"
          size="sm"
          onPress={() => session.run(chain([extendMarkRange("link"), command("unsetLink")]))}
        >
          <Icon icon={Unlink} {...iconButtonGlyph({ size: "sm" })} />
        </IconButton>
      </View>
    ) : undefined
  }
/>;
```

### A node in the text [#a-node-in-the-text]

An extension's node view: `addNodeView` returns the app's own component, and the editor draws
every node of that type with it — the component runs when a node appears, and its props change in
place when the node's attributes or its selection do. `RichNodeViewProps` carries `node` (its
`attrs`), `selected` (it takes presses, so the caret steps over an atom as one character and
Backspace deletes it) and the session's own `updateAttributes` / `deleteNode` for a node that edits
itself. Typing never runs the component.

```tsx
const mention = (name: string): RichNodeJSON => ({ type: "mention", attrs: { name } });

function MentionChip(props: RichNodeViewProps) {
  return (
    <View
      style={{
        flexDirection: "row",
        alignItems: "center",
        gap: 4,
        paddingHorizontal: 5,
        borderRadius: 5,
        backgroundColor: colors.primary,
        borderWidth: 1,
        borderColor: props.selected ? colors.primaryForeground : "transparent",
      }}
    >
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, fontWeight: "600", color: colors.primaryForeground }}>@</Text>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, color: colors.primaryForeground }}>
        {String(props.node.attrs.name ?? "")}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}

const Mention = defineExtension({
  name: "mention",
  node: { group: "inline", inline: true, atom: true, attrs: { name: { default: "" } } },
  addNodeView: () => MentionChip,
});

const session = createRichEditor({
  extensions: [StarterKit, Mention],
  doc: {
    type: "doc",
    content: [
      {
        type: "paragraph",
        content: [
          { type: "text", text: "Ask " },
          mention("Runtime"),
          { type: "text", text: " about the engine." },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
});

// The chips sit on the text's line, not above it.
const classes = {
  ...richEditorClasses,
  nodes: { ...richEditorClasses.nodes, mention: "align-middle" },
};

<RichEditor editor={session} accessibilityLabel="Chat" classes={classes} />;
```

## API [#api]

| Part                                                                        | Props                                                                              | Description                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `RichEditor`                                                                | every `nsh/base` RichEditor prop; `classes` over `richEditorClasses`, part by part | Themed `nsh/base` RichEditor              |
| `richEditorClasses`                                                         | —                                                                                  | `RichEditor` document chrome              |
| `RichEditorProps`                                                           | —                                                                                  | `nsh/base`'s `RichEditorProps`, unchanged |
| `createRichEditor`, `defineSchema`                                          | `nsh/base`'s                                                                       | The session the view shows                |
| `StarterKit`, `TableKit`                                                    | —                                                                                  | The extensions a session starts from      |
| `chain`, `command`, `undo`, `redo`, `extendMarkRange`, `insertContent`      | `nsh/base`'s                                                                       | The Tiptap commands a toolbar runs        |
| `defineExtension`, `richExtension`, `RichEditorPlugin`                      | `nsh/base`'s                                                                       | An extension or plugin of the app's       |
| `RichEditorSession`, `RichCommand`, `RichNodeViewProps`, `RichEditorRef`, … | —                                                                                  | `nsh/base`'s types, re-exported           |

# Scrollbar (/dev/docs/components/scrollbar)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add scrollbar
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Scrollbar } from "@/components/ui/scrollbar";
```

```tsx
<Scroll name="inbox" scrollbar={false} />
<Scrollbar scroll="inbox" />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A list [#a-list]

`Scroll` hides its platform bar; `Scrollbar` draws the theme's bar for it.

```tsx
<Scroll ref={inbox} scrollbar={false} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  …
</Scroll>
<Scrollbar scroll={inbox} accessibilityLabel="Inbox scroll" />
```

### Every scroll view [#every-scroll-view]

`Scrollbar.setTheme()` installs the same look on every view that still uses the platform indicator; `null` gives the platform's back.

```tsx
Scrollbar.setTheme();
```

## API [#api]

Uses `scrollbarTheme` by default. Call `Scrollbar.setTheme()` to install it on every scroll view. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Scrollbar](https://nsh.dev/elements/scrollbar) passes through.

| Part        | Props | Description                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Scrollbar` |       | Uses `scrollbarTheme` by default; `setTheme()` installs it on every scroll view |

# Segmented (/dev/docs/components/segmented)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add segmented
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Segmented, SegmentedItem, SegmentedList } from "@/components/ui/segmented";
```

```tsx
<Segmented defaultValue="list">
  <SegmentedList>
    <SegmentedItem value="list">List</SegmentedItem>
  </SegmentedList>
</Segmented>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Segmented`:

```text
Segmented
└── SegmentedList
    └── SegmentedItem
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Fill / small [#fill--small]

`size` is the scale: `default` is the theme's `height.md` high (28 points with a pointer in the
library's themes, 40 on a touch screen) and `sm` its `height.sm` (24, 32).

The track is the theme's `channel` and the thumb its `plate`, both read where they are drawn: a
well holding a raised block. The thumb is always as big as a segment's own box, so the pointer's
hover shade covers exactly the box the chosen block covers. Every theme draws this one form — the
list reads no control dimension, so `apple`'s capsule-in-a-capsule and `material`'s connected
cells are gone; what the native controls look like instead is in the theme's difference table
(`docs/specs/native-themes.md` §3.6).

```tsx
<SegmentedList size="default" fill>
  …
</SegmentedList>
<SegmentedList size="sm">
  …
</SegmentedList>
```

## API [#api]

Uses `segmentedLook`. Composition: `Segmented`, `SegmentedList`, `SegmentedItem`. Every prop of [`nsh/base` Tabs / `Tab`](https://nsh.dev/elements/tabs) passes through on the list and items.

| Part            | Props                                                             | Description                                           |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Segmented`     |                                                                   | Composition, with `SegmentedList` and `SegmentedItem` |
| `SegmentedList` | `size` (`SegmentedSize`, default `"default"`), `fill` (`boolean`) | `size` is `"default"` or `"sm"`                       |
| `SegmentedItem` |                                                                   | Composition, with `Segmented` and `SegmentedList`     |

`SegmentedSize` is `"sm" | "default"`.

# Select (/dev/docs/components/select)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add select
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "@/components/ui/select";
```

```tsx
<Select value={value} onChange={({ value }) => setValue(value)}>
  <SelectTrigger>
    <SelectValue placeholder="Language" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="en">English</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="de">Deutsch</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Select`:

```text
Select
├── SelectTrigger
│   └── SelectValue
└── SelectContent
    ├── SelectGroup
    │   ├── SelectLabel
    │   └── SelectItem
    └── SelectItem
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Disabled choice, disabled select [#disabled-choice-disabled-select]

```tsx
<SelectItem value="svelte" disabled>
  Svelte
</SelectItem>
<Select disabled>…</Select>
```

### Invalid [#invalid]

The trigger's edge takes the danger tone.

```tsx
<SelectTrigger invalid>
  <SelectValue placeholder="Country" />
</SelectTrigger>
```

### Grouped choices [#grouped-choices]

`SelectLabel` names the section; the list draws its header.

```tsx
<SelectContent>
  <SelectGroup>
    <SelectLabel>Europe</SelectLabel>
    <SelectItem value="de">Deutsch</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="fr">Français</SelectItem>
  </SelectGroup>
  <SelectGroup>
    <SelectLabel>Asia</SelectLabel>
    <SelectItem value="ja">日本語</SelectItem>
  </SelectGroup>
</SelectContent>
```

### Outline trigger, and a width [#outline-trigger-and-a-width]

`variant="outline"` is a trigger that is not a form's field: the raised finish instead of the
field's well.

```tsx
<SelectTrigger variant="outline" style={{ width: 260 }}>
  <SelectValue placeholder="Filter" />
</SelectTrigger>
```

### A trigger that takes the room of a row [#a-trigger-that-takes-the-room-of-a-row]

`style` on `SelectTrigger` is the trigger's box in the app's layout: the properties that place it
where the app puts it — `flex`, `flexGrow`, `flexShrink`, `flexBasis`, `width`, `minWidth`,
`maxWidth`, `alignSelf` and the margins — go on the view around the trigger, so it grows, shrinks
and keeps its distances like any other view. The rest of the style (the fill, the edge, the
padding) stays on the trigger itself.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
  <Select placeholder="MM">
    <SelectTrigger style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }} />
    <SelectContent accessibilityLabel="Month">
      <SelectItem value="01">01</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
  <Select placeholder="YYYY">
    <SelectTrigger style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }} />
    <SelectContent accessibilityLabel="Year">
      <SelectItem value="2026">2026</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
</View>
```

With a pointer the trigger asks for 180 points at least (room for the list's rows). A `width` on
`style` is the trigger's size and wins over that floor, so `style={{ width: 120 }}` stays 120
points inside its parent. `minWidth: 0` still lets a narrow row squeeze a trigger that has no
width of its own, and its title ends in an ellipsis instead of overflowing.

### Uncontrolled [#uncontrolled]

```tsx
<Select defaultValue="en" onChange={({ value }) => save(value)}>
  …
</Select>
```

## API [#api]

The root owns the open flag and the value; `SelectContent` mounts [`nsh/base` Select](https://nsh.dev/elements/select) and every base prop passes through except those. `listboxProps` and `OptionRow` fill the popup, the scrim and the rows by default.

| Part            | Props                                                                                                                                               | Description                                                                                                               |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Select`        | `value`, `defaultValue`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `disabled`, `cleanable`, `placeholder`, `onChange`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onCancel` | The root owns the open flag and the value                                                                                 |
| `SelectTrigger` | `icon`, `lead`, `invalid`, `variant`, `chevron`, `style`                                                                                            | A `Picker`. The layout keys on `style` place it where the app puts it; a `width` there also overrides the 180-point floor |
| `SelectValue`   | `placeholder`                                                                                                                                       | The placeholder while nothing is chosen                                                                                   |
| `SelectContent` | `items`, `minWidth`                                                                                                                                 | The list; `items` instead of `SelectItem` children                                                                        |
| `SelectItem`    | `value`, `disabled`, `group`                                                                                                                        | A string child is its title                                                                                               |
| `SelectGroup`   |                                                                                                                                                     | A section                                                                                                                 |
| `SelectLabel`   |                                                                                                                                                     | The section's name                                                                                                        |

# Separator (/dev/docs/components/separator)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add separator
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/ui/separator";
```

```tsx
<Separator />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Orientation [#orientation]

`horizontal` (the default) runs across its container, one point thick; `vertical` runs down it and
is as tall as its row, so the row has to have a height (its own, or one its content gives it).

```tsx
<Separator orientation="horizontal" />
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 12, height: 20 }}>
  <Text>Blog</Text>
  <Separator orientation="vertical" />
  <Text>Docs</Text>
</View>
```

### Space around it [#space-around-it]

The separator is the line and nothing else: the room above and below it is the caller's.

```tsx
<Separator style={{ marginVertical: 12 }} />
```

### Decorative or not [#decorative-or-not]

A separator is usually a line of the layout: `decorative` is `true` by default, and a screen reader
walks from one group of content to the next without stopping on it. `decorative={false}` keeps it
in the accessibility tree, as a `role="group"` (`nsh` has no `separator` role — the nearest is a
boundary between groups); give it an `accessibilityLabel` saying what it divides.

```tsx
<Separator decorative={false} accessibilityLabel="End of the account settings" />
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through (`style`, `role`,
`accessibilityLabel`, …); `style` goes over the look's.

| Part        | Props                                                                                                          | Description                                     |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `Separator` | `orientation` (`"horizontal" \| "vertical"`, default `"horizontal"`), `decorative` (`boolean`, default `true`) | The line is one point of the theme's edge color |

The line is one point of the theme's edge color (`colors.border`, `theme.json`'s `border`), with
no other look: a corner is the caller's `style`, and so is its room. `separatorLook(orientation)`
is exported for a line the app draws itself.

# Sheet (/dev/docs/components/sheet)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add sheet
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/sheet";
```

```tsx
<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger>Open</SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="bottom">
    <SheetHeader>
      <SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle>
      <SheetDescription>Sort, price and availability.</SheetDescription>
    </SheetHeader>
    <SheetFooter>
      <SheetClose>Done</SheetClose>
    </SheetFooter>
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Sheet`:

```text
Sheet
├── SheetTrigger
└── SheetContent
    ├── SheetHeader
    │   ├── SheetTitle
    │   └── SheetDescription
    ├── SheetClose
    └── SheetFooter
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Side [#side]

```tsx
<SheetContent side="bottom">…</SheetContent>
<SheetContent side="right">…</SheetContent>
```

### Grabber [#grabber]

A bottom sheet has a grabber at its top: `nsh/base`'s own handle, which screen readers adjust to
change the detent and which moves to the next larger one when pressed, drawn in the theme's look
(`sheetGrabber`). It is the handle itself, not a picture of one, so a sheet never shows two. `grabber`
off shows it; `grabberAccessibilityLabel` names it ("Sheet" by default).

```tsx
<SheetContent side="bottom" grabberAccessibilityLabel="Resize comments">
  …
</SheetContent>
```

The look alone is `sheetPanel(side)` and `sheetGrabber()`.

### Detents [#detents]

A bottom sheet can rest at heights instead of fitting its content: `detents` names them (`"medium"`
is half the screen, `"large"` its room), and a drag or a press on the grabber moves between them. Pass
`detent` and `onDetentChange` to own which one it rests at, and leave `closeOnSwipe` on to let a
downward swipe below the smallest close it.

```tsx
const detent = signal<"medium" | "large">("medium");

<SheetContent
  side="bottom"
  detents={["medium", "large"]}
  detent={detent()}
  onDetentChange={({ detent: next }) => detent.set(next === "large" ? "large" : "medium")}
  closeOnSwipe
  footer={
    <SheetFooter>
      <Input
        value={comment()}
        onChange={({ value }) => comment.set(value)}
        placeholder="Add a comment"
        returnKeyType="send"
        onSubmit={send}
        style={{ flex: 1 }}
      />
      <Button variant="default" onPress={send}>
        Send
      </Button>
    </SheetFooter>
  }
  footerStyle={{ borderTopWidth: 1, borderColor: colors.line, paddingTop: 10 }}
>
  {/* the thread: a Scroll that shrinks */}
</SheetContent>;
```

The `footer` stays at the bottom of the part of the panel that shows, at every detent; the smallest
one has to be tall enough to show it. A `Scroll` above it takes what room is left, so the thread
moves under a thumb while the field and its send button stay put.

### A draft the footer applies [#a-draft-the-footer-applies]

A sheet of filters edits a draft, and the footer decides whether the page sees it. Copy the applied
filters in when the sheet opens, keep the draft in the content, and write it back only in the
footer's button; closing any other way throws the draft away.

```tsx
const open = signal(false);
const applied = signal(NONE);
const draft = signal(NONE);

const openFilters = () => {
  draft.set(applied());
  open.set(true);
};

const apply = () => {
  applied.set(draft());
  open.set(false);
};

<Sheet open={open()} onOpenChange={({ open: next }) => open.set(next)}>
  <SheetContent
    side={wide() ? "right" : "bottom"}
    closeOnSwipe
    footer={
      <SheetFooter>
        <Button variant="ghost" disabled={isNone(draft())} onPress={() => draft.set(NONE)}>
          Reset
        </Button>
        <View style={{ flex: 1 }} />
        <Button variant="default" onPress={apply}>
          {`Show ${results(draft())} results`}
        </Button>
      </SheetFooter>
    }
  >
    {/* sort, price and the toggles, each writing the draft */}
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>;
```

The count in the apply button follows the draft while the page's own count still follows `applied`,
so the difference between "what I am choosing" and "what is on" is visible at every press. `Reset`
clears the draft only; the footer's other button is still what applies it.

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh/base` Sheet](https://nsh.dev/elements/sheet) passes through on `SheetContent`. `popupStyle` and `backdropStyle` go over the look's.

| Part               | Props                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SheetHeader`      | `style`                                                                                                                                                                                                                | The heading block: a title and its description, 2 points apart                                                                                                   |
| `SheetFooter`      | `style`                                                                                                                                                                                                                | The actions, in a row 8 points apart                                                                                                                             |
| `SheetTitle`       | `children`, `style`                                                                                                                                                                                                    | The title in `DialogTitle`'s type; a string also names the sheet's dialog for screen readers, unless `SheetContent`'s `accessibilityLabel` says otherwise        |
| `SheetDescription` | `children`, `style`                                                                                                                                                                                                    | The description in `DialogDescription`'s type. `nsh/base`'s sheet has no description prop, so it is read as content                                              |
| `SheetContent`     | `side` (`"bottom" \| "top" \| "left" \| "right"`, default `"bottom"`), `grabber` (on for `side="bottom"`), `grabberAccessibilityLabel`, `detents`, `detent`, `onDetentChange`, `closeOnSwipe`, `footer`, `footerStyle` | Every prop of `nsh/base` Sheet passes through; `popupStyle` and `backdropStyle` go over the look's. `footer` stays at the visible panel's bottom at every detent |

# Sidebar (/dev/docs/components/sidebar)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add sidebar
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Sidebar, SidebarInset, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger } from "@/components/ui/sidebar";
import { Icon } from "@/lib/ui/icons";
```

The examples draw icons with `Icon` from `lib/ui/icons`; see [Icons](../icons) for adding it and picking a size and color.

```tsx
<SidebarProvider>
  <Sidebar>{/* a header, its groups, a footer */}</Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>
    <SidebarTrigger />
    {/* the page */}
  </SidebarInset>
</SidebarProvider>
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `Sidebar`:

```text
SidebarProvider
├── Sidebar
│   ├── SidebarHeader
│   │   ├── SidebarMenu
│   │   │   └── SidebarMenuItem
│   │   │       └── SidebarMenuButton
│   │   └── SidebarInput
│   ├── SidebarSeparator
│   ├── SidebarContent
│   │   └── SidebarGroup
│   │       ├── SidebarGroupLabel
│   │       ├── SidebarGroupAction
│   │       └── SidebarGroupContent
│   │           └── SidebarMenu
│   │               └── SidebarMenuItem
│   │                   ├── SidebarMenuButton
│   │                   ├── SidebarMenuAction
│   │                   ├── SidebarMenuBadge
│   │                   ├── SidebarMenuSkeleton
│   │                   └── SidebarMenuSub
│   │                       └── SidebarMenuSubItem
│   │                           └── SidebarMenuSubButton
│   ├── SidebarFooter
│   └── SidebarRail
└── SidebarInset
    └── SidebarTrigger
```

## Examples [#examples]

### The column [#the-column]

`Sidebar` is a column as wide as the sidebar (`sidebarSize.width`, 256 points) on the sidebar's fill,
its edge against the page, holding a `SidebarHeader`, the groups in a `SidebarContent` that scrolls
when they do not fit, and a `SidebarFooter`.

Three axes say how it meets the window:

- `side` — `left` (default) or `right`: which edge it stands on.
- `variant` — `sidebar` (default) its own edge against the page; `floating` a card standing in the
  window's air, 8 points of room around it; `inset` a card on the sidebar's ground, with the page's
  own card beside it on that same ground, 8 points from it and from the window's edges.
- `collapsible` — `offcanvas` (default) leaves the window when it closes; `icon` folds to a strip of
  icons (`sidebarSize.icon`, 48 points); `none` never closes.

```tsx
<Sidebar side="right" variant="inset" collapsible="icon">
  …
</Sidebar>
```

Closing takes the room away at once: the platform transitions colors, opacity and transforms, not
layout, so there is no 200 ms width animation to land (and no `motion-reduce` to switch off) — the
column is either as wide as its state says, or gone.

### The page beside it [#the-page-beside-it]

`SidebarInset` is the page, filling what is left of the window: the page's own fill, or in the `inset`
variant a card with its corners 8 points from the column's card and from the window's edges. Room for
the header of the page is the app's: a row with the trigger, a `Separator` (`orientation="vertical"`,
16 high), where you are, and what it holds.

```tsx
<SidebarInset>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8, padding: 8 }}>
    <SidebarTrigger />
    <Separator orientation="vertical" style={{ height: 16 }} />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 13 }}>Documents</Text>
  </View>
  {/* the page */}
</SidebarInset>
```

### The open state [#the-open-state]

`SidebarProvider` owns it: `open` (controlled) or `defaultOpen` (default `true`), reported by
`onOpenChange({ open, reason })` — `triggerPress`, `railPress` or `shortcut`. Nothing is written
down: storage is the app's, which usually keeps the state where it keeps the rest of its settings
and passes it back as `open`.

```tsx
const open = signal(stored("sidebar") ?? true);

<SidebarProvider
  open={open()}
  onOpenChange={({ open: next }) => {
    open.set(next);
    store("sidebar", next);
  }}
>
  …
</SidebarProvider>;
```

`useSidebar()` is what the parts read, and what an app reads inside the provider: `state`
(`"expanded"` or `"collapsed"`), `open`, `openMobile`, `isMobile`, `setOpen`, `setOpenMobile` and
`toggleSidebar`. Every value is live: read it in a JSX binding and it follows the provider.

⌘B on Apple platforms, Ctrl+B elsewhere, folds the column and opens it — `keymap.bind("mod+b")`,
made where the provider draws and gone with it. The rail at the column's inner edge takes a press
too: it is 8 points wide (16 wide to a press, past its bounds with `hitSlop`) and shows a hairline in
the sidebar's edge color while the pointer is over it. That hairline follows the pointer through the
class language (`group-hover:`), not a signal, so passing the cursor over the rail commits no frame;
the pointer has to be on the 8-point strip itself, not only in its `hitSlop` margin. `SidebarTrigger` is the button that usually
sits in the page's header.

### On a phone [#on-a-phone]

A touch screen, or a window narrower than 600 points, shows the column as a sheet instead — this
library's `Sheet`, 288 points wide from the side the column stands on, with the same trigger opening
it. The column's own state is left alone, so a window that widens again finds it as it was.

```tsx
const sidebar = useSidebar(); // in a view inside the provider

<Text>{() => `open ${sidebar.openMobile}, sheet ${sidebar.isMobile}`}</Text>;
```

### A row [#a-row]

`SidebarMenuButton` is a row of `SidebarMenu`, inside a `SidebarGroupContent` of a `SidebarGroup`
that a `SidebarGroupLabel` names: the theme's row high (`controlSize.row`), its label the `body`
type role, the pointer's fill under it, the `sidebarAccent` fill when `isActive` (the page the app
is on), the keyboard's ring, and 50% while `disabled`. It takes a press (`onPress`), or it is a
row of its own; no `href`, as a navigation menu's link has none.

`size` is the row's step — `default` the theme's row, `sm` the height step under it, `lg` a team's
switcher or a user's row, 48 points where the row is a pointer's (a touch screen's row is already a
finger's height) — and `variant` is its look: `default`, bare until the pointer is over it, or
`outline`, a card of its own on the column.

A string child is the row's name. Anything else is drawn as given, which is how an icon leads a name:
the look has the words for it.

```tsx
const row = sidebarMenuButtonLook({ size: () => "sm" });

<SidebarMenuButton size="sm" tooltip={project.name} isActive={project.isActive}>
  <Icon icon={project.icon} size={row.glyph.size} tint={row.glyph.tint} />
  <Text style={row.label}>{project.name}</Text>
</SidebarMenuButton>;
```

Folded to icons, the row is a square the height of a row (`sidebarSize.folded`) with its icon, and
`tooltip` names it on a desktop: a
string is the name, or the tooltip's own props (`placement`, `delay`, …). It also names the row for
screen readers when nothing else does — and it replaces `nsh/base`'s element `tooltip`, which is what
this prop is.

A row keeps its name only while the column is open: nothing else moves, so a look is written once
where the row draws. A row the app draws hands its look the column's fold — `open` and `collapsible`,
the app's own signals — and its name goes; a look given no fold options draws the open row, and an
action or a badge inside a folded item leaves the tree.

### An action, a badge [#an-action-a-badge]

`SidebarMenuAction` is a 20-point square at the row's trailing edge, in `SidebarMenuItem`, and
`SidebarMenuBadge` a pill there — a count, a short word, its numbers tabular. The item keeps the room
they need, so the row's name stops short of them; both on one row, the action steps in by the
badge's width rather than drawing over it.

```tsx
const action = sidebarMenuActionLook();

<SidebarMenuItem>
  <SidebarMenuButton size="sm" tooltip={project.name}>
    {project.name}
  </SidebarMenuButton>
  <SidebarMenuBadge>{project.unread}</SidebarMenuBadge>
  <SidebarMenuAction accessibilityLabel={`More about ${project.name}`} onPress={more}>
    <Icon icon={Ellipsis} size={action.glyph.size} tint={action.glyph.tint} />
  </SidebarMenuAction>
</SidebarMenuItem>;
```

An action is always there: hover alone is something a touch screen has no way to do.

### A sub menu [#a-sub-menu]

`SidebarMenuSub` holds the rows under a row that opens them — `SidebarMenuSubItem` and its
`SidebarMenuSubButton`, the height step under the row (`controlHeight.md`). It is 14 points in from
the row above it, with a hairline down its start in the sidebar's edge color, and it hides while the
column is folded.

The row above it opens it. `nsh/base`'s `Collapsible` does the reveal — not this library's
`Collapsible`, which draws a disclosure row of its own (a settings list wants that; a sidebar row
wants the row it already has):

```tsx
const open = signal(false);

<SidebarMenuItem>
  <Collapsible
    open={open()}
    reveal
    content={
      <SidebarMenuSub>
        <SidebarMenuSubItem>
          <SidebarMenuSubButton onPress={() => go("history")}>History</SidebarMenuSubButton>
        </SidebarMenuSubItem>
      </SidebarMenuSub>
    }
  >
    <SidebarMenuButton onPress={() => open.set(!open())}>
      <Text style={row.label}>Playground</Text>
    </SidebarMenuButton>
  </Collapsible>
</SidebarMenuItem>;
```

### A group [#a-group]

`SidebarGroupLabel` names a group in 32 points of quiet type; folded to icons it takes no room and
draws nothing, and stays in the tree for a screen reader. `SidebarGroupAction` stands at its trailing
edge — a search, a settings — 20 points square. `SidebarGroupContent` takes the rows, as wide as the
group.

### A row that is still coming [#a-row-that-is-still-coming]

`SidebarMenuSkeleton` is the skeleton's blocks where an icon and a name will be: an icon's box when
`showIcon`, then a line of text as long as `width` says (70% when it says nothing). A length made up
per mount is a picture that changes between runs, so this one is told.

## API [#api]

The provider owns the state and lays the column and the page out; a column and its parts draw on
`nsh`'s `View` (`SidebarSeparator` wraps this library's `Separator`, and the phone's sheet is this
library's `Sheet`). Every `nsh` view prop passes through; a row is an `nsh/base` button's props too.

| Part                   | Props                                                                                                                           | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SidebarProvider`      | `open` / `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange({ open, reason })`, `style`                                                               | Owns the state and the ⌘B / Ctrl+B binding, and lays the column and the page out                                                |
| `Sidebar`              | `side`, `variant`, `collapsible`                                                                                                | The column; on a phone it is this library's `Sheet`                                                                             |
| `SidebarTrigger`       | `children` (its icon), `accessibilityLabel` (default `"Toggle Sidebar"`), and an icon button's props                            | The button that opens and closes the column                                                                                     |
| `SidebarRail`          | `accessibilityLabel`                                                                                                            | A press at the column's inner edge                                                                                              |
| `SidebarInset`         | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | The page beside the column                                                                                                      |
| `SidebarHeader`        | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | The top: a stack of rows, 8 points apart, 8 of room                                                                             |
| `SidebarFooter`        | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | The bottom, as the header                                                                                                       |
| `SidebarContent`       | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | The scrolling middle                                                                                                            |
| `SidebarSeparator`     | `Separator`'s props                                                                                                             | A separator in the sidebar's edge color, 8 points inset from either side                                                        |
| `SidebarInput`         | `Input`'s props                                                                                                                 | An input as tall as a row, on the page's fill                                                                                   |
| `SidebarGroup`         | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | A titled group, 8 points of room                                                                                                |
| `SidebarGroupLabel`    | `children`                                                                                                                      | A string is the name; folds away to nothing                                                                                     |
| `SidebarGroupAction`   | `accessibilityLabel`, `onPress`, and an `nsh/base` button's props                                                               | A 20-point square at the group's trailing edge                                                                                  |
| `SidebarGroupContent`  | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | What the group holds                                                                                                            |
| `SidebarMenu`          | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | The rows: a column of them 4 points apart                                                                                       |
| `SidebarMenuItem`      | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | One row's box: its button, an action, a badge, a sub menu                                                                       |
| `SidebarMenuButton`    | `isActive`, `size`, `variant`, `tooltip`, `children`, `accessibilityLabel`, and an `nsh/base` button's `onPress`, `disabled`, … | A row of the menu                                                                                                               |
| `SidebarMenuAction`    | `accessibilityLabel`, `onPress`, and an `nsh/base` button's props                                                               | A 20-point square at the row's trailing edge                                                                                    |
| `SidebarMenuBadge`     | `children`                                                                                                                      | A count or a short word at the row's trailing edge                                                                              |
| `SidebarMenuSub`       | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | The rows under a row that opens them                                                                                            |
| `SidebarMenuSubItem`   | every `nsh` view prop                                                                                                           | One of them                                                                                                                     |
| `SidebarMenuSubButton` | `isActive`, `size`, `children`, `accessibilityLabel`, and an `nsh/base` button's props                                          | A sub row; it takes a press                                                                                                     |
| `SidebarMenuSkeleton`  | `showIcon`, `width`                                                                                                             | The skeleton's blocks where an icon and a name will be                                                                          |
| `useSidebar()`         | —                                                                                                                               | What the parts read inside the provider: `state`, `open`, `openMobile`, `isMobile`, `setOpen`, `setOpenMobile`, `toggleSidebar` |

The looks — spread them on the view they name, or read their words for content of your own:
`sidebarLook({ side, variant, collapsible, open, isMobile })` (`root`, `frame`, `column`, `inset`,
`rail`, `railLine`, `header`, `footer`, `content`, `contentRows`, `separator`),
`sidebarGroupLook()`, `sidebarMenuButtonLook({ size, variant, isActive, trailing })`,
`sidebarMenuActionLook({ trailing })`, `sidebarMenuBadgeLook()`, `sidebarMenuSubLook()`,
`sidebarMenuSubButtonLook({ size, isActive })`, `sidebarMenuSkeletonLook()` and
`sidebarInputLook()`. `sidebarSize` has the numbers.

# Skeleton (/dev/docs/components/skeleton)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add skeleton
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";
```

```tsx
<Skeleton style={{ width: 250, height: 14 }} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### A line, an avatar, a button [#a-line-an-avatar-a-button]

A skeleton has no size of its own: the box is the caller's `style`. A line is as tall as the type
it will hold and as wide as that text runs; an avatar or an icon is a square, round with
`borderRadius` half its side.

```tsx
<Skeleton style={{ width: 250, height: 14 }} />
<Skeleton style={{ width: 48, height: 48, borderRadius: 24 }} />
```

### A block of content [#a-block-of-content]

Placeholders keep the layout of what is coming: a column with a `gap` where the rows will be, and
a row for the parts that sit side by side.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 16 }}>
  <Skeleton style={{ width: 48, height: 48, borderRadius: 24 }} />
  <View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
    <Skeleton style={{ width: 250, height: 14 }} />
    <Skeleton style={{ width: 200, height: 14 }} />
  </View>
</View>
```

### Motion [#motion]

The block breathes (an endless motion). When the user asks for less motion it stays still, and a
terminal shows it still: nothing to play there.

```tsx
{
  /* Nothing to turn off: the skeleton follows the system's reduce-motion setting. */
}
<Skeleton style={{ width: 200, height: 14 }} />;
```

## API [#api]

Every prop of [`nsh` View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view) passes through (`style`, `accessibilityLabel`, …); `style` goes over the look's.

| Part       | Props       | Description                                                           |
| ---------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Skeleton` | `ViewProps` | The block; its box, corners and breathing are the look's and `style`. |

There is no axis: a skeleton is one look — the theme's `accent` fill, the theme's control corners,
the breathing. `skeletonLook()` is exported for a block the app draws (or animates) itself.

# Slider (/dev/docs/components/slider)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add slider
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Slider } from "nsh/base";

import { sliderFill, sliderLook } from "@/components/ui/slider";
```

```tsx
const look = sliderLook();

<Slider
  value={volume()}
  onChange={({ value }) => volume.set(value as number)}
  rangeStyle={sliderFill(0, volume() / 100)}
  {...look}
/>;
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Disabled [#disabled]

Opacity on the track comes from the look's `disabled:opacity-50` class on `trackClass`.

### The rail and the knob [#the-rail-and-the-knob]

Both come from the theme, read where the slider draws: the `track` value of `control()` gives the
groove — its face colour, and, on a graved groove (`sunk`), the inset shade that is also the edge of
the accent's run — and the `handle` value gives the knob: a disc, or WinUI's ring, with the rail's
thickness, the band around it, the pressed size, and a vertical rail 128 points long (144 on a
touch screen) on every form.

### Value column [#value-column]

`showValue` lays the value beside a horizontal rail (a 42-point column) or above a vertical one.
A string of your own replaces the formatted number and keeps that place.

```tsx
import { sliderValueClass, sliderValueStyle } from "@/components/ui/slider";

<Slider showValue value={volume()} onChange={({ value }) => volume.set(value as number)}>
  <Text class={sliderValueClass} style={sliderValueStyle()}>
    64%
  </Text>
</Slider>;
```

### Vertical [#vertical]

A fill that starts at the rail's start (`from` at or below 0) stays nsh's own run, from the
minimum to the thumb. A fill that starts later sets its own edges. Name the farther end first
when the span reaches back to the start, so a band lit from the middle still places itself at
the minimum:

```tsx
const at = (db + 12) / 24;

<Slider
  axis="vertical"
  showValue
  min={-12}
  max={12}
  value={db}
  rangeStyle={sliderFill(Math.max(0.5, at), Math.min(0.5, at), true)}
>
  <Text class="text-center font-mono text-[11px] leading-none" style={sliderValueStyle()}>
    {db}
  </Text>
</Slider>;
```

## API [#api]

`Slider` is [`nsh/base` Slider](https://nsh.dev/elements/slider) wearing `sliderLook` and `sliderFill`: every base prop passes through, and the look's classes and styles are defaults the caller can override.

| Part                                     | Props                                                                                                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Slider`                                 | `axis`, `showValue`, and every `nsh/base` Slider prop (`value`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `onChange`, `onChangeEnd`, `disabled`, `rangeStyle`, …) | The rail, the thumb and the fill. `showValue` lays the value beside a horizontal rail, or above a vertical one                                      |
| `sliderLook()`                           | `vertical`, `value`                                                                                                                           | The parts to spread on a slider of your own: `class`, `trackClass`, `indicatorClass` / `indicatorStyle`, `rangeClass`, `thumbClass` / `thumbStyle`  |
| `sliderFill()`                           | `from`, `to`, `vertical`                                                                                                                      | The accent between `from` and `to` when `from` is past the rail's start. A `from` of 0 or less leaves placement to nsh, so a thumb can drag the run |
| `sliderValueClass`, `sliderValueStyle()` | —                                                                                                                                             | The horizontal value column's label: 42 points, right aligned, monospaced. A vertical readout uses a centered line instead                          |

# Spinner (/dev/docs/components/spinner)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add spinner
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/ui/spinner";
```

```tsx
<Spinner size="default" tint={colors.brand} />
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Size [#size]

`size` is the theme's icon tier, so the ring follows the pointer: 12, 16 and 20 points with a
pointer, 16, 20 and 24 on a touch screen. `side` takes an exact size in points where the scale's
does not fit.

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
<Spinner size="default" tint={colors.brand} />
<Spinner size="lg" tint={colors.brand} />
<Spinner side={14} tint={colors.mutedForeground} />
```

### In a button [#in-a-button]

`Button`'s `busy` state draws the ring before the label and blocks a second press.

```tsx
<Button busy={saving()} onPress={save}>
  Save
</Button>
```

## API [#api]

A ring with its top arc in `tint`, turning once every 800 ms; its stroke is an eighth of its side, at least 1.5 points.
A groove behind the arc is the theme's track form to say: under the sunk form the rest of the ring follows
`tint` at a quarter, under the tint and hairline forms there is none.

| Part      | Props                  | Description                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Spinner` | `size`, `side`, `tint` | The ring: `size` the icon tier (`sm`, `default`, `lg`) or `side` its side in points; `tint` its arc (under a sunk track form, the rest of it that color at a quarter). |

# SplitView (/dev/docs/components/split-view)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add split-view
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { createNavStack, NavPage, NavStack } from "@/components/ui/nav-stack";
import {
  SplitView,
  SplitViewContent,
  SplitViewDetail,
  SplitViewSidebar,
  SplitViewTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/split-view";
```

```tsx
const folders = createNavStack(["folders"]);
const notes = createNavStack(["notes"]);
const note = createNavStack(["note"]);

<SplitView
  style={{ flex: 1 }}
  columnVisibility={visibility()}
  onColumnVisibilityChange={({ columnVisibility }) => visibility.set(columnVisibility)}
  sidebar={
    <NavStack state={folders}>
      {() => <SplitViewSidebar title="Folders">{/* the folders */}</SplitViewSidebar>}
    </NavStack>
  }
  content={
    <NavStack state={notes}>
      {() => (
        <SplitViewContent
          title="Inbox"
          leading={
            <SplitViewTrigger
              columnVisibility={visibility()}
              onColumnVisibilityChange={({ columnVisibility }) => visibility.set(columnVisibility)}
            />
          }
        >
          {/* the notes */}
        </SplitViewContent>
      )}
    </NavStack>
  }
  detail={
    <NavStack state={note}>
      {() => <SplitViewDetail title="Design review">{/* the note */}</SplitViewDetail>}
    </NavStack>
  }
/>;
```

`sidebar`, `content` and `detail` stay props, and each one is a `NavStack`. The platform finds that stack in the slot, so these parts are the pages inside it, not wrappers around it. Leave `content` out for two columns.

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `SplitView`:

```text
SplitView
├── SplitViewSidebar
├── SplitViewContent
│   └── SplitViewTrigger
└── SplitViewDetail
```

## Examples [#examples]

The behavior — which columns show, the phone collapsing to one, the system's sidebar button on iOS — is NSH's [`SplitView`](https://nsh.dev/elements/split-view). This component is that view, plus the column's surface, the header a desktop draws, and the button that hides the sidebar.

The columns' widths are the platform's. Panes the user resizes are [`Resizable`](./resizable).

### Three columns [#three-columns]

Each column is a stack of its own, so pushing a page in the detail leaves the sidebar and the list where they are. `SplitViewSidebar` is the sidebar's fill (`colors.sidebar`) with a hairline of `colors.sidebarBorder` after it. `SplitViewContent` is the page's fill with `colors.line` after it. `SplitViewDetail` has no hairline. iOS draws the columns' own edges, so the hairlines are left out there.

```tsx
<SplitViewSidebar title="Folders">{/* rows */}</SplitViewSidebar>
```

### The sidebar button [#the-sidebar-button]

`SplitViewTrigger` hides the sidebar (`"doubleColumn"`) or shows every column (`"all"`). It does not show or hide anything itself: the app sets `columnVisibility`, the same value the split takes. The glyph stays `colors.mutedForeground`; the button is selected while the sidebar is showing. iOS draws the system's sidebar button, so leave this one out there.

```tsx
<SplitViewContent
  title="Inbox"
  leading={
    <SplitViewTrigger
      columnVisibility={visibility()}
      onColumnVisibilityChange={({ columnVisibility }) => visibility.set(columnVisibility)}
    />
  }
>
  {/* the notes */}
</SplitViewContent>
```

`leading` and `trailing` are the header's items. On a desktop they sit in the bar; on iOS and Android they are the system header's leading and trailing buttons.

### On a phone [#on-a-phone]

Where the window is horizontally compact, one column shows: the first that `columnVisibility` includes. A choice that should bring the next column in front sets `"doubleColumn"`, then `"detailOnly"`. The way back is the page's — a button in `leading`, since a desktop has no system back between columns.

```tsx
const compact = () => horizontalSizeClass() === "compact";

<SplitViewDetail
  title={note()}
  leading={
    compact() ? (
      <BackButton title={folder()} onPress={() => visibility.set("doubleColumn")} />
    ) : undefined
  }
>
  {/* the note */}
</SplitViewDetail>;
```

### Controlled [#controlled]

`columnVisibility` is the app's. `"automatic"` (the view's own starting value, when the prop is left out) shows every column except where iPadOS decides, and the sidebar where the room is compact. `"all"`, `"doubleColumn"` and `"detailOnly"` are the other values. `onColumnVisibilityChange` reports what the user or the system shows instead — the sidebar button, a swipe from the edge, going back from a column's first page on a phone.

```tsx
const visibility = signal<ColumnVisibility>("all");

<SplitView
  columnVisibility={visibility()}
  onColumnVisibilityChange={({ columnVisibility }) => visibility.set(columnVisibility)}
  sidebar={sidebar}
  detail={detail}
/>;
```

## API [#api]

`SplitView` takes every prop of [`nsh/base`'s SplitView](https://nsh.dev/elements/split-view); `style` goes over the look's. A column page takes every prop of [`nsh/base`'s NavPage](https://nsh.dev/elements/nav-stack); `style` goes over the column's. `ColumnVisibility` is `nsh/base`'s, re-exported.

| Part               | Props                                                                | Description                                                     |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SplitView`        | `sidebar`, `content`, `detail`, `columnVisibility`                   | The columns. `content` is optional: without it the view has two |
| `SplitViewSidebar` | `title`, `leading`, `trailing`, `header`                             | The sidebar's page: its fill, a hairline after it               |
| `SplitViewContent` | `title`, `leading`, `trailing`, `header`                             | The middle page: the page's fill, a hairline after it           |
| `SplitViewDetail`  | `title`, `leading`, `trailing`, `header`                             | The detail's page: the page's fill                              |
| `SplitViewHeader`  | `column`, `title`, `leading`, `trailing`                             | The bar a desktop draws. `header` on a column page replaces it  |
| `SplitViewTrigger` | `columnVisibility`, `onColumnVisibilityChange`, `accessibilityLabel` | The sidebar button. A press reports `"doubleColumn"` or `"all"` |

The looks — spread them on the views they name: `splitViewLook()` (`root`), `splitViewColumnLook(column)` (`page`), `splitViewHeaderLook(column)` (`bar`, `title`) and `splitViewTriggerLook()` (`style`, `hoverStyle`, `activeStyle`, `focusVisibleStyle`, `glyph`).

# Stat (/dev/docs/components/stat)

## Installation [#installation]

```npm
npx shadcn-nsh@latest add stat
```

## Usage [#usage]

```tsx
import { Stat, StatGroup } from "@/components/ui/stat";
```

```tsx
<Stat label="Users" value="12.4k" />
```

## Composition [#composition]

Use the following composition to build a `StatGroup`:

```text
StatGroup
└── Stat
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Tone [#tone]

```tsx
<Stat label="Users" value="12.4k" tone="neutral" />
<Stat label="Latency" value="42 ms" tone="accent" />
<Stat label="Queue" value="3" tone="info" />
<Stat label="Errors" value="0.2%" tone="warn" />
<Stat label="Failures" value="2" tone="destructive" />
<Stat label="Growth" value="+8.1%" tone="up" />
<Stat label="Churn" value="−1.2%" tone="down" />
```

### Truncate [#truncate]

```tsx
<Stat label="Display" value="MacBook Pro 16-inch, 2024" truncate />
```

### Unit and note [#unit-and-note]

`unit` sits beside the value, smaller and muted. `note` is a line under it. shadcn/ui has no stat, so the names follow the figure a chart shows: a value, its unit, and a note.

```tsx
<Stat label="Latency" value="42" unit="ms" note="p95" tone="accent" />
```

### A row [#a-row]

`StatGroup` wraps several stats onto one row. A stat with no `width` shares that row. A hairline above a chart's figures is the group's class, not the default.

```tsx
<StatGroup class="border-line border-t pt-3">
  <Stat label="Open" value="182.40" />
  <Stat label="High" value="184.10" />
</StatGroup>
```

### A trend beside a figure [#a-trend-beside-a-figure]

A figure whose value moves with a series reads better with the series beside it: the `Stat` gives
the name, the value and the change in the same tone as the line, and a `Plot` at 104 × 38 draws the
trend without axes or a pointer — `interactive={false}`.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 16 }}>
  <Stat label="Composite" value="4,182.60" note="+11.80 today" tone="up" />
  <View style={{ width: 104, height: 38 }}>
    <Plot
      data={minutes}
      y="price"
      yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [lo, hi] }}
      interactive={false}
      style={{ width: 104, height: 38 }}
    >
      <Area curve="natural" backgroundStyle={plotWash(colors.up, 0.2)} />
      <Grid y={[previousClose]} style={plotReference(colors.mutedForeground)} />
      <Line curve="natural" style={{ stroke: colors.up, strokeWidth: 1.75 }} />
    </Plot>
    <View
      style={{ position: "absolute", top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0, pointerEvents: "none" }}
    >
      <Plot
        data={[minutes[minutes.length - 1]]}
        y="price"
        yScale={{ type: "linear", domain: [lo, hi] }}
        interactive={false}
        style={{ width: 104, height: 38 }}
      >
        <Dot
          value="price"
          r={5.5}
          style={{ fill: "transparent", stroke: alpha(colors.up, 0.4), strokeWidth: 1.5 }}
        />
        <Dot value="price" r={2.5} style={{ fill: colors.up }} />
      </Plot>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

`note` carries the signed move and `tone` the role it and the line share; the previous close is a
dashed `Grid` behind the wash, so the day's direction is read at a glance.

## API [#api]

Gallery atom: no `nsh/base` counterpart. shadcn/ui has no stat either.

| Part        | Props                                                         | Description                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Stat`      | `label`, `value`, `unit`, `note`, `tone`, `width`, `truncate` | A muted label over a larger value; `tone` colors the value, `truncate` keeps it to one line. |
| `StatGroup` | —                                                             | A wrapping row of stats, 12 points apart.                                                    |


```tsx
<Status label="Idle" tone="neutral" />
```
